## 2026-08-06 - Revised-data diagnostic literature survey and frozen boundaries

### Why this branch exists

The first executable benchmark pass uses a current, revised snapshot only to
exercise transformations, expanding-window model estimation, matched-sample
scoring, and deterministic output. It is deliberately quarantined from the
prospective-origin registry. The Philadelphia Fed's
[Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/real-time-data-set-for-macroeconomists)
defines vintages as snapshots of the information available at different
dates, and Croushore and Stark explain why those vintages are necessary for
realistic forecast evaluation
([article](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0164-0704(02)00062-9)). A single revised
history therefore cannot establish real-time forecast accuracy, even when its
recursive calculations are otherwise out of sample.

This section records the literature survey required by the standing
unknown-or-dubious-field protocol. It freezes the following diagnostic
operators without promoting them to prospective truth operators.

### Frequency conversion and transformations

1. BEA real GDP, PCE price, core PCE price, GDP deflator, and nominal GDP use
   the protocol's already frozen annualized quarter-on-quarter log operator,
   `400 * (log(x_q) - log(x_{q-1}))`. This is consistent with the
   Philadelphia Fed's convention for continuously compounded annualized
   quarterly growth
   ([SPF documentation](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/-/media/FRBP/Assets/Surveys-And-Data/survey-of-professional-forecasters/spf-documentation.pdf))
   and the transformation discipline in McCracken and Ng's
   [FRED-QD](https://doi.org/10.20955/r.103.1-44).
2. CES total nonfarm payroll employment (`CES0000000001`) is first the
   arithmetic mean of the three published seasonally adjusted monthly levels,
   then `100 * (log(E_q) - log(E_{q-1}))`. The Philadelphia Fed describes the
   SPF payroll level as a seasonally adjusted quarterly average
   ([EMP data documentation](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/emp)).
   The unannualized log-point output follows this project's frozen target
   contract. An annualized `400 * delta log` representation may be reported
   only as a separately labelled sensitivity.
3. CPS unemployment (`LNS14000000`) is normally the arithmetic mean of the
   three published seasonally adjusted monthly percentage levels. BLS warns
   that recent seasonally adjusted CPS estimates are revised as asymmetric
   filters become symmetric
   ([seasonal-adjustment methodology](https://www.bls.gov/cps/seasonal-adjustment-methodology.htm));
   that is another reason the current snapshot remains revised-data
   diagnostic evidence rather than origin evidence.
4. The quarterly EFFR is the equal-weight arithmetic mean of published daily
   rates by **effective date**. No weekend or holiday observations are
   invented, and publication timestamps control vintage availability rather
   than receive observation weight. The New York Fed already constructs each
   daily EFFR as a volume-weighted median, so this project does not apply a
   second volume weighting
   ([EFFR definition](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/effr);
   [methodology and revision policy](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates)).
   This quarterly mean is a project operator, not an official quarterly New
   York Fed series.

The raw New York Fed response contains one anomalous Sunday-labelled row,
`2003-07-20`, whose published fields other than date exactly duplicate the
adjacent Monday row, `2003-07-21`. The source bytes and SHA-256 remain
unchanged. Independent review of the New York Fed's
[EFFR definition](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/effr)
and
[business-day publication policy](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates)
supports excluding the Sunday row from the canonical quarterly
business-effective-date mean. Because the anomaly predates the 2016 FR 2420
method change, the review also checked the New York Fed's contemporary
broker-market description; it says the published effective rate represented
brokered trades for the previous business day
([Staff Report 416, p. 7](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr416.pdf)).
The generator must verify the exact known date, rate, complete non-date-field
equality, and matching Monday before exclusion; any other nonbusiness-date
observation fails closed. The row is not reassigned because Monday is already
present, and the SOFR weekend carry convention is not imported into EFFR.
This is a transparent analyst-side validation rule, not a claim that the New
York Fed corrected its source.

### The missing October 2025 CPS observation

The source extract exposed a genuinely unknown field rather than a numeric
value: BLS did not collect October 2025 CPS data during the lapse in
appropriations and did not reconstruct the month later. Independent review
found decisive official guidance. BLS states that, with one of three months
missing, it could not produce a reliable 2025Q4 quarterly CPS estimate
([shutdown-impact questions 2, 13, and 14](https://www.bls.gov/cps/methods/2025-federal-government-shutdown-impact-cps.htm)).
Its 2025 annual estimate instead uses eleven months and is explicitly not
strictly comparable. The November release also compares September directly
with November rather than fabricating an October observation
([archived release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_12162025.htm)).

The frozen decision is therefore:

- preserve the native `-` and BLS footnote in the source extract;
- do not impute October, convert it to zero, or call the November-December
  mean an official quarterly observation;
- define canonical `2025Q4` unemployment truth as unavailable;
- end the first complete-case eight-variable diagnostic panel at `2025Q3`,
  while retaining later raw observations and their provenance; and
- if a future sensitivity uses `(November + December) / 2`, label it
  `partial_quarter_two_month_mean`, record `coverage = 2/3`, and keep
  `official_quarterly_estimate`, `protocol_eligible`, origin admission, and
  promotion false.

The complete-case truncation is stricter than merely dropping one
target-quarter, but it avoids feeding an invented value through every
multivariate VAR and BVAR equation. A future missing-data model may retain the
other post-gap targets only as a separately specified sensitivity with its
uncertainty propagated. Rubin's
[missing-data framework](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/63.3.581) supports
making the missingness mechanism explicit instead of silently treating an
unobserved value as observed.

### Model and sample policies

Two benchmark branches must remain visibly distinct:

- The **production-oriented branch** uses frozen stationary target
  transformations, an expanding estimation window, univariate AR candidates,
  VARs, and a shrinkage BVAR. Iterated multi-step forecasts are primary;
  direct forecasts remain a prespecified robustness check. This choice is
  informed by Marcellino, Stock, and Watson's
  [direct-versus-iterated comparison](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2005.07.020)
  and the shrinkage evidence in Bańbura, Giannone, and Reichlin
  ([large BVARs](https://doi.org/10.1002/jae.1137)) and Giannone, Lenza, and
  Primiceri
  ([prior selection](https://doi.org/10.1162/REST_a_00483)).
- The **paper-parity branch** will reproduce Poledna et al.'s VAR(1),
  VAR(2), and VAR(3) comparisons in log levels and report the paper's relative
  RMSE gain convention,
  `100 * (1 - RMSE_model / RMSE_VAR1)`. It must not be relabelled as the
  stationary production branch
  ([Poledna et al.](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.euroecorev.2022.104306)).

The first diagnostic reports horizons 1, 2, 4, 8, and 12 on two explicit
matched samples: all cells available to every requested model, and a balanced
horizon-12 sample. It records the exact observation count for every
target/horizon/model cell. RMSE and MAE are primary; MASE uses a
training-only scale, following Hyndman and Koehler
([MASE](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2006.03.001)). Once genuine
common-information forecast origins exist in adequate numbers, inference will
add Diebold-Mariano loss-differential tests
([DM](https://doi.org/10.1080/07350015.1995.10524599)), the
Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold small-sample correction
([HLN](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0169-2070(96)00719-4)), Clark-West tests for
nested comparisons
([CW](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2006.05.023)), and a model confidence
set to control multiple comparisons
([MCS](https://doi.org/10.3982/ECTA5771)). These tests are not meaningful
substitutes for the missing prospective-origin evidence.

Pandemic observations remain in the headline sample. Pre-pandemic, acute
pandemic, and post-pandemic slices and robust/down-weighted variants will be
reported as prespecified sensitivities, not selected after seeing rankings.
The need for this separation is documented by Lenza and Primiceri
([macroeconomic variables during COVID-19](https://doi.org/10.1002/jae.2895))
and Schorfheide and Song
([real-time mixed-frequency VAR forecasting during the pandemic](https://doi.org/10.21799/frbp.wp.2020.26)).

### Current status

The synthetic diagnostic contract passes 48 focused assertions after Runic
1.7.0 formatting. It requires ten models (three naïve, three univariate AR,
VAR(1)-VAR(3), and BVAR(1)), retains structured model failures, and refuses
origin admission, promotion, ABM accuracy, equilibrium-benchmark, or
paper-parity claims. The real revised fixture and score tables are still being
constructed at this checkpoint.

These decisions refine data engineering and evaluation design only. There
remain **zero admitted forecast origins and zero production forecast scores**.
No ABM-versus-equilibrium or ABM-versus-autoregressive accuracy result exists,
so forecasting suitability remains **not evaluated**.

### Capture and failure semantics

The API request uses the unregistered, v1-compatible two-series signature at
the v2 endpoint and never exceeds 25 attempts in one invocation. Transport is
direct and bounded: no redirects, netrc, cookies, or ambient proxies; a
12-second request timeout; and object-specific response-size caps. Each API
response body is retained under a content-addressed attempt object before the
next poll. An accepted `M07` response is installed immediately as an API-only
checkpoint before slower HTML/PDF news routes are attempted.

News-route evidence is deliberately weaker. Sanitized content-addressed news
diagnostics preserve route, timing, headers, and failure outcomes, but remain
unbound caller-correlated host diagnostics; they are not proof that an
API-plus-news receipt was installed. Invalid or unavailable news may
legitimately leave the verified API-only checkpoint. In contrast, a complete,
validated API+HTML+PDF set that fails installation is now fatal: independent
review reproduced an earlier fail-open using a corrupt pre-existing full
bundle, after which the collector returned API-only success while both news
objects were marked complete. The fix preserves the API checkpoint and
unbound diagnostic, then rethrows the installation error. A five-assertion
regression seals that behavior.

Transaction identifiers are collision-resistant and stage-specific.
Serialized receipt timing, strict IMF-fixdate parsing, source revision,
release identity, replica independence, local path confinement, and raw hashes
all fail closed. External timestamp, cryptographic signoff, durable external
storage, anonymous same-IP quota availability, and network-path attestation
remain explicitly unverified.


It also pins the schema/artifact identity, row and period bounds, target
order, revised-data flag, and every non-real-time/nonadmitting quarantine
flag. October 2025 CPS unemployment remains unavailable and unimputed; no
post-gap quarter enters the complete-case multivariate panel.

### Frozen v2 experiment

`beforeit-us-revised-data-benchmark-diagnostic.v2` uses a 40-quarter initial
window, expands the training sample one quarter at a time, and produces
iterated forecasts at horizons 1, 2, 4, 8, and 12. The ten models are:
no-change, drift, historical mean, AR(1), AR(4), target-specific
BIC-selected AR(1:8), BeforeIT VAR(1), VAR(2), VAR(3), and a fixed-prior
natural-conjugate BVAR(1). VAR(1) is the relative-score reference.

An adversarial review found that the first implementation validated only model
IDs, discarded fit diagnostics, allowed a complete 40-cell score grid to hide
model failures, and used `truth - forecast` even though the frozen protocol
defines `forecast - truth`. Version 2 corrects those defects:

- a deterministic recursive, type-tagged serialization binds every complete
  model specification and model card;
- an impostor with an identical model ID but changed behavior is rejected;
- the ordered model-ID digest is
  `873f7c65b3e9fbaa9c22f46170a284d88fa5ef29d92c943c9808dd77317dec43`
  and the full model-record-set digest is
  `a3cf9e4b1928a42fe1b19bcf052f786f87603cd78ac0aeef871a3252144d4fe8`;
- `error = point_forecast - actual` is checked against
  `protocol.toml`, recorded in the result manifest, and covered by a
  direction-sensitive integration test;
- AR selected lags, VAR design shape/rank/condition number and companion
  spectral radius, BVAR MNIW prior/version/exact hyperparameters, and maximum
  absolute forecast are retained for every model-origin run; and
- any model failure makes every weighted ranking `NOT_RANKED`, even if a
  40-cell grid can still be formed from remaining common observations.

All-available samples contain 61, 60, 58, 54, and 50 common origins at
horizons 1, 2, 4, 8, and 12. The balanced-horizon-12 track contains 50
origins at every horizon. The aggregate statistic is explicitly

```text
sum(target_weight[target] * horizon_weight[horizon] *
    cellwise_score_ratio[target, horizon])
```

with equal `1/8` target weights and horizon weights
`[0.30, 0.25, 0.20, 0.15, 0.10]`. It is a macro-average of 40 matched
target-by-horizon ratios, **not** a ratio of pooled losses.

### Reproducible revised-data result

The accepted one-thread Julia 1.10.3/LBT-BLAS run produced 22,640 forecast
cells, 610 model-origin diagnostics, zero structured failures, 800 score
summaries, 800 relative scores, and 20 weighted rows. Ratios below are
relative to VAR(1); smaller is better.

| Model | All RMSE | All MAE | Balanced RMSE | Balanced MAE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| No change | 0.951263 | 0.991718 | 0.942606 | 0.982854 |
| Drift | 0.990557 | 1.062904 | 0.981821 | 1.056127 |
| Historical mean | 0.976868 | 1.239199 | 0.926833 | 1.147906 |
| AR(1) | 0.872229 | **0.893327** | 0.867626 | **0.884323** |
| AR(4) | 1.494636 | 1.270642 | 1.493859 | 1.282213 |
| AR-BIC(1:8) | 0.942735 | 0.934519 | 0.940421 | 0.932318 |
| VAR(1) | 1.000000 | 1.000000 | 1.000000 | 1.000000 |
| VAR(2) | 1.734271 | 1.384431 | 1.730737 | 1.364190 |
| VAR(3) | 4.912122 | 2.657647 | 4.911035 | 2.634676 |
| BVAR(1) | **0.862434** | 0.896143 | **0.860248** | 0.890686 |

Thus BVAR(1) has the lowest weighted macro-average cellwise RMSE ratio:
13.76% below VAR(1) on the all-available track and 13.98% below it on the
balanced track. AR(1) has the lowest corresponding MAE ratio: 10.67% and
11.57% below VAR(1). This is not universal dominance. Across the 40
all-available target/horizon RMSE cells, historical mean wins 15, BVAR(1)
wins 6, no-change wins 5, AR(4) wins 2, and AR(1)/AR-BIC account for the
remaining cells; one PCE-price horizon-4 cell is an exact AR(1)/AR-BIC tie.

The retained diagnostics explain much of the poor higher-order VAR result:

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|

The BVAR's posterior companion stability and conditioning are not yet emitted,
so its row is deliberately not interpreted as proof of stability. The current

## 2026-08-06 - Literature policy for taxes, inventory, reconciliation, `Used`, and `Other`

### Why this survey was added

At the user's direction, an independent literature-survey subagent reviewed
official national-accounts guidance and the main academic reconciliation
methods before any unknown or dubious accounting boundary is implemented.
The survey is now a standing design constraint for WS-2C. Its purpose is to
prevent a convenient residual allocation from silently becoming an economic
assumption.

The evidence hierarchy for this decision is:

1. current BEA definitions and U.S. source-account methodology;
2. current UN, Eurostat, and OECD supply-use guidance;
3. peer-reviewed reconciliation methods; and
4. repository conventions only where the first three do not determine the
   treatment.

These are accounting-method decisions, not forecast results. They add no
admitted origin and no ABM or equilibrium-model score.

### Product taxes and valuation: two coherent candidates

The official valuation bridge is, cell by cell:

```text
purchasers-price use
  = basic-price use
  + trade margin
  + transport margin
  + taxes less subsidies on products
```

Eurostat defines the price bases and requires valuation matrices with the
same dimensions as the use table in its
[Eurostat Manual of Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables, pp. 91, 162, and 214](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/3859598/5902113/KS-RA-07-013-EN.PDF.pdf/b0b3d71e-3930-4442-94be-70b36cea9b39?t=1414781402000).
The same separation of basic-price uses from margin and product-tax valuation
tables appears in the
[OECD Supply and Use Tables description](https://www.oecd.org/en/data/datasets/supply-and-use-tables.html)
and the
[2025 OECD Handbook on Extended Supply and Use Tables, step 4](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2025/04/handbook-on-extended-supply-and-use-tables-and-extended-input-output-tables_d85a746f/e9fdcf85-en.pdf).
BEA's U.S. table relationship is documented in its
[Guide to the Interactive Industry Input-Output Accounts Tables](https://www.bea.gov/resources/guide-interactive-industry-input-output-accounts-tables);
Eurostat also maintains a
[current SUT methodology index](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/esa-supply-use-input-tables/methodology).

The frozen implementation policy is therefore:

- **Observed-product-tax candidate.** Allocate `T015` through a governed
  commodity-by-use tax matrix, reconcile basic and purchasers' prices, and
  record the matching government receipt. Keep product taxes `T015`
  definitionally separate from industry taxes `V002`, with an explicit
  double-counting test.
- **Zero-product-tax candidate.** Set the model's dynamic product-tax wedges
  and matching receipts to zero, but preserve the complete observed `T015`
  valuation bridge as an immutable off-model observation/model-gap ledger.
  This candidate must not report that observed basic and purchasers' prices
  are equal.
- **No blind proportional allocation.** Eurostat's tax-allocation guidance
  says allocation follows the applicable tax rules and eligibility: a tax may
  apply only to selected products or users, only to consumption, or to uses
  excluding exports; mixed tax/subsidy rows can require manual treatment
  ([Eurostat Manual, section 8.5.8, p. 220](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/3859598/5902113/KS-RA-07-013-EN.PDF.pdf/b0b3d71e-3930-4442-94be-70b36cea9b39?t=1414781402000)).
  A proportional allocator may be retained only as a rejected diagnostic
  comparator, never as evidence for admission.
- **Selection before forecasting.** Candidate selection and all allocation
  rules must be frozen from source-accounting and transition tests before
  evaluating any held-out forecast accuracy.

This extends the retained controls in
`USAfterRedefinitionsValuationEnvelope.jl` and
`USAfterRedefinitionsFinalUseEnvelope.jl`; it does not fill the presently
missing recipient-cell mapping.

### Inventory, discrepancy, margins, and special commodities

BEA defines change in private inventories as the signed flow of additions
less withdrawals and values the physical-volume change at period-average
prices. Inventory stocks are a separate point-in-time concept
([BEA NIPA Handbook, chapter 7, updated December 2024](https://www.bea.gov/resources/methodologies/nipa-handbook/pdf/chapter-07.pdf)).
The UN SUT/IOT handbook likewise distinguishes changes in inventories by
industry, product, and inventory type and warns that inventory should not be
used as a generic balancing item
([UN Handbook on Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables, inventory discussion in chapters 5 and 6](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SUT_IOT_HB_Final_Cover.pdf)).

The resulting policy is:

- Keep `F030` as signed inventory investment. Never relabel `F030`, a
  commodity imbalance, or a GDP discrepancy as an opening stock.
- Reconcile inventory by holder, stage, and period using:

  ```text
  closing stock
    = opening stock
    + inventory transactions
    + other volume changes
    + holding gains or losses
  ```

  A current-cost stock difference is not generally CIPI because holding gains
  are excluded from the transaction flow
  ([Eurostat Manual, section 5.6.2, p. 155](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/3859598/5902113/KS-RA-07-013-EN.PDF.pdf/b0b3d71e-3930-4442-94be-70b36cea9b39?t=1414781402000)).
- Keep the BEA statistical discrepancy separate. It is the difference
  between GDP and GDI arising from their independent source data, not a
  commodity-balance residual
  ([BEA definition](https://www.bea.gov/help/glossary/statistical-discrepancy);
  [BEA GDP-versus-GDI FAQ](https://www.bea.gov/help/faq/484)).
- Treat margin matrices as valuation reallocations. Positive margins on
  purchased products require the corresponding negative entries on
  margin-service rows so the relevant margin-industry output is conserved;
  margins are not unexplained final use.
- Decompose `Used` before mapping. Transfers of used goods reclassify assets
  among uses and do not create new product output; separately identified
  dealer and transport margins remain current output. Scrap and
  secondhand/used assets therefore remain distinct economic types.
- Preserve the components inside `Other`. Noncomparable imports and the
  rest-of-world adjustment remain separately typed and neither is balancing
  slack. The BEA special-account classification underlying that separation is
  described in the
  [BEA 2017 benchmark industry-tables article, appendix, printed p. 15](https://apps.bea.gov/scb/issues/2018/08-august/pdf/0818-industry-tables.pdf).
- Preserve three different source states: unavailable/suppressed `...`,
  explicit numeric zero, and a confirmed structural zero.

These decisions support the current direction of the final-use, inventory
stock, T50805B, and 2017 special-account diagnostics. The annual-flow to
quarterly-stock bridge and holder/stage allocation remain deliberately
unimplemented.

### Reconciliation method and preregistered comparison

The default candidate for the complete signed, multi-source ledger will be
constrained Stone/generalized least squares (GLS), with cross-entropy and a
corrected sign-aware GRAS implementation as preregistered robustness
comparators. Ordinary RAS is ineligible for the full ledger.

This choice follows the
[UN 2018 SUT/IOT Handbook](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SUT_IOT_HB_Final_Cover.pdf):

- sections 11.104--11.116 require investigation of large and
  non-statistical discrepancies before automatic balancing and favor
  combined manual and automated work;
- sections 11.52--11.55 require reliability categories before balancing;
- Box 11.3 describes ordinary RAS as a method for a nonnegative matrix with
  authoritative margins and Stone reconciliation as covariance-weighted
  adjustment under linear constraints; and
- sections 18.23--18.40 explain limitations of RAS for conflicting sources,
  relative reliability, multiple valuations, and legitimate signed cells,
  while describing GRAS and SUT-RAS extensions.

The academic method lineage is:

- Stone, Champernowne, and Meade,
  [“The Precision of National Income Estimates,” DOI 10.2307/2967664](https://doi.org/10.2307/2967664);
- Byron,
  [“The Estimation of Large Social Account Matrices,” DOI 10.2307/2344807](https://doi.org/10.2307/2344807);
- Robinson, Cattaneo, and El-Said,
  [cross-entropy reconciliation with errors, priors, and constraints, DOI 10.1080/09535310120026247](https://doi.org/10.1080/09535310120026247);
  and
- Lenzen, Wood, and Gallego,
  [corrected GRAS treatment of zeros and signs, DOI 10.1080/09535310701698613](https://doi.org/10.1080/09535310701698613).

An official U.S. example of a reliability-aware least-squares industry
reconciliation is Chen's
[“A Balanced System of U.S. Industry Accounts and Distribution of the Statistical Discrepancy”](https://www.bea.gov/research/papers/2006/balanced-system-industry-accounts-us-and-structural-distribution-statistical).

The implementation sequence is frozen as follows:

1. classify valuation differences, inventory, special accounts, and genuine
   measurement discrepancies before optimization;
2. fix only authoritative controls and confirmed structural zeros;
3. fit constrained GLS to the signed ledger using documented source
   covariance or versioned reliability classes;
4. compare cross-entropy and corrected GRAS only on their eligible,
   explicitly typed problems;
5. allow ordinary RAS only for homogeneous nonnegative blocks with known
   margins; and
6. compare methods by masked-cell and perturbed-control recovery on a frozen
   official benchmark, then freeze the winner and its hyperparameters before
   scoring a forecast origin.

### Acceptance tests implied by the literature

The following tests are now requirements for any admissible WS-2C artifact:

1. **Cell valuation identity:** purchasers minus basic equals trade margin,
   transport margin, and product tax less subsidy for every use cell, with
   only source-rounding tolerance.
2. **Observed-tax conservation:** allocated tax cells reaggregate exactly to
   core plus `Used`/`Other` `T015`; the fiscal receipt has identical scope;
   `T015` and `V002` are disjoint.
3. **Zero-tax isolation:** dynamic tax cells and receipts are exactly zero,
   the observed bridge is byte-unchanged, and no bridge value writes model
   state.
4. **Tax eligibility:** versioned rules cover exemptions and export
   treatment; blind proportional allocation fails closed.
5. **Stock-flow identity:** opening stock plus CIPI, other-volume changes, and
   revaluation equals closing stock for every holder/stage/period; stocks are
   nonnegative and CIPI remains signed.
6. **No residual aliasing:** independent mutation of a commodity residual,
   GDP--GDI discrepancy, `F030`, or stock must not alter any of the others.
7. **Used-goods identity:** seller and purchaser transfers net to zero new
   product output; only separately typed current dealer/transport margins add
   output; scrap remains separate.
8. **Special-account preservation:** `S00401`, `S00402`, `S00300`, and
   `S00900` reaggregate exactly to `Used`/`Other`; no component may be dropped
   or smeared.
9. **Zero semantics:** structural zeros, measured zeros, and unavailable
   `...` cells remain distinguishable.
10. **Signed-cell policy:** every negative has an allowed economic type; no
    clipping, epsilon injection, or unreported sign change is permitted.
11. **Method eligibility:** ordinary RAS rejects negative values, unknown
    margins, mixed price bases, and conflicting controls.
12. **Reliability behavior:** predetermined cells remain fixed; a synthetic
    constraint makes lower-confidence cells absorb more adjustment; every
    covariance/reliability assumption is versioned.
13. **Full per-period accounting:** product supply equals use, industry output
    equals intermediate input plus value added, and expenditure, income, and
    production GDP agree without cross-period cancellation.
14. **Adjustment report:** archive raw, bridged, and balanced values plus
    absolute/relative adjustment, uncertainty, binding constraint,
    method/version, tolerance, and provenance for every cell.
15. **Fail closed:** infeasible controls, missing reliability classes,
    unclassified negatives, or unsatisfied constraints produce no promotable
    artifact.
16. **Benchmark recovery:** on a frozen masked/noised official table, compare
    GLS, cross-entropy, and eligible GRAS by weighted recovery error, maximum
    adjustment, sign/zero violations, and temporal stability.

### Standing `DUBIOUS` register

The following boundaries must remain tagged `DUBIOUS` until direct evidence
or an explicit frozen sensitivity treatment resolves them:

- projecting the 2017 special-account/valuation topology into 2024;
- recipient-cell allocation of `T015`;
- possible `T015`/`V002` overlap;
- annual `F030` to quarterly inventory-stock mapping;
- holder and inventory-stage scope of T50805B;
- scrap versus used-asset treatment inside `Used`;
- noncomparable imports versus the rest-of-world adjustment inside `Other`;
- whether an observed zero is structural;
- legitimate sign changes in subsidy and inventory cells; and
- unavailable source covariance and dependence across source estimates.

For any new unknown of this kind, the standing escalation protocol is:
retain the raw field and provenance, block model-state use, commission a
focused literature/source survey, add the cited decision and adversarial test
to this log, and only then implement a versioned candidate. These findings
justify continuing WS-2C as an accounting and reconciliation gate; they do
not support a forecasting-accuracy claim.

## 2026-08-06 - Canonical opening replay envelope and transition harness

### Why the opening artifacts needed an execution envelope

An adversarial rebuild of the opening candidates with
`--check-bounds=yes` did not reproduce the installed candidate bytes.
Recursive comparison found roughly 2,916 changed floating leaves across
parameters, initial conditions, and derived diagnostics. Typical differences
were approximately `1e-16` to `1e-8`; they were not metadata-only.

The audit traced the change to Julia's bounds option overriding `@inbounds`
inside generic reductions, which changes SIMD/vectorization and floating
reduction order. All economic classifications remained unchanged:

```text
source observation identity: PASS_AT_SOURCE_ROUNDING
latent-state reconciliation: FAIL
inventory-stock evidence:     MISSING
supply/make valuation:        FAIL
full accounting/promotion:    FAIL
origin admissibility:         false
```

This distinction matters scientifically. A numerically different binary is
not automatically a different economic specification, but calling it the
same byte-reproducible artifact would also be false.

### Frozen local rebuild contract

`USJuliaExecutionEnvelope.jl` now defines and validates the exact historical
local build envelope:

```text
Julia:                    1.10.3
platform / CPU:           Darwin aarch64 / Apple M1
bounds:                   auto, code 0
optimization:             O2, minimum O0
fast-math code:           0
inline / Polly:           enabled
CPU target:               native
startup file:             disabled
Julia / BLAS threads:     1 / 1
BLAS vendor:              lbt
```

The builder throws a typed `ExecutionEnvelopeMismatch` containing the
expected environment, actual environment, and per-field differences.
Installed artifacts still receive raw-byte, schema, and semantic validation
on every host. Exact rebuilding occurs only when the complete environment
matches. The declared scope is
`same_frozen_local_execution_envelope_only`, and
`cross_machine_byte_determinism_claimed=false`.

Adversarial subprocesses cover bounds checking, optimization level,
observable IEEE math mode, inlining, and generic CPU target. The initially
considered `--math-mode=fast` probe was removed because Julia 1.10.3 accepts
it without changing `Base.JLOptions().fast_math`; `--math-mode=ieee` is the
observable probe. The helper itself is now hash-pinned by the builder,
candidate manifest, harness contract, and harness output. A wrong helper
hash and a valid hash of the wrong helper file both fail.

An independent provenance audit then found that the build contract did not
bind the mutable Julia builder inputs that were actually executed: its
included source readers and runtime source tree. That gap is now closed.
`opening_macro_candidates.toml` binds the builder, execution-envelope module,
`USSupplyMakeDiagnostics.jl`, `UST10105Controls.jl`, active Project/Manifest,
and a canonical digest of all 57 runtime `src/**/*.jl` files. The builder
records both the actual contract-byte hash and a typed semantic snapshot,
then checks configuration identity again after execution. Copied, unverified,
wrong-hash, or post-verification-mutated configurations fail. Candidate
metadata and the manifest carry the same reader/source-tree commitments, and
the transition harness cross-checks them.

## 2026-08-06 - OECD U.S. source-axis valuation evidence

### Source acquisition and scope

At the user's direction, a source-focused subagent investigated the dubious
tax and valuation boundary before any recipient allocation was attempted.
The official
[OECD Supply and Use Tables dataset](https://www.oecd.org/en/data/datasets/supply-and-use-tables.html)
and
[OECD SDMX API guidance](https://www.oecd.org/en/data/insights/data-explainers/2024/09/api.html)
expose a current 2024 U.S. source system with:

- `T1600`: use at purchasers' prices;
- `T1610`: use at basic prices;
- `T1620`: combined trade and transport margins;
- `T1630`: taxes less subsidies on products;
- `T1633`: gross taxes on products; and
- `T1634`: subsidy magnitude.

The precise public query is `A.USA......V.<table>` with
`startPeriod=2024`, `endPeriod=2024`, and
`dimensionAtObservation=AllDimensions`. The acquisition follows the
[OECD terms and attribution policy](https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html).

All 25 exact responses are archived locally: six data CSVs, three data
structures, four hierarchies, and twelve codelists. They require no
credentials. Every URL, query, requested MIME type, byte count, SHA-256, and
capture time is recorded. The canonical raw-bundle digest is:

```text
b202aa776874eb712a207f9be6f312a12c5d73ed367db881c32f7bb81936a1f7
```

This is a retrieval-day current-vintage diagnostic, not an origin-time
release package.

### Source-axis result

The fixture retains 10,675 unique transaction/activity/product cells and 245
hierarchy-aware axis codes. It does not sum aggregate and descendant rows.
It also quarantines 245 T1610 observations whose valuation is not basic
(`O=123`, `Y=122`).

An identity is evaluated only when every required component is observed:

```text
T1600 = T1610[B] + T1620 + T1630
T1630 = T1633 - T1634
```

The valuation identity is evaluated for 4,226 cells; 6,449 cells are
`NOT_EVALUABLE_SOURCE_MISSING`. The tax identity is evaluated for 1,257
cells; 9,418 cells are not evaluable. Missing components are never
substituted with additive zero: each non-evaluable row has a missing numeric
residual and records the absent component names. Among evaluated rows, the
maximum residual for each equation is one hundredth of a million dollars, the
published source precision.

Published OECD totals are:

| Component | OECD, $m | OECD minus local BEA, $m | Status |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Purchasers-price use | 54,568,422.35 | +150,330.35 | `DUBIOUS` release/boundary residual |
| Basic-price use | 53,558,096.81 | +150,328.81 | `DUBIOUS` release/boundary residual |
| Combined margin | -0.04 | +0.96 | `DUBIOUS`: outside derived +/-$0.505m rounding bound |
| Net product tax | 1,010,325.58 | -0.42 | pass at cross-source rounding |
| Gross product tax | 1,099,681.66 | -0.34 | pass at cross-source rounding |
| Subsidy magnitude | 89,356.07 | +0.07 | pass at cross-source rounding |

The large purchasers/basic residuals are retained unadjusted. Their release
identity and exact source boundary have not been tied to the local BEA
fixture. The combined-margin residual is also retained unadjusted: one OECD
$0.01m observation and one BEA $1m control imply a component-specific
half-unit bound of $0.505m, so +$0.96m is not a rounding pass. Gross product
tax has one OECD term and two BEA terms, hence a $1.005m bound; the net-tax,
gross-tax, and subsidy comparisons remain within their respective exact
bounds. None is a balancing target.

The OECD final-use controls also provide useful falsification evidence:
current-vintage net product tax is $54,853.06m on gross fixed capital
formation, $1,009.27m on inventory change, and $8,346.64m on exports. This
contradicts a universal structural-zero interpretation of export product tax,
but does not by itself identify the 68-sector recipient mapping or authorize
a runtime tax wedge.

Two separate tax records are retained:

1. an observed-tax source-axis record carrying T1630; and
2. an explicit zero-dynamic-tax record that preserves the same immutable
   observed valuation sidecar.

Both leave fiscal-receipt scope, CPA08/ISIC4-to-BEA/model mapping, the
trade-versus-transport split inside T1620, `Used`/`Other`, model state, and
transition testing `NOT_RUN_BLOCKED`. No proportional allocation is

## 2026-08-06 - Fail-closed inventory transition evidence ledger

### Why the sources cannot yet be joined

The literature policy above distinguishes inventory transactions from
point-in-time stocks. BEA's
[NIPA Handbook chapter 7](https://www.bea.gov/resources/methodologies/nipa-handbook/pdf/chapter-07.pdf)
defines change in private inventories as additions less withdrawals, valued
at average prices of the period. The pinned T50805B note separately states
that differences between end-of-quarter current-dollar stocks are not CIPI
because the stock levels use their respective end-quarter prices and CIPI is
a quarterly transaction flow at average-quarter prices. The
[UN SUT/IOT Handbook](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SUT_IOT_HB_Final_Cover.pdf)
also requires product, industry/holder, inventory-type, valuation, and
stock-flow boundaries to be kept explicit.

The new ledger therefore keeps four namespaces separate:

| Evidence | Rows | Economic meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| BEA T10105 | 119 | signed quarterly aggregate CIPI, already divided from SAAR by four exactly once |
| BEA T50805B | 24 | 2026Q1 end-of-quarter current-cost holder-stock rows |
| after-redefinitions F030 | 70 | signed 2024 annual producer-price commodity/closure flow |
| synthetic stage fixture | 5 | non-evidentiary materials/WIP/finished-goods contract comparator |

T10105 contains 94 positive and 25 negative observations; its largest GPDI
identity residual is $0.25m. T50805B lines 1 and 16 deliberately duplicate
the $4,223,030m private-inventory total and remain separately addressed rather
than summed.

The after-redefinitions producer-price F030 cells retain seven negative core
entries:

```text
68-sector core:       $44,095m
Used/Other closure:    $9,450m
cell sum:             $53,545m
published control:    $53,546m
signed residual:          -$1m
```

The four 2024 T10105 quarters also sum to $53,546m. The cross-source check
therefore compares the independently published F030 control with the
independently published quarterly aggregate and has residual $0m under a
±$1m bound. It does not reuse the derived 73-cell numerator. The separate
F030 cell-to-control residual is -$1m under its 73-cell, whole-million
rounding envelope. Neither check is corrected.

This producer-price ledger is not the older Table 259 purchasers-price F030
diagnostic, whose core/`Used` component values differ. The valuation bases
are named explicitly and are never combined.

### Blocked transitions and outputs

Eight transition questions are represented, all as `NOT_RUN_BLOCKED`:

2. revaluation, timing, and inventory-valuation terms;
3. holder-to-commodity mapping;

7. an origin-eligible source release state; and
8. model stock scope, price, and latent-state reconciliation.

Every blocked diagnostic value and tolerance is structurally missing rather
than numeric zero. The ledger emits no 68-sector inventory vector, `S_s`,
initial condition, runtime state, accounting gate, origin, or score.

## 2026-08-06 - Independent evidence-audit corrections

An independent review was run against the newest accounting and origin
artifacts before allowing them to influence a candidate model. It found three
material false-positive paths and four provenance or test-coverage gaps in the completed
artifacts:

1. a synthetically ready origin could self-assert its referenced hashes and
   external gate results without resolving the bytes or running the gate
   validators;
2. the OECD diagnostic used missing components as additive zero while
   describing the resulting identity as cellwise evidence;
3. the +$0.96m OECD/BEA combined-margin residual was compared with a generic
   ±$1m threshold instead of the exact component-specific half-unit bound;
4. the inventory cross-source check reused the 73-cell derived sum rather than
   comparing independently published controls; and
5. the inventory report bound its inputs and contract but not the executable
   module and runner;
6. the opening-candidate contract omitted the executed source readers and
   mutable runtime source tree; and
7. off-envelope CI tested rejection of the Darwin/M1 byte rebuild but did not
   execute candidate construction and transitions.

All seven paths are now corrected. The changes are deliberately recorded here
because earlier entries in this log reported 352 OECD assertions, a margin
rounding pass, a -$1m cross-source inventory residual, and 125 inventory
assertions. The corrected results are the 421/421 and 133/133 checkpoints
above, plus the fully bound opening build and platform-neutral semantic lane.
No prior artifact was promoted and no forecast origin or forecast score was
affected.

The OECD missingness rule now follows the fail-closed validation semantics in
the [SDMX Validation and Transformation Language 2.0 reference manual](https://sdmx.org/wp-content/uploads/VTL-2.0-Reference-Manual-20180416-final.pdf)
and preserves source observations as documented by the
[SDMX guidelines](https://sdmx.org/guidelines/). The source-boundary
interpretation remains grounded in the
[OECD Supply and Use Tables](https://www.oecd.org/en/data/datasets/supply-and-use-tables.html)
and [BEA input-output concepts and methods](https://www.bea.gov/index.php/resources/methodologies/concepts-methods-io-accounts).

## 2026-08-06 - Origin readiness resolver

`USOriginPackages.jl` now requires an `OriginReadinessResolver` whenever a
package would otherwise emit `READY`. The resolver must provide exactly the
protocol, environment, macro-source, and available-block paths declared by
the package. Each path must be an existing non-symlink file, and its raw
SHA-256 is recomputed before and after validation. It must also provide
exactly one callable validator for each required external gate; the callback
must independently return the declared status, reason, and evidence. The
macro-control identity and semantic-mapping gates remain built into the
origin kernel.

Adversarial tests reject:

- a ready-looking package with no resolver;
- changed protocol bytes behind a declared hash;
- a gate whose package text simply declares a pass;
- a fake macro-source hash;
- missing, extra, or mismatched artifact-path keys;
- missing, extra, throwing, or mismatching gate validators; and
- artifact mutation during gate validation.

The suite passes 62/62 assertions in both the default and
`--check-bounds=yes` modes. Current implementation hashes are:

```text
USOriginPackages.jl:
eeaff4ea96d2afbc21bb1674d61fe43ce44745b5b4a0a2388f531a608509dfa1
test_origin_packages.jl:
d548b944d71fbd49f272ac2b91c47e247347df5e5e7af69ffe2f617b4cefcaa4
```

The current diagnostic origin remains non-ready, so its package and
`cannot_run` hashes do not change. This resolver closes self-asserted local
readiness but is not itself an external trust anchor: production admission
still requires a registry that freezes and attests the allowed validator
implementations and identities. Zero origins have been admitted.

## 2026-08-06 - Literature-backed `Used`/`Other` evidence ledger

### Literature survey and source-vintage finding

At the user's direction, a dedicated literature-review subagent investigated
the `Used`, `Other`, scrap, existing-good, dealer-service, transport,
noncomparable-import, and rest-of-world boundaries. A second independent
review found no unsupported inference in the resulting artifact.

The exact current
[BEA after-redefinitions make/use archive](https://apps.bea.gov/industry/release/zip/MAKE-USE-IMPORTS%20(AFTER%20REDEFINITIONS).zip)
has producer-detail workbook sheets for 2007, 2012, and 2017 only; its
producer-summary workbooks extend through 2024. The archive therefore does
not contain a 2022 or 2024 detailed split of the special-account components.
Its pinned ZIP has SHA-256
`c93326b3e4ba3bc2024165448800acb89e9b549090b6b4e0c0c0db27c0eea7da`.
The workbook-sheet inventory is byte-pinned separately.

The semantic policy draws on:

- BEA's official component crosswalk in
  [Preview of the 2018 Comprehensive Update of the Industry Economic Accounts](https://apps.bea.gov/scb/issues/2018/08-august/pdf/0818-industry-tables.pdf),
  Appendix A, page 15;
- BEA's
  [Concepts and Methods of the U.S. Input-Output Accounts](https://www.bea.gov/sites/default/files/papers/WP2006-6.pdf),
  chapters 6, 7, and 12, for used goods, scrap, noncomparable imports, and
  byproduct treatment;
- the [System of National Accounts 2008](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SNA2008.pdf),
  paragraphs 10.38-10.42 and 14.101-14.109, for transfers of existing assets
  and scrap disposal;
- the [European System of Accounts 2010](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/3859598/5925693/KS-02-13-269-EN.PDF.pdf/44cd9d01-bc64-40e5-bd40-d17df0c69334?t=1414781932000),
  paragraphs 9.38-9.47, for existing goods and trade/transport valuation;
- the [UN SUT/IOT Handbook](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SUT_IOT_HB_Final_Cover.pdf),
  paragraphs 2.70-2.72, 7.60-7.64, 7.98-7.114, and 12.26-12.28, for
  byproducts and separately identified services on used goods, waste, and
  scrap; and
- the [2025 OECD Handbook on Extended Supply and Use Tables](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/oecd/en/publications/reports/2025/04/handbook-on-extended-supply-and-use-tables-and-extended-input-output-tables_d85a746f/e9fdcf85-en.pdf),
  chapter 3, steps 4-5, for valuation and domestic/import separation.

The common best-practice conclusion is narrow but decisive: a transfer of an
existing good does not create new output of the underlying good. Current
output may arise from separately observed dealer, auction, repair,
ownership-transfer, or transport services, but those services cannot be
inferred as a percentage of a net `Used` row. Scrap can contain both
current-production byproduct output and disposal of existing assets; those
channels must remain distinct.

### Evidenced component semantics

The ledger retains 4,162 cells with separate numeric, blank, ellipsis,
selected-zero-not-shown, explicit-zero, and signed-value masks. It keeps 2017
detail, 2017 summary, and 2024 summary as separate namespaces. The pinned 2017
evidence supports:

## 2026-08-06 - Constrained Stone/GLS reconciliation method qualification

The planned reconciliation method has now been implemented and qualified on a
frozen synthetic signed ledger. The estimator is:

```text
x_hat = y + Sigma A' (A Sigma A')^+ (b - A y)
Sigma_hat = Sigma - Sigma A' (A Sigma A')^+ A Sigma
```

Predetermined cells and confirmed structural zeros are removed from the
adjustable vector. The covariance must be symmetric positive definite on that
vector. A tolerance-ranked Moore-Penrose inverse accepts consistent dependent
adjustable controls and rejects inconsistent exact controls. Fixed-only
validation rows are classified separately from adjustable restrictions.

This method follows Stone, Champernowne, and Meade,
[The Precision of National Income Estimates](https://doi.org/10.2307/2967664)
(1942); Byron,
[The Estimation of Large Social Account Matrices](https://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/645001467980482557/pdf/REP65000The0es0ial0account0matrices.pdf)
(1978), equations 5-9; and the
[UN SUT/IOT Handbook](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SUT_IOT_HB_Final_Cover.pdf),
sections 11.104-11.120 and 18.79-18.81. The defining best practice is that
more reliable observations receive lower variance and therefore move less
under exact accounting restrictions.

The frozen six-cell benchmark contains four adjustable cells, two exact cells
(one predetermined and one structural zero), and five exact controls. An
adversarial audit corrected the original report's taxonomy: there are three
controls with adjustable coefficients, two fixed-only validation controls,
adjustable rank two, and one genuinely dependent adjustable control—not three
“redundant” controls. A new negative test with one adjustable identity and two
fixed-only checks reports zero dependent adjustable controls. The
low-confidence cell has nine times the variance and absorbs nine times the
absolute adjustment of its paired high-confidence cell:

| Diagnostic | Raw | Reconciled |
|---|---:|---:|
| RMSE versus frozen truth | 2.2546248764 | 0.0577350269 |
| MAE versus frozen truth | 1.0000000000 | 0.0333333333 |
| covariance-weighted RMSE | 0.9501461876 | 0.0527046277 |
| maximum exact-control residual | n/a | 0 |

There are zero sign, exact-cell, and structural-zero violations. These
improvements are a synthetic recovery test only and are not economic forecast
accuracy.

Three comparator families are preregistered but correctly remain
`NOT_RUN_BLOCKED`:

- ordinary RAS is ineligible for this signed, general-linear-control
  benchmark under the UN handbook;
- cross-entropy requires frozen supports, priors, error treatment, and a
  verified solver, following Robinson, Cattaneo, and El-Said,
  [Updating and Estimating a Social Accounting Matrix Using Cross Entropy Methods](https://doi.org/10.1080/09535310120026247);
- signed GRAS requires the corrected zero and objective treatment in Lenzen,
  Wood, and Gallego,
  [Some Comments on the GRAS Method](https://doi.org/10.1080/09535310701698613),
  plus an eligible row/column-margin problem.

## 2026-08-06 - Census M3 manufacturing inventory-stage evidence

### Pinned current-vintage source

The exact Census historical M3 workbook was captured from the official
mutable current-workbook URL at `2026-08-06T16:40:45Z`. It is 969,323 bytes,
has SHA-256
`74ee0d3b9d4a9673a39f1f4ece28206dcccca6451f48aee63506c61675373538`,
and carried a server `Last-Modified` date of 2026-08-04. The workbook contains

`CURRENT_VINTAGE_DIAGNOSTIC_NOT_ORIGIN_ELIGIBLE`, not a reconstructed
historical vintage.

The source-faithful fixture retains:

| Quantity | Count |
|---|---:|
| workbook rows | 11,060 |
| series | 316 |
| seasonally adjusted / unadjusted series | 158 / 158 |
| total-inventory series | 172 |

For each of 48 same-code adjusted or unadjusted stage sets, the artifact
evaluates:

```text
total inventory = materials and supplies + work in process + finished goods
```

There are 20,160 potential identities: 19,872 pass exactly, 288 are
`NOT_RUN_SOURCE_MISSING` for workbook cells in 2026-07 through 2026-12, and
zero fail. Missing terms remain missing; they are never materialized as zero.

For orientation, the December 2024 total-manufacturing seasonally adjusted
values are total $941,027m, materials $347,829m, WIP $261,679m, and finished
goods $331,519m. The corresponding unadjusted values are $919,666m,
$344,159m, $255,443m, and $320,064m. These are end-of-month manufacturing
holder stocks, not economy-wide stocks or quarterly inventory-investment
flows.

### Why exact additivity is not independent validation

The official
[Census M3 collection and estimation methodology](https://www.census.gov/manufacturing/m3/how_the_data_are_collected/index.html)
states that many companies report total inventories but cannot report stage
detail. Census uses the three-digit NAICS total as a control, ratio-estimates
materials, WIP, and finished goods, and proportionally allocates the
difference back to the stages. After separate seasonal adjustment, it again
proportionally allocates the discrepancy to the adjusted total. Exact
additivity is therefore a published controlled accounting identity, not four
independent measurements and not validation of the ABM's inventory
transitions.

This interpretation is consistent with the
[M3 historical code/layout documentation](https://www.census.gov/manufacturing/m3/historical_data/naicshist.pdf),
the [historical-series revision warning](https://www.census.gov/manufacturing/m3/historical/timeseries.html),
the [M3 inventory definitions](https://www.census.gov/manufacturing/m3/definitions/index.html),
and the [survey scope description](https://www.census.gov/manufacturing/m3/about_the_surveys/index.html).

### Literature-survey mapping boundary

A dedicated follow-up literature survey compared M3 concepts with national
accounts and inventory-model practice. The resulting boundary is:

| Question | Evidence-based determination | Required model treatment |
|---|---|---|
| coverage and sample | domestic manufacturing; a large-company, nonprobability panel used to estimate the universe | constrain holder-industry aggregates only; do not infer firm-size distributions or individual agents |
| reporting unit | a reporting unit can contain several establishments and activity outside its assigned category | treat NAICS as a noisy aggregate holder classification, not a pure establishment or commodity |
| materials | title-held raw and semifabricated inputs for production | possible noisy manufacturer-input-stock observation; product composition remains unidentified |
| WIP | accumulated production cost, including some undelivered long-term-contract work not reported as sales | possible noisy production-pipeline stock; no physical units, completion rates, or gross transitions |
| finished goods | completed goods ready for shipment plus goods bought for resale without further processing | not pure own-output inventory and not automatically SNA finished goods or model `S_s` |
| valuation | nominal non-LIFO business-accounting values; published estimates are not price adjusted | not physical quantity or uniform replacement cost; raw book-value changes cannot be CIPI |
| timing | end-of-month stocks | use March/June/September/December for a quarter-end state; never sum monthly stock levels |
| product mapping | holder industry, not commodity composition | an I-O materials-purchase bridge is an explicit assumption requiring sensitivity analysis |
| ownership boundary | manufacturer-owned goods can include inventory in transit, warehouses, and sales branches; customer/government-owned goods are excluded | ownership is not plant location, logistics availability, or delivery readiness |
| economy-wide distribution | independent wholesale and retail inventories are outside M3 | require separate wholesale/retail sources and states |
| transitions | closing stocks only | MI-to-WIP, WIP-to-FI, withdrawals, losses, and sales flows require additional evidence |

The [Census M3 Instruction Manual](https://www.census.gov/manufacturing/m3/get_forms/instructionman.pdf)
(form dated 2024-03-18, part A section 1 and part B sections 1 and 5-8)
establishes the title/location, non-LIFO valuation, resale-good, stage, and
required-additivity rules. [M3 Benchmark Table 6](https://www.census.gov/manufacturing/m3/bench/pdf/benchtable6.pdf),
note 1, states that the estimates are end-of-period and not adjusted for price
changes.

BEA's
[NIPA Handbook chapter 7](https://www.bea.gov/resources/methodologies/nipa-handbook/pdf/chapter-07.pdf)
(December 2024, pages 7-2 and 7-5 through 7-14, plus appendix B) distinguishes
holder industry from product, uses final-month quarter-end differences, and
revalues M3 book values using product prices, unit labor costs, turnover, and
accounting-method information. Its benchmark materials allocation uses the
industry's input-output materials-purchase composition; this is a bridge
assumption, not information contained in M3.

The [2008 SNA concepts-in-brief](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/2008sna-conceptsbrief.pdf)
(paragraphs 10.118-10.147 and 14.110-14.111) makes inventory stage
holder-relative and distinguishes producer finished goods from goods for
resale. The
[Eurostat-OECD Compilation Guide on Inventories](https://doi.org/10.1787/9789264283060-en)
(2017, paragraphs 1.7-1.10, 4.1-4.6, and 4.39-4.42) explains why business book
values require an accounting-method-specific bridge to national-account
current prices.

Iacoviello, Schiantarelli, and Schuh,
[Input and Output Inventories in General Equilibrium](https://www.federalreserve.gov/Pubs/Ifdp/2010/1004/ifdp1004.pdf)
(2010, pages 10-11 and footnote 14), explicitly warn that there is no uniquely
justified mapping from manufacturing finished goods and wholesale inventories
to a model output-inventory concept. Schuh,
[Evidence on the Link between Firm-Level and Aggregate Inventory Behavior](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/feds/evidence-on-the-link-between-firm-level-and-aggregate-inventory-behavior.htm)
(1997, especially pages 16-18), finds substantial aggregation bias in
inventory-adjustment speeds. Those results rule out proportional assignment to
identical agents and calibration of representative-agent adjustment speeds
from the M3 aggregate alone.

Accordingly, `M3 finished goods = model sellable stock S_s` is classified
`DUBIOUS_NOT_IDENTIFIED`. It could be used only as a noisy observation if the
model state were explicitly restricted to nominal, end-of-month,
manufacturer-owned U.S. or qualifying in-transit goods requiring no further
processing by that holder, including resale goods. It cannot stand for
own-produced goods only, consumer-ready availability, economy-wide
manufacturing/wholesale/retail stocks, physical quantity, product-specific
availability, or plant-located inventory.

The recommended future observation layer is:

```text
y_M3(i,t,v) = H(i,v; x_ABM(t)) + measurement_error(i,t,v)
```

where `H` freezes holder/title scope, NAICS aggregation, end-of-month timing,
valuation, seasonal adjustment, industry-to-commodity bridge, and resale-good
treatment. To avoid counting the Census-enforced identity four times, the
target vector should use total manufacturer inventory plus two independent
composition coordinates, such as materials and WIP shares; the finished-goods
share is then residual. The measurement covariance must be singular/correlated
or expressed in those independent coordinates, with uncertainty informed by
revisions and alternate mapping assumptions.

## 2026-08-06 - Production reconciliation readiness ledger

### Outcome and scope

The first production-reconciliation checkpoint is now implemented as an
authenticated readiness ledger rather than a premature balance. It freezes
one future problem tuple:

```text
country:           USA
reference period:  calendar year 2024
frequency/timing:  annual calendar-year accounting flow
stock-flow class:  flow
currency/unit:     USD, millions of current dollars
price basis:       producers' prices
axis:              BEA after-redefinitions 68-sector core
                   plus explicit Used/Other closure
candidate method:  constrained Stone/GLS
```

The implementation is
`scripts/us/accounting/USProductionReconciliationReadiness.jl`; its strict
contract is `production_reconciliation_readiness.toml`. The ledger
authenticates exact upstream artifacts, probes their economic boundary fields,
and keeps evidence validation separate from statistical admission. It does
not construct a production observation, exact control, reliability class,
covariance entry, reconciliation result, model state, origin, or score.

### Audit-driven deviation: the qualified Stone schema is synthetic-only

Two independent audit subagents reviewed the proposed production intake and
the existing Stone implementation before it could be reused. They found a
hard interface boundary that was not explicit in the original plan:

- the current `LedgerCell` requires a synthetic `truth_value` and
  `benchmark_role`;
- `StoneProblem` validation requires a classification containing
  `SYNTHETIC`, `noised=true`, and `production_source=false`; and
- every current control is exact.

It would therefore be invalid to fabricate truth for BEA/OECD observations or
disable those checks. `PRODUCTION_STONE_PROBLEM_SCHEMA_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` is now
a hard blocker. The future production cell schema has no truth field and
instead requires source hash, release ID, availability/vintage, period,
frequency, time basis, stock/flow class, country, currency/unit, price and
valuation basis, classification axes, source cell state, signed economic
type/domain, transformation lineage, uncertainty/covariance IDs, and
scope-hash-bound approval.

The audit also identified a report defect in the synthetic qualification. The
old `control_count - rank = 3` label called two fixed-only validation rows
“redundant.” The corrected result is:

```text
total exact controls:                    5
controls with adjustable coefficients:  3
fixed-only validation controls:          2
adjustable restriction rank:             2
dependent adjustable controls:           1
```

A new test containing one adjustable restriction plus two fixed-only checks
returns zero dependent adjustable controls. The numerical solution and
adjustment ledger are unchanged. This correction raises the focused Stone
suite to 168/168 and prevents fixed-cell checks from being interpreted as
duplicate statistical information.

The audit recorded additional production requirements rather than weakening
the research-only module: normalized restriction scaling, dimensionless
feasibility diagnostics, complete missing/zero states, explicit economic sign
domains, positive-semidefinite posterior checks, `A Sigma_hat` diagnostics,
unconstrained-cell reporting, non-synthetic uncertainty receipts, and one
trusted writer that recomputes from rehashed inputs. These are represented in
the readiness blockers and future tests.

### Source-family intake result

Nine evidence families are now represented with complete declared semantic
tuples:

| Evidence family | Relation to target | Current admission |
|---|---|---|
| 2024 BEA after-redefinitions producer core | year, flow, unit, price basis, and core axes match | evidence validated; zero cells admitted pending mask/sign/import/control/uncertainty approval |
| 2024 BEA `Used`/`Other` summary | year and producer-price summary match; economic type is mixed | blocked; current components and transaction services unresolved |
| BEA before/after-redefinitions valuation envelope | mixed basic/producer/purchaser concepts and unbound cross-archive release | quarantined |
| OECD USA 2024 SUT source axes | independent valuation challenger with CPA08/ISIC4 axes | quarantined; mapping absent and cross-source residuals dubious |
| BEA T10105 2024 CIPI | signed quarterly transaction flow at average-quarter prices | aggregate cross-check only; no commodity allocation |
| BEA T50805B 2026Q1 inventory | quarter-end holder stock at current cost | quarantined; wrong period, timing, stock/flow class, valuation, and axis |
| Census M3 stages | monthly manufacturer-holder book-value stock | quarantined; controlled stages and no observation operator |
| BEA 2017 special-account detail | semantic evidence for scrap, used transfers, imports, and residence adjustment | semantic only; 2017-to-2024 share projection prohibited |
| synthetic Stone benchmark | algebraic method fixture | method qualification only; not an economic source |

The F030 and `Used`/`Other` ledgers are recognized as semantic projections of
the same underlying BEA lineage, not extra independent observations. A
`canonical_source_key` and `lineage_hash` are mandatory before these views can
enter a covariance model.

### Literature and official-practice policy

At the user's direction, literature-survey subagents were used for the
dubious covariance, control, zero/sign, inventory, M3, `Used`, and `Other`
questions. The following practices are now frozen in the contract and cited
there by exact locator:

- The
  [UN SUT/IOT Handbook](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SUT_IOT_HB_Final_Cover.pdf)
  (sections 11.52-11.55, 11.104-11.120, 18.23-18.40, and 18.79-18.81)
  requires reliability categories and investigation of large/non-statistical
  discrepancies before automated balancing. It supports Stone-style
  covariance weighting but does not make every published total an exact,
  independent restriction.
- Stone, Champernowne, and Meade's
  [precision framework](https://doi.org/10.2307/2967664) and Byron's
  [large-SAM estimator](https://doi.org/10.2307/2344807) support
  source-reliability covariance, predetermined cells, and explicit accounting
  restrictions. They do not justify synthetic variances as production
  measurement error.
- Stanger's IMF paper,
  [Estimating and Reconciling Supply and Use Tables within a Balanced System of National Accounts](https://doi.org/10.5089/9781484363966.005),
  provides an official restricted, reliability-weighted GLS example. The
  resulting policy is that source reliability must be versioned before
  balancing; confidence labels alone cannot become arbitrary variances.
- Nalewaik's Federal Reserve study,
  [News, Noise, and Estimates of the “True” Unobserved State of the Economy](https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2007/200734/revision/index.html),
  shows why variance weights are not self-identifying: essentially arbitrary
  weights can be rationalized without additional information, and revisions
  can either add news or reduce noise. The project therefore requires
  revision/source evidence and shared-source dependence in `V`; a “hard”
  label by itself is not a variance estimate.
- Smith, Weale, and Satchell,
  [Measurement Error with Accounting Constraints](https://doi.org/10.1111/1467-937X.00037),
  extend reconciliation to serially correlated errors, efficient weight
  estimation, interval estimates, and specification tests. The production
  report must consequently include uncertainty or sensitivity bands and
  covariance diagnostics; a point-balanced matrix alone is not an
  accuracy-qualified result.
- The IMF's official
  [Algorithm to Balance Supply and Use Tables](https://doi.org/10.5089/9781484363966.002)
  makes adjustment size depend on relative input reliability and recommends
  economic diagnostic ratios after balancing. This supports an auditable
  hard/soft evidence hierarchy, while still requiring the numerical weights
  to be sourced rather than invented.
- The
  [Eurostat SUT Manual](https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/3859598/5902113/KS-RA-07-013-EN.PDF.pdf/b0b3d71e-3930-4442-94be-70b36cea9b39)
  requires explicit valuation matrices for trade margins, transport margins,
  and taxes less subsidies. Mixed price bases cannot be reconciled by merely
  relabeling a row or spreading an aggregate discrepancy.
- The
  [BEA NIPA Handbook chapter 7](https://www.bea.gov/resources/methodologies/nipa-handbook/pdf/chapter-07.pdf)
  and the
  [Eurostat-OECD Compilation Guide on Inventories](https://doi.org/10.1787/9789264283060-en)
  require source/accounting-method-specific bridges between business book
  values, current-cost stocks, holding gains, and inventory transactions.
  This supports the hard separation of F030/T10105 flows, T50805B holder
  stocks, and M3 stages.
- Census's
  [M3 estimation methodology](https://www.census.gov/manufacturing/m3/how_the_data_are_collected/index.html)
  says total inventory controls the three reported stages and discrepancies
  are proportionally allocated. Total plus materials plus WIP plus finished
  goods therefore cannot be four independent diagonal observations.
- The
  [2008 SNA](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SNA2008.pdf)
  distinguishes inventory stages, goods for resale, current output, and
  existing-asset transfers. This rules out treating all `Used` as output,
  all M3 finished goods as model sellable stock, or `Other` as domestic
  technology.
- Cross-entropy remains blocked until supports, priors, and error
  distributions are frozen, following
  [Robinson, Cattaneo, and El-Said](https://doi.org/10.1080/09535310120026247).
  Corrected GRAS remains restricted to eligible signed row/column-margin
  problems with proper zero treatment, following
  [Lenzen, Wood, and Gallego](https://doi.org/10.1080/09535310701698613).
  The original signed-matrix motivation in
  [Junius and Oosterhaven](https://doi.org/10.1080/0953531032000056954)
  also rules out removing negative cells, applying nonnegative RAS, and then
  adding the negatives back.

The production contract consequently distinguishes:

```text
EXACT_ACCOUNTING_IDENTITY
MEASURED_PUBLISHED_MARGIN
FIXED_PUBLISHED_CONTROL_APPROVED
```

A rounded published total defaults to a measured observation, not an exact
fixed control. Shared source lineage, enforced identities, revisions,
crosswalks, valuation bridges, and aggregate/component relationships must be
represented through covariance or independent coordinates; different labels
do not establish independence.

### Literature survey: identity, lineage, dependence, and source states

At the user's direction, a literature-survey subagent reviewed the dubious
lineage, alternate-view, measured-control, and selected-zero questions before
the policies were frozen.

The resulting policy is:

1. **Separate semantic identity from release-specific evidence.** W3C
   [PROV-DM sections 5.2.1 and
   5.7.1](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/#term-Derivation) requires identified
   entities and explicit derivations; its
   [primary-source relation](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/#term-primary-source)
   supports tracing derived records to their source. The
   [SDMX glossary](https://sdmx.org/wp-content/uploads/SDMX_Glossary_Version_2_1_December_2020.htm#_Toc59116913)
   defines observations through dimension/series keys and time, while W3C
   [Data on the Web BP11](https://www.w3.org/TR/dwbp/#VersionIdentifiers)
   separates a persistent resource identifier from immutable version
   identifiers. The ledger therefore uses a value-independent
   `canonical_source_key` and a release/value/state-sensitive `lineage_hash`.
   Length-prefixed cryptographic serialization is a project implementation
   inferred from these standards, not a W3C or SDMX mandate.
2. **Do not count alternate views as independent evidence.** PROV-DM
   [sections 5.5.1-5.5.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/#term-specialization)
   represents specialization and alternate views explicitly. Weale's
   [national-accounts reconciliation
   paper](https://academic.oup.com/jrsssa/article/151/1/211/7106651)
   (1988, p. 211) requires attention to covariance implied by how estimates
   were constructed. The official BEA reconciliation study by Rassier et al.
   ([2007, sections 4.1-4.2, PDF pp.
   6-8](https://www.bea.gov/sites/default/files/papers/WP2007-5.pdf))
   explains that zero-correlation assumptions can lose efficiency and that
   misspecified correlations can be harmful. F030 and `Used`/`Other` views
   are consequently annotations on canonical owners, not new likelihood
   terms. The F030 IO total and T10105 annual sum receive an explicit
   common-estimand/dependence-unresolved relation.
3. **Keep latent identities separate from published measurements.** The
   [UN SUT/IOT Handbook](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SUT_IOT_HB_Final_Cover.pdf)
   treats supply/use and production/income relations as fundamental
   identities (sections 2.7-2.10 and 11.10-11.17), but also warns that
   published examples need not add exactly because of rounding (section
   1.46). The ledger therefore distinguishes unapproved
   `EXACT_ACCOUNTING_IDENTITY` candidates from
   `MEASURED_PUBLISHED_MARGIN` records. A whole-million published total
   carries an unapproved rounding/measurement model; it is not silently made
   exact.
4. **Keep value separate from observation status.** SDMX's
   [observation-status
   definition](https://sdmx.org/wp-content/uploads/SDMX_Glossary_Version_2_1_December_2020.htm#_Toc59116859)
   and current
   [`CL_OBS_STATUS` codelist, version
   2.3](https://sdmx.org/wp-content/uploads/CL_OBS_STATUS_v2_3-for-publication.docx)
   distinguish normal values, generic missingness, suppression,
   non-significant/rounded values, imputation, and values that cannot exist.
   W3C [BP31](https://www.w3.org/TR/dwbp/#Enrichment) also requires inferred
   values to remain distinguishable from originals. Accordingly, explicit
   numeric zero, selected-zero-not-shown, and an approved structural zero are
   different states. Selected-zero cells and controls have a null value;
   nothing in this checkpoint imputes them to zero.

The current canonical key is stable inside this authenticated BEA projection
contract: it excludes release hashes, values, authenticated positions,
descriptions, and local semantic-view IDs. It still contains the official
source member and projection semantics. A higher-level persistent
cross-release `estimand_id` remains an addition for the bitemporal warehouse;
the new key must not be overclaimed as already solving cross-archive identity.
That limitation remains covered by the common-release and vintage blockers.

### Canonical source and derived lineage

The target and control parent sets are disjoint, individually unique, and

### Controls, overlays, and the axis bug found adversarially

The control registry contains **924 quarantined candidates**:

Of the measured margins, 527 have numeric right-hand sides and 51 retain
selected-zero/null right-hand sides. All identities remain
`CANDIDATE_UNAPPROVED_NOT_SOLVER_ADMITTED`; all margins remain
`NOT_APPROVED_NOT_SOLVER_ADMITTED`.

There are 588 value-free overlays: 70 F030 references and 518
`Used`/`Other` source-coordinate annotations. The latter comprise 508 cell
references and ten control references and resolve to 500 unique
`Used`/`Other` owners. Two owners intersect the F030 view, so the union is 568
canonical owners.

The first full validation observed only 500 owners in the union. The cause
was not a count typo: BEA industry and commodity codes overlap, and a generic
code-membership mapper reversed the row/column roles for the make table,
collapsing distinct owners. The fix dispatches on each authenticated
projection's axis semantics:

```text
make:              row = industry, column = commodity
use/import use:    row = commodity, column = industry
final/control:     row = commodity
```

After the correction, the exact relationship is
`70 + 500 - 2 = 568`. This is a concrete example of why typed axes, not code
strings or equal vector lengths, determine economic meaning.

### Synthetic solver trust-boundary correction

An independent adversarial audit found that the public synthetic
`reconcile_stone(problem, contract)` method previously accepted a hand-built
`StoneProblem` carrying copied synthetic flags and hashes but fabricated
values. That did not admit the new production ledger, but it made the
synthetic qualification boundary weaker than its documentation.

The public method now:

1. requires the exact fixture ID, classification, unit, and source hash;
2. reloads the hash-pinned contract and fixture;
3. compares the caller's full contract and problem semantics to those trusted
   objects, allowing only cell/control/term order permutations; and
4. solves from the freshly loaded objects rather than caller-owned mutable
   state.

Forged values, controls, metadata, source hashes, and hash-copied contract
mutations are rejected. Deliberately altered qualification fixtures reach
only an unexported test helper. The production ledger module contains no
`StoneProblem`, `LedgerCell`, `truth_value`, `benchmark_role`,
`reconcile_stone`, or synthetic-solver import.

The corrected synthetic suite passes 183/183 with the same numerical
qualification result. This strengthens method-fixture integrity; it remains
neither a production balance nor economic accuracy evidence.
