## 2026-08-06 - WS-2C admission evidence: full-grid display semantics, signed-flow literature, and zero-weight lineage

### Outcome and scientific boundary

The next production-reconciliation checkpoint is implemented as authenticated
**admission evidence, not solver approval**. It resolves the narrow published
display meaning of the pinned BEA ellipsis tokens, materializes the complete
raw-source observation loading, adds an exact literature-backed sign-domain
overlay for the 23 previously unresolved negative cells, and records the
smallest defensible producer-price domestic/import sidecar.

The evidence artifact deliberately does not create a reliability weight,
covariance parameter, structural-zero certificate, approved identity,
solver-input cell, reconciliation adjustment, model-state write, forecast
origin, gate change, or forecast score. Those counts remain zero.

### Release-scoped ellipsis evidence and the full-grid correction

The producer make and producer use workbooks in the immutable [BEA September
25, 2025 archive](https://apps.bea.gov/HistData/Files/Releases/Industry/2025/GDP_by_Industry/Q2/Annual_September-25-2025/MAKE-USE-IMPORTS%20(AFTER%20REDEFINITIONS).zip)
state at `2024!A83` and `2024!A89` that selected zero-valued data are not
shown. The authenticated source-note fixture also preserves ellipsis witnesses
at `2024!E8` and distinct literal-zero witnesses. This proves a published
display value of zero in those producer workbooks, but not a structural zero,
an exact unrounded zero, a variance, or a general missing-value rule.

The import workbook has no equivalent local note. A BEA iTable capture was
therefore made from the exact `UIMARI` and `MakeAR` POST requests to
`https://apps.bea.gov/iTablecore/data/app/GetSteps`. The request contains no
release selector. An initial implementation compared only marker and
literal-zero coordinates; adversarial review correctly rejected that as
insufficient to bind the mutable iTable response to the archived release.

The corrected receipt checks in every common-basis API token and archived
workbook value:

| Table | API axes | Archived common basis | Markers | Literal zeros | Nonzero integers | Exact cells | Mismatches |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| UIMARI | 73 × 93 | 6,789 | 4,102 | 369 | 2,318 | 6,789 | 0 |
| MakeAR | 72 × 74 | 71 × 73 = 5,183 | 4,682 | 84 | 417 | 5,183 | 0 |
| **Total** | — | **11,972** | **8,784** | **453** | **2,735** | **11,972** | **0** |

The maximum absolute numeric difference is `$0m`. The extra MakeAR API row and
column are empty total-axis entries and are excluded explicitly rather than
silently dropped. The checked-in 11,972-row grid preserves table, positions,
codes, raw API token, token class, parsed value, authenticated display value,
archived source-cell kind/value, and the exact-match flag. Offline CI reparses
that grid and recomputes its order, counts, hashes, class coordinates, semantic
matches, and value matches without trusting receipt-only assertions.

This establishes captured iTable content identity with the pinned archive on
the complete modeled grid. The import ellipsis may therefore be used as a
**published display point of zero for this release/table only**. It remains
distinct from numeric zero in raw provenance and remains unapproved as a
structural-zero or statistical-error model.

The 346 identity candidates and 578 published-margin diagnostics remain
unapproved. The half-unit envelope is a deterministic display-resolution
sensitivity calculation, not a confidence interval, probability distribution,
variance, or solver weight. The source does not certify a nearest-integer
rounding model.

### Observation loading and domestic/import boundary

The report emits 19,428 coefficient-one source loadings covering 17,422 target
cells and 578 measured-margin owners. The loading is an evidence-only `H`
mapping: all numerical reliability and covariance receipt IDs are null and all
solver-admissible flags are false.

Following the [BEA import-matrix methodology, chapter 12, printed pp.
12-5–12-7](https://www.bea.gov/sites/default/files/papers/WP2006-6.pdf) and
the [BEA interactive I-O guide, “Import matrix”](https://www.bea.gov/resources/guide-interactive-industry-input-output-accounts-tables),
the imported-use cells remain signed BEA imputed allocations, not directly
observed recipient-level trade and not automatically nonnegative model demand.
The smallest defensible sidecar is:

```text
domestic display point = producer-use display point - import-allocation display point
```

This creates 6,160 deterministic, zero-extra-likelihood records:

| Domestic-use state | Count |
|---|---:|
| raw numeric residual evaluable: neither parent lineage contains a selected-zero leaf | 2,480 |
| display point only: at least one selected-zero source leaf | 3,680 |
| total | 6,160 |
| F050 import-accounting-offset diagnostics within total | 70 |

An adversarial review found that the first draft used the aggregated target
state. Nine mixed numeric/ellipsis aggregates were thereby misreported as raw
numeric because an aggregate is labeled numeric when not all leaves are
selected-zero. The corrected implementation counts selected-zero **source
leaves** across both parent lineages. For example,
`AR24:DOMESTIC_INTERMEDIATE_USE:CORE:113FF:4A0` has six selected-zero leaves,
a display point of `$44m`, and a null raw residual. Positive- and
negative-import arithmetic witnesses are also fixed:

```text
113FF × 111CA: 31,652 - 290 = 31,362
113FF × F030:     356 - (-9) = 365
```

Internal controls now recompute every display point, nullable raw residual,
selected-leaf count, leaf count, source-coordinate pairing, scenario ID, and
`domestic1:` lineage hash from the observation loading. F050 remains an
accounting-offset diagnostic only.

No 2024 commodity-by-recipient allocation of trade margins, transport margins,
or product taxes has been authenticated. Historical 2017 wedges are not
projected, and the independent [OECD Supply and Use Tables
dataset](https://www.oecd.org/en/data/datasets/supply-and-use-tables.html)
remains a source-axis challenger rather than a BEA recipient bridge.

### `Used`, `Other`, and other negative cells: literature survey and exact overlay

The requested academic/industry survey was applied only through exact
cell-keyed evidence:

- [BEA Concepts and Methods, chapter 6, printed pp.
  6-5–6-6](https://www.bea.gov/sites/default/files/papers/WP2006-6.pdf)
  distinguishes scrap as current byproduct output from used/secondhand goods
  produced in prior periods and records purchases and sales as signed uses.
- [SNA 2008, paragraphs 10.38–10.42 and
  14.101–14.109](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SNA2008.pdf)
  records existing-asset acquisitions and disposals with buyer/seller signs
  and keeps ownership-transfer services as separate current output.
- [BEA Concepts and Methods, chapter 7, printed pp.
  7-9–7-11](https://www.bea.gov/sites/default/files/papers/WP2006-6.pdf)
  describes noncomparable imports and the rest-of-world residence
  reclassification.
- [BEA’s 2018 classification appendix, p.
  15](https://apps.bea.gov/scb/issues/2018/08-august/pdf/0818-industry-tables.pdf)
  shows summary `Used = S00401 + S00402` and
  `Other = S00300 + S00900`; it is a crosswalk, not a 2024 allocation.
- [BEA NIPA Handbook chapter 7, printed pp.
  7-2–7-3](https://www.bea.gov/resources/methodologies/nipa-handbook/pdf/chapter-07.pdf)
  defines change in private inventories as additions less withdrawals, an
  intrinsically signed flow distinct from an inventory stock.

The overlay binds every row to the exact target ID, raw value, workbook hash,
sheet, derived workbook address, A–G classification signature, registered
literature ID, and page/paragraph locator. Sign, magnitude, adjacency, and
label-pattern inheritance are forbidden.

| Class | Exact cells | Evidence classification | Result |
|---|---:|---|---|
| A | four import F030 cells: `113FF -9`, `211 -79`, `323 -14`, `3364OT -10,549` | imputed import allocation to inventory change | signed flow |
| B | six `Used` fixed-investment cells: `F02E -165,381`, `F02R -1,182`, `F02S -3,668`, `F06S -4`, `F07S -1,048`, `F10E -22,969` | acquisitions less disposals in the summary used/scrap composite | signed flow; component/counterpart unresolved |
| C | five `Used` intermediate cells: `111CA -18`, `481 -302`, `483 -183`, `711AS -166`, `GFGD -60` | net sale/disposal by industry in the summary composite | signed flow; component/counterpart unresolved |
| D | `Other × F010 = -36,201` | composite noncomparable-import/ROW signed final-use reclassification | signed flow; component unresolved |
| E | four `511` intellectual-property import allocations: `F02N -28`, `F06N -1`, `F07N -1`, `F10N -3` | no admissible mechanism established | unresolved blocker |
| F | import intermediate `332 × 315AL = -3`; `3364OT × 5412OP = -2` | allocation/redefinition/rounding cause not identified | unresolved blocker |
| G | make `GFGN × 22 = -9` | negative current industry/commodity make not explained | unresolved blocker |

Thus the 129 negative source cells partition as 106 already mechanically
typed, 16 newly literature-supported signed cells, and seven unresolved
blockers. Twelve of the signed cells still lack the 2024 component/service
bridge: the 11 `Used` cells and the one `Other` cell. These classifications are
project inferences from exact source-row semantics plus documented sign
domains; BEA does not textually classify those individual coordinates.

The first overlay draft also used the use-table segment order for the one make
cell. The full build rejected the set partition. Its corrected canonical ID is
`AR24:PRODUCER_MAKE:GFGN:CORE:22`, and the fixture remains bound to source
`2024!H75`.

### Decision and next boundary

This checkpoint removes the narrow import-display ambiguity and reduces the
evidence-layer unresolved negative partition from 23 to seven. It does not
silently rewrite the earlier readiness report: that gate still probes the
underlying candidate ledger, where the 23 source types remain unresolved, and
must be explicitly integrated with this overlay in the next readiness
revision.

WS-2C remains in progress. The next admissible work is to:

1. integrate the admission overlay into a new fail-closed readiness contract;
2. resolve or explicitly exclude the seven remaining negative cells;
3. complete or scope out the recipient-level valuation/tax/margin bridge and
   select a behavioral domestic/import boundary;
4. materialize a revision panel and source-specific numerical reliability and
   dependence evidence;
5. independently approve the identity/control set and structural-zero policy;
   and only then
6. construct and run a production reconciliation solver.

This is stronger accounting evidence, not an accuracy result. The current
vintage remains ineligible as a historical forecast origin, and no claim about
the model’s forecasting suitability is made here.

## 2026-08-06 - WS-2C readiness v2: authenticated admission overlay and transitive fail-closed gate

### Outcome

The admission overlay is now integrated into a new versioned readiness
contract. The public readiness evaluator does not accept a caller-supplied
admission report. It authenticates the admission contract as the eleventh
direct readiness artifact and then rebuilds the complete admission report in
process from its 12 nested artifact bindings, implementation module, and
runner. The rebuilt `admission1:` identity, exact promotion-blocker set, and
full admission controls must match the sealed readiness-v2 expectations.

This changes one evidence criterion from absent to `PASS`; it does not convert
any scientific blocker into a solver admission:

The new passing criterion is
`production_admission_evidence_authenticated`. It means that the evidence
overlay is reproducible and correctly joined to the candidate ledger. It is
not a claim that its unresolved cells, display envelopes, domestic-use
sidecar, dependence groups, or revision receipts are solver-ready.

### Admission path-integrity correction and superseded checkpoint

An adversarial review found that the admission loader's original containment
check was lexical. A final-file symlink or a symlinked parent directory could
therefore point outside the intended repository while presenting matching
bytes. `safe_artifact_path` now:

1. canonicalizes the repository root;
2. rejects a final symbolic link;
3. requires a regular file;
4. resolves the candidate with `realpath`; and
5. rejects a resolved path outside the canonical root.

The admission suite now includes both a final-symlink attack and a
parent-directory escape. It passes 114/114 assertions.

This implementation-only hardening changes the admission trust hashes and
therefore **supersedes**, without deleting, the hashes recorded in the

### Public trust boundary and report integrity

The public evaluator now rejects a contract object loaded with
`verify_hash=false` unless its source SHA-256 is the approved sealed contract
hash. The lower-level unsealed evaluator is unexported and is referenced only
by adversarial tests that need to reach a specific downstream failure.

Further report hardening:

- direct artifact paths are unique, non-symlink regular files contained under
  the repository root;
- every direct artifact is rehashed after the in-process admission rebuild;
- a report target must be a fresh or empty non-symlink directory, preventing
  mixed reports and overwrite-through-symlink behavior;
- the manifest is written last as the completion marker;
- the source-family CSV now preserves all 25 registry fields, including
  namespace, country, valuation basis, cell-state policy, artifacts, and
  literature; and
- the blocker CSV preserves `required_for`, while tests assert an exact
  path/role/hash bijection for all manifest outputs.

Directory publication is manifest-last but not yet an atomic directory rename.
That is retained as a low-priority engineering hardening item. The normalized
module seal is drift detection bound into the repository contract; it is not
an external signature or independent authenticity authority.

parent-directory symlinks, admission-module mutation, semantic-probe attacks,

| `511 × F07N = -1` | import summary `2024!CL47` | -1 | same |
| `511 × F10N = -3` | import summary `2024!CP47` | -3 | same |
| `332 × 315AL = -3` | import summary `2024!W18` | -3 | authentic imputed import-matrix cell; detailed cause unresolved |
| `3364OT × 5412OP = -2` | import summary `2024!BC23` | -2 | same |
| `GFGN × 22 = -9` | make summary `2024!H75` | -9 | authentic negative make entry; mechanism unresolved |

This rules out the after-redefinition transformation itself as the cause. It
does not prove that a value is rounding, balancing, a return, disinvestment,
reexport, subsidy, negative physical production, or publication error.

The summary workbooks extend through 2024, but both detailed workbook pairs
contain only 2007, 2012, and 2017. Historical detail is informative but is not
a 2024 component bridge:

- the four 2017 `511` IPP summary cells reconstruct entirely from `511200
  Software publishers`, but that cannot establish the component of the
  negative 2024 values;
- `332 × 315AL` reconstructs as `+2` in 2017, whereas the 2024 summary is
  `-3`;
- `3364OT × 5412OP` reconstructs as zero in 2017; and
- 2017 `GFGN × 22 = +79` is entirely `S00600 × 221300`, whereas the 2024
  summary is `-9`.

The time series also argues against a magnitude-based repair: the four `511`
IPP cells turn negative together in 2015 and again in 2022–2024;
`3364OT × 5412OP` is `-2` in both 2023 and 2024; the other two cells change
sign only in 2024. Persistence or co-movement is evidence that the published
sign is deliberate, but it still does not identify the accounting mechanism.

#### What the methods support—and do not support

- The [BEA import-matrix FAQ](https://www.bea.gov/help/faq/453) and [BEA
  interactive I-O
  guide](https://www.bea.gov/resources/guide-interactive-industry-input-output-accounts-tables)
  establish that intermediate import-matrix cells are imputed allocations
  rather than directly observed industry-specific imports. They do not explain
  why any of these exact six allocations is negative.
- [BEA, *Concepts and Methods of the U.S. Input-Output Accounts*, chapter 12,
  printed pp. 12-5–12-7](https://www.bea.gov/sites/default/files/papers/WP2006-6.pdf)
  documents import-matrix construction; chapter 6, pp. 6-5–6-6 distinguishes
  scrap and existing goods; and chapter 7, pp. 7-9–7-11 documents
  noncomparable-import and rest-of-world treatments. These define possible
  accounting domains, not the mechanism of an unannotated cell.
- [SNA 2008, paragraphs 10.38–10.42 and
  14.101–14.109](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SNA2008.pdf)
  supports signed acquisitions less disposals and requires explicit
  counterpart and ownership-transfer-service treatment for existing goods. It
  supports the already recorded signed domain for `Used`; it does not identify
  a 2024 component, buyer, seller, asset, or service.
- The [BEA NIPA Handbook, chapter 7, printed pp.
  7-2–7-3](https://www.bea.gov/resources/methodologies/nipa-handbook/pdf/chapter-07.pdf)
  establishes that inventory change is an intrinsically signed flow. It
  supports the inventory cells already classified in the overlay, not any of
  the seven residual cells.
- The [UN SUT/IOT Handbook, sections 11.52–11.55, 11.104–11.120,
  18.23–18.40, and
  18.79–18.81](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SUT_IOT_HB_Final_Cover.pdf)
  requires classifications, valuation adjustments, balancing choices, and
  transformations to remain explicit and auditable. It supplies no
  cell-specific sign mechanism here.

For `Used`, the literature permits a negative signed flow from acquisitions
less disposals or a net sale of an existing asset. It does not justify
inferring used equipment versus scrap, dealer/transport/installation service,
seller, buyer, asset counterpart, or a behavioral state. For `Other`, the
documented noncomparable-import/rest-of-world composition permits a signed
closure composite, but not reinterpretation as ordinary production, imports,
final demand, or a behavioral model account without the 2024 component bridge.

#### Adopted best practice

The project will:

1. preserve the published value, sign, exact tuple, workbook hash, sheet,
   address, and vintage;
2. never take an absolute value, clip, coerce to zero, declare a structural
   zero, inherit a neighboring classification, or treat small magnitude as a
   rounding certificate;
3. keep unresolved cells outside solver likelihoods, calibration targets,
   reliability weights, covariance estimation, and behavioral-state mapping;
4. permit them in a published-accounting diagnostic only under an explicit
   unresolved label; and
5. label any zero/adjustment/unrestricted-flow sensitivity treatment as a
   counterfactual robustness case, never as promoted source evidence.

The descriptive provenance types
`PUBLISHED_SIGNED_IMPORT_MATRIX_VALUE__MECHANISM_UNRESOLVED` for the six
import cells and
`PUBLISHED_NEGATIVE_MAKE_VALUE__MECHANISM_UNRESOLVED` for `GFGN × 22` are
scientifically safe summaries, but they do not close the semantic blocker and
are not inserted into the authenticated overlay as economic classifications.

Promotion requires vintage-matched, cell-level evidence: an unrounded 2024
allocation or make worksheet; the source-program control and exact allocation,
redefinition, or balancing rule; pre/post values; the named adjustment and
accounting counterpart; evidence separating a genuine signed transaction from
rounding, residual balancing, suppression, or error; and a BEA note or agency
confirmation tying that mechanism to the exact cell.

The literature/source audit therefore changes no contract, partition, or
admission status. All seven remain authentic observations in the accounting
ledger and unresolved blockers outside the production solver.

### Decision and next boundary

The planned integration step is complete, but WS-2C is not. The seven residual
negative cells, 12 component-unresolved `Used`/`Other` cells, recipient-level
valuation/tax/margin bridge, behavioral import boundary, revision-derived
reliability model, numerical covariance model, structural-zero policy,
independent control approval, production solver admission, and vintage-clean
forecast-origin qualification remain open.

No production problem was materialized, no solver was run, and no current
vintage was treated as a pseudo-historical forecast origin. This checkpoint is
evidence-integrity progress, not a forecast-accuracy result.

## 2026-08-06 - Frozen statistical/semi-structural benchmark registry and hermetic origin adapter

### Outcome and boundary

The first executable benchmark checkpoint is complete. The project now has:

- tested naïve, iterated AR, VAR, BVAR, and compact semi-structural kernels;
- a fail-closed, hash-sealed registry with exact model, target-panel, window,
  density, fallback, and convergence records;
- a hermetic adapter from a synthetic `OriginData` fixture to forecast-registry
  v2 records; and
- canonical track vocabulary shared by the protocol, forecast registry, model
  registry, and adapter.

This is implementation evidence only. The model registry still declares
`empirical_forecast_execution_allowed = false` and
`production_scoring_allowed = false`. No historical or prospective origin was
run, no truth was opened, and no RMSE or density-score result was produced.

The audit made two substantive corrections before the checkpoint was recorded:

1. Because the output gap is a percent level while real-GDP growth is an
   annualized quarter-over-quarter rate, the semi-structural measurement
   equation is

   ```text
   real_gdp_growth[t]
       = potential_growth[t] + 4 * (gap[t] - gap[t-1]) + measurement_error[t].
   ```

   The initial implementation had omitted the factor four. Tests now bind the
   observation row to `[1, 4, -4]`.
2. The first registry seal referenced the registry README as the
   semi-structural model card. That would have allowed the actual scientific
   card to change without invalidating the model manifest. The registered
   artifact now binds `SEMI_STRUCTURAL_MODEL_CARD.md` itself, and a test proves
   that changing its artifact hash changes the semi-structural manifest.

### Canonical track vocabulary

The protocol uses `common_information` and `published_forecast`. The forecast

the protocol value nor a harmless alias because it could split an experiment
across two labels. `USForecastRegistry.jl` now accepts only the two canonical
values; `published_information` is rejected in the registry, model registry,
and origin adapter.

The published-forecast track remains a distinct future workstream. None of the

### Compact semi-structural v1

`SemiStructuralSpec` is an eight-state linear-Gaussian model with potential
growth, the output gap, natural unemployment, the neutral real rate, the
inflation anchor, inflation, the policy rate, and the lagged output gap. It
contains transparent IS, Phillips, Okun, Taylor-rule, and GDP-growth links.
The exact Kalman filter updates the latent-state distribution at an origin.
No coefficient or covariance is selected, fitted, or tuned there.

Predictive paths jointly sample the terminal filtered state and future process
and measurement shocks. They therefore form a coherent fixed-parameter,
conditional-on-hyperparameters posterior-state predictive density. Parameter
uncertainty is excluded.

The default model identity is:

```text
semi_structural_lgssm_v1_quarterly_core4_contract_v1_8dd9b5ddf4875de7cf44569dd3acaa5706bf19f8b34a1020b65afad1772b3715
```

Its final 64 characters are the SHA-256 of a versioned canonical parameter
payload. All forecast-relevant `Float64` values use exact IEEE-754 hexadecimal
tokens, covariance upper triangles are complete, and the observable contract
and annualization factor are included.

The structural form follows the small-model forecasting tradition described
in Berg, Karam, and Laxton,
[*Practical Model-Based Monetary Policy Analysis: A How-To
Guide*](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/wp/issues/2016/12/31/practical-model-based-monetary-policy-analysis-a-how-to-guide-18842),
and the IMF's
[*Canonical Quarterly Projection
Model*](https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/005/2026/003/article-A001-en.xml):
gaps and equilibrium concepts are latent, while aggregate demand, inflation,
and the policy rule are linked as a system. This supports the chosen
transparent state-space architecture; it does not validate the numerical
coefficients or turn the implementation into a DSGE model.

The [Bank of Canada real-time output-gap
study](https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2018/03/staff-working-paper-2018-10/)
reinforces the need to treat latent slack as a filtered, revision-sensitive
state rather than a known historical regressor.

The model is explicitly **not** a DSGE. The [New York Fed DSGE
description](https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/policy/dsge) identifies its
production model as a micro-founded, representative-agent,
rational-expectations system used for forecasting and policy analysis. This
v1 kernel has no optimizing-agent equilibrium solution or parameter posterior.
It also omits the planned fiscal and foreign-demand blocks, ELB mechanism,
regimes, stochastic volatility, and future exogenous conditioning. It is an
equilibrium-oriented low-cost challenger, not completion of WS-3C or of the
full compact specification in §III.7.

### Poledna-style reporting translation

The user-supplied Poledna, Miess, and Hommes paper,
[*Economic Forecasting with an Agent-Based
Model*](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.3484768), was reviewed as a reporting
reference. Its main forecast experiment:

- initially estimates models over 1997:Q1-2010:Q1;
- re-estimates each model every quarter over the 2010:Q2-2016:Q4 evaluation;
- uses common observable series;
- reports horizons 1, 2, 4, 8, and 12 quarters;
- shows an anchor model's RMSE level and competitors' percentage gain or loss
  relative to it; and
- averages the ABM over 500 Monte Carlo simulations.

Its DSGE appendix separately documents quarterly Bayesian re-estimation, 13
observables, a 250,000-draw Metropolis-Hastings run, calibrated and estimated
parameters, posterior summaries, variance decompositions, and VAR(1)
comparison tables. These features are useful templates for model cards,
convergence reporting, and horizon-by-target accuracy tables.

The U.S. report will preserve the useful table grammar:

1. target × horizon loss levels for a frozen reference;
2. percentage gain/loss for every challenger;
3. exact estimation and evaluation windows;
4. simulation/draw counts and failures; and
5. separate unconditional and conditional experiments.

It will not copy the paper's evidentiary limitations. The U.S. study must add:

- exact-as-of vintage-clean origin manifests and a separately frozen truth
  policy;
- balanced-sample and model-failure counts;
- MAE and RMSE plus CRPS, WIS, coverage, calibration, and joint density scores;
- forecast-comparison inference and multiplicity control;
- raw, postprocessed, and combined ABM variants shown separately; and
- regime, revision, structural-age, and pandemic/ELB robustness slices.

Poledna et al.'s conditional experiment uses realized paths for exports,
imports, and government consumption. That is an ex-post conditional
replication, not an ex-ante forecast. The U.S. quarterly-unconditional product
will never receive those realized paths. Scenario and ex-post replication
results require separately sealed assumption contracts and will never enter
the same ranking as the unconditional common-information experiment.

## 2026-08-06 - Direct multi-step AR extension and registry reseal

### Outcome and comparison design

The first benchmark-registry checkpoint above is superseded by a 15-model,
seven-artifact registry. Three direct multi-step univariate AR challengers are
now implemented alongside the three iterated AR challengers:

| Direct implementation | Selection rule |
|---|---|
| fixed AR(1) | one horizon-specific AR(1) equation per target and horizon |
| fixed AR(4) | one horizon-specific AR(4) equation per target and horizon |
| BIC AR(1:8) | select the lag separately for each target and horizon on a common candidate window |

For target \(j\), horizon \(h\), historical forecast origin \(t\), and lag
\(p\), the direct equation is

```text
y[t+h,j] = c[h,j] + sum(beta[h,j,l] * y[t+1-l,j], l=1:p) + e[t,h,j].
```

At the live origin \(T\), only target observations available through \(T\)
enter the regressors. Candidate BIC fits at a given horizon use identical
response dates, from the maximum candidate lag through \(T-h\). The selected
lag is then refitted on its complete eligible window. This avoids favoring a
longer candidate by comparing its BIC on a different sample while retaining
the training observations that become eligible after selection.

The comparison follows Marcellino, Stock, and Watson,
[*A comparison of direct and iterated multistep AR methods for forecasting
macroeconomic time series*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2005.07.020),
and Chevillon,
[*Direct Multi-Step Estimation and
Forecasting*](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-6419.2007.00518.x). The literature
supports treating direct and iterated forecasting as distinct, defensible
procedures whose ranking depends on specification and misspecification. It
does **not** support a prior claim that the direct method is more accurate.

### Coherent density and limitations

Separate direct equations do not form a recursive multivariate system. The
implemented density therefore aligns training residuals on common historical
forecast origins through \(T-H\), orders each vector by horizon then target,
estimates the full corrected covariance over the resulting \(H \times K\)
columns, and adds one joint zero-mean Gaussian draw to the entire point path.
This preserves estimated dependence across both horizons and targets.

Density construction fails visibly unless:

- aligned observations outnumber the \(H \times K\) joint dimensions;
- every direct OLS design is full rank with positive residual degrees of
  freedom;
- the centered aligned residual matrix has full column rank; and
- the resulting covariance is finite and positive definite.

A point-only forecast may still succeed when the joint density cannot be
estimated. The plug-in draws exclude coefficient, lag-selection, and
covariance-estimation uncertainty. The equations also exclude cross-target
lags, exogenous predictors, regularization, structural breaks, explicit
pandemic/ELB treatment, stochastic volatility, and heavy tails. Overlapping
multi-step residuals are not given a HAC-adjusted BIC. These are registered
limitations, not silent fallbacks.

### Registry trust-boundary correction

The direct source and its distinct model card are both sealed. The prior
semi-structural correction remains intact: the registry continues to bind the
actual `SEMI_STRUCTURAL_MODEL_CARD.md`, not a README.

An adversarial review also found that a correct artifact hash was not by itself
enough if a local path could be redirected. Artifact verification now:

- permits only one plain relative filename;
- rejects a final symbolic link;
- rejects directories and other non-regular paths;
- resolves both the registry directory and artifact; and
- requires the resolved artifact to remain directly inside the resolved
  registry directory.

The validator is still a local integrity boundary, not remote attestation or
an empirical-execution authorization. Both
`empirical_forecast_execution_allowed` and `production_scoring_allowed`
remain false.

## 2026-08-06 - Forecast-score kernel and adversarial numerical qualification

### Outcome and boundary

The first hermetic WS-3D mathematical score layer is implemented in
`scripts/us/forecasting/scoring/USForecastScores.jl`. It computes:

- mean error, RMSE, MAE, median absolute error, MASE, and relative skill;
- quantile and central-interval scores, weighted interval score (WIS),
  empirical-ensemble CRPS, coverage/width, empirical-PIT tie intervals, and
  Brier score; and
- energy and variogram scores for coherent multivariate draws.

This module does not read forecasts, origins, truth, registries, or source
data. It therefore cannot authorize an empirical evaluation and has produced
no U.S. forecast score. Balanced-sample construction, truth authentication,
score records, forecast-comparison inference, multiplicity control, and
Monte Carlo error remain later layers.

The definitions follow the proper-scoring-rule framework of Gneiting and
Raftery,
[*Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and
Estimation*](https://doi.org/10.1198/016214506000001437), and the calibration
framework of Gneiting, Balabdaoui, and Raftery,
[*Probabilistic Forecasts, Calibration and
Sharpness*](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9868.2007.00587.x). WIS follows
Bracher et al.,
[*Evaluating epidemic forecasts in an interval
format*](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008618). The energy and
variogram implementations follow Gneiting et al.,
[*Assessing probabilistic forecasts of multivariate quantities, with an
application to ensemble predictions of surface
winds*](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11749-008-0114-x), and Scheuerer and Hamill,
[*Variogram-Based Proper Scoring Rules for Probabilistic Forecasts of
Multivariate Quantities*](https://doi.org/10.1175/MWR-D-14-00269.1).

MASE denominators are accepted only as positive origin-training quantities
and can be constructed with a seasonal-naïve scale. This implements the
scale-free comparison logic of Hyndman and Koehler,
[*Another look at measures of forecast
accuracy*](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijforecast.2006.03.001), but the
mathematical kernel cannot prove the caller supplied origin-eligible history.

CRPS and energy use the equal-weight empirical-distribution `M^2` definition,
not an unbiased finite-sample `U` statistic. Final comparisons must therefore
freeze equal draw counts and report Monte Carlo uncertainty. Log score remains
absent until a finite-ensemble density estimator, tail safeguard, and failure
policy are preregistered.

### Independent review and the 256-bit defect

The first overflow hardening used 256-bit `BigFloat` intermediates. Independent
adversarial review found that this avoided many overflows but was numerically
wrong over the full Float64 exponent range. Three literal examples failed:

```text
mean([floatmax, 3, -floatmax, 0])                -> 0 instead of 0.75
seasonal scale([-floatmax, 2, prevfloat(max), 0]) -> prevfloat(max) instead of max
one-interval extreme WIS                          -> prevfloat(max) instead of max
```

The problem was not a nonrepresentable output. Low-order terms were discarded
before later cancellation or rounding. Random 4,096-bit reference checks
found 129 point-score mismatches among 1,976 representable bundles, 68
MASE-bundle mismatches among 981, 46 seasonal-scale mismatches among 1,961,
and 14 WIS mismatches in an 8,374-case one-interval boundary sweep. The
256-bit version was blocked and never accepted as a checkpoint.

Every finite Float64 is an integer multiple of `2^-1074`. Even at Julia's
largest indexable vector length, an exact squared-error sum needs fewer than
4,262 significand bits and the WIS product sum fewer than 3,237. The accepted
implementation therefore uses fixed 4,608-bit intermediates for point
aggregation, seasonal scales, MASE division, and WIS before the final
Float64 conversion.

Post-fix independent 8,192-bit checks produced:

| Audit | Result |
|---|---:|
| representable random point bundles | 4,958/4,958 exact matches |
| representable random MASE bundles | 4,955/4,955 exact matches |
| representable random seasonal scales | 4,952/4,952 exact matches |
| point input-order permutations | 2,000/2,000 exact matches |
| seasonal input-order permutations | 1,989/1,989 exact matches |
| valid extreme random WIS cases | 5,000/5,000 exact matches |
| exhaustive one-interval WIS boundary cases | 8,374/8,374 exact matches |

All literal defects now pass. Representable boundary results remain finite,
while mathematically unrepresentable point, scale, and WIS outputs fail with
`DomainError`. Other kernels intentionally fail closed if a finite-input
Float64 intermediate overflows; that narrower contract is explicit in their
README.

Future inference will be a separate preregistered layer. The planned methods
remain the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold small-sample correction,
<https://doi.org/10.1016/S0169-2070(96)00719-4>, Giacomini and White's
conditional predictive-ability test,
<https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-0262.2006.00718.x>, and the Hansen-Lunde-Nason
model confidence set, <https://doi.org/10.3982/ECTA5771>. Listing those
methods here is not a claim that their validity conditions have been met.

### Verification and seals

## 2026-08-06 - Authenticated origin-data receipt and forecast-registry v3

### Exact sample ownership and provenance

The hermetic benchmark adapter no longer accepts a bare in-memory
`OriginData`. `USOriginDataReceipt.jl` validates and deep-copies the complete
sample, then seals:

- origin ID and key;
- typed, ordered training and forecast keys;
- target and predictor order;
- exact `Float64` bits of `y_train`, `x_train`, and `x_future`, including
  signed zero and exact exogenous absence;
- origin-manifest, protocol, model-registry, target-contract, and target-panel
  hashes; and
- a sorted unique set of source-artifact IDs and hashes.

The canonicalization is typed, length-prefixed, and big-endian rather than
Julia `Serialization`. Supported key types are deliberately closed:
fixed-width signed/unsigned integers, `String`, `Date`, and `DateTime`.
Boolean, floating, symbolic, arbitrary-precision, composite, and caller-defined
keys fail. Both the canonical sample and the whole receipt have
domain-separated SHA-256 identities.

The receipt is fixed to `synthetic_fixture_only` and
`empirical_execution_authorized = false`; those values are not caller
arguments. The focused fixture identities are:

```text
sample_sha256  = fdedf8ec447a3312f853d2533eef0d6bd1e52d4c6814c9a3d390b8caaa9ec6e8
receipt_sha256 = 4993f81d4f00b1c5388388921c0ce781bc211cc84f393399f9e5ef8af0bb4d90
```

Both public adapter paths require the concrete `AuthenticatedOriginData`
envelope. The adapter copies and revalidates it before execution, matches its
manifest/protocol/model/target bindings to the readiness and model handoffs,
executes only the validated copy, and revalidates after the injected runner
returns. Every success and structured-failure forecast carries
`origin_data_sample_sha256` and `origin_data_receipt_sha256`. The integrated
adapter fixture identities are:

```text

receipt_sha256 = 80e9d7f3f11156a50feec4da9a69e7abdef756352f42014afb26dd0ac9bf63c5
```

### Schema-version correction

Adding two mandatory fields to the already sealed forecast-record v2 schema
would have silently redefined archived evidence. The registry and forecast
record were therefore advanced to:

```text
beforeit-us-forecast-registry.v3
beforeit-us-forecast-record.v3
```

Truth and score records remain v2. V3 preserves the prospective and
retrospective-replay modes but requires both origin-data hashes on every
successful or failed forecast. A regression proves that a legacy v2 forecast
payload is rejected rather than reinterpreted. Existing v1/v2 archives must
remain immutable.

The receipt establishes exact byte ownership and declared provenance. It does
**not** prove that the named source artifacts semantically produced the
matrices. `map_benchmark_run` also cannot prove how an injected run was
computed. Empirical execution remains blocked until a trusted origin-data
builder emits a transformation receipt joining source bytes, series/line
selectors, transformations, keys, and matrix cells to these exact sample
bytes.

## 2026-08-06 - Literature-backed release-availability interval policy

### Research question and policy addition

The backfill audit repeatedly encountered official **actual release dates**
without an authenticated intraday publication time. The previous precision
rule rejected all date-only records. A literature and official-practice survey
was added to determine whether a conservative, explicit uncertainty interval
could be used without fabricating midnight availability.

Croushore and Stark's real-time-data work defines a vintage as the information
available at a particular past date and warns that evaluation on final revised
data can mislead. Their data construction required determining what was
actually available and excluding observations not known at the time:
[*A Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists: Does Data Vintage Matter for
Forecasting?*](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0) and the
[Philadelphia Fed working
paper](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/-/media/FRBP/Assets/working-papers/2000/wp00-6.pdf?sc_lang=en).
The [Philadelphia Fed RTDSM](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/real-time-data-set-for-macroeconomists)
describes its data as vintage snapshots, while
[ALFRED real-time periods](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/realtime_period.html)
record when information was known and the
[FRED vintage-date endpoint](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/series_vintagedates.html)
returns dates on which values changed or were released.

Those date systems support retrospective research but do not authenticate
first-public bytes or an intraday publication instant. The
[IMF SDDS Guide](https://dsbb.imf.org/content/pdfs/sddsguide.pdf) distinguishes
precise dates, date ranges, and "no later than" dates, encourages release
times, and defines public release as first availability on equal terms. A
[BEA release schedule](https://www.bea.gov/news/schedule) is useful planning
metadata and commonly gives exact times, but a planned calendar entry is still
different from evidence of the actual event.

The next-midnight rule below is therefore a conservative project
operationalization of bounded uncertainty, not a claim that the cited sources
mandate that formula.

### Accepted temporal claims

`USReleaseAvailability.jl` and its sealed policy accept only:

1. an evidenced exact actual-public UTC timestamp;
2. an official actual release date in a named source timezone; or
3. an inclusive official actual release-date range in a named source
   timezone.

For exact time evidence, the safe threshold is that exact instant. For local
dates `D_start:D_end`, with separately sealed boundary offsets:

```text
lower_utc     = local_midnight(D_start)   - start_offset
upper_utc     = local_midnight(D_end + 1) - end_offset
safe_not_before_utc = upper_utc
```

The possible-publication interval is half-open. Every same-local-day origin
fails; equality at the upper bound may pass **only the temporal gate**. The
implementation covers normal 24-hour dates, New York's 23/25-hour DST dates,
47/49-hour two-date ranges, leap day, and year rollover.

Schedules, planned dates, retrieval times/dates, unexplained vintage dates,
route-level claims, inferred times, unknown timezones, and unknown assertion
bases fail closed. Exact-time evidence is never coarsened to a date.

Every evidence object binds nonzero availability, release-byte, and vintage
hashes and locators. They must be pairwise distinct. Date claims additionally
bind separate timezone-rule evidence. Missing, uppercase, malformed, or zero
hashes fail. The evidence is strictly `retrospective_research`, and all results
hold these fields false:

```text
empirical_forecast_execution_allowed
production_scoring_allowed
origin_admission_authorized
inventory_mutation_authorized
```

Independent timestamp tokens and hash-manifest packages could strengthen an
upstream capture—see [RFC 3161](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc3161/) and
[RFC 8493](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc8493/)—but neither alone proves
public availability or semantic correctness.

### Adversarial correction and remaining blocker

The first validator separated release-byte from vintage evidence but allowed
the availability locator/hash to alias either. An independently rehashed
"availability = vintage" object therefore passed. The policy, validator, and
tests now require all three evidence roles to be pairwise distinct. Both alias
counterexamples fail, and a self-consistently restamped policy cannot disable
the rule because the canonical policy digest is pinned in the module.

One boundary remains intentionally open. The validator checks that a supplied
offset belongs to an allowlisted timezone and that a boundary transition is
`-60`, `0`, or `+60` minutes; it does not prove that `America/New_York`
actually used that offset on the asserted historical date. For example, a
caller can presently supply a fictitious January `-05:00 -> -04:00`
transition and a self-chosen nonzero timezone-evidence hash. This is acceptable
only because the module is standalone and cannot admit or run anything.

Before any real evidence record is connected to an origin workflow, a pinned
date-specific timezone semantic artifact must be added and actually verified:
timezone, source/TZDB version, local boundary dates, applicable offsets, and
artifact digest. Merely carrying an arbitrary 64-hex locator/hash is
insufficient.

### Verification and seals

The focused checked-bounds suite passes **172/172**. Separate source-registry
and backfill-plan guards pass 98/98 and 246/246, respectively. No inventory,
backfill plan, or origin package was mutated; strict retrospective origin
count remains zero.

| Artifact | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| canonical availability-policy content | `0ee6d287cd676d512886c86e614c621a62be804ed46e6bd6205d40a247d5b302` |
| `USReleaseAvailability.jl` | `59624c52343103b36a710778647005566035519eac1c43ddd693bcf8a9192b6d` |
| `test_release_availability.jl` | `af6f9aaf425fbcde42147e5983e2f0041cd0fd0ec1eb7648f429d46978182405` |
| `release_availability_policy.toml` | `57637dfa1909edba10329860c5b121f9a059f79cf3be275eccb5cd858a64bd12` |

The original blanket date-only rejection is not relaxed for origin admission.
The new policy only defines how a trusted date claim could pass an isolated
temporal check after the entire uncertain date has elapsed.

## 2026-08-06 - Equilibrium-benchmark feasibility and implementation decision

### Public implementation survey

The equilibrium benchmark must be a genuine solved, estimated DSGE—not the
existing compact semi-structural challenger under a stronger label. The
primary public candidate remains the
[New York Fed `DSGE.jl` repository](https://github.com/FRBNY-DSGE/DSGE.jl)
and its Model1002 implementation. The New York Fed describes the package as an
implementation of its DSGE model and a framework for estimating user-specified
DSGE models. Its model-based forecasting method is documented in
[*DSGE Model-Based Forecasting*](https://www.newyorkfed.org/medialibrary/media/research/staff_reports/sr554.pdf).

The initial release-parity candidate was pinned to:

```text
tag:    v1.3.0
commit: 45c26624ec225d6d355219cde71638f6171694ad
model:  Model1002
example subspec: ss10
```

The tag's `Project.toml` SHA-256 is
`b60d28de48c60a5358640774ff6d87591a1e1e7954df493f62083831ca277f69`.
Its `run_default.jl` is
`b17bac77147ca6f1fcd3b75614cdf9da8677628e289d1f0587d53bc273a1ce07`,
and its Model1002 observable mapping is
`f930274b8dacb5d98801b66116904159a629f0b5551f5f076dd3127797707af1`.

The observable mapping is materially broader than the Tier-1 forecast panel:
GDP, hours, labor share, wages, GDP-deflator inflation, core PCE inflation,
the nominal policy rate, consumption, investment, credit spread, long-run
inflation, long rate, TFP, and GDI appear in the source, subject to exact
subspec settings. Every active measurement equation and transformation must
be frozen; no missing series may be silently dropped.

### Clean-environment probes and deviation

The plan originally anticipated freezing a public implementation directly.
A clean, separate Julia 1.10.3 depot proved that v1.3.0 cannot resolve:

```text
DSGE v1.3.0 requires JLD2 0.1.3-0.3.3
Julia 1.10 compatibility leaves JLD2 0.4.28-0.6.5
result: unsatisfiable requirements
```

No project dependency was changed to force a resolution. The current upstream
main commit was also pinned for a feasibility check:

```text
c09dfe881f8809f65b8c0f08a761ec6cc456a6fb
```

It also fails a clean Julia 1.10 resolution through incompatible
ModelConstructors/DataFrames/SortingAlgorithms constraints. More importantly,
the upstream state is internally transitional: its README says main moved to
Julia 1.12 on 2026-07-23, while the same commit's CI still calls Julia 1.5 the
supported version and allows Julia 1.12 to fail. An untagged transitional
commit is not promoted merely because some constraints were widened.

The [v1.3.0 example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FRBNY-DSGE/DSGE.jl/45c26624ec225d6d355219cde71638f6171694ad/examples/run_default.jl)
instantiates `Model1002("ss10")`, warns that estimation takes two to three
hours, reduces Metropolis-Hastings to 100 steps only for a short example, and
states that not all model data are public. The
[repository README](https://github.com/FRBNY-DSGE/DSGE.jl/tree/v1.3.0)
also states that data-loading examples require a FRED API key. Live package
loaders and incomplete-column execution cannot satisfy this project's
authenticated common-information contract.

### Adopted path and promotion gates

The DSGE is **not** added to the 15-model benchmark registry. The adopted next
step is a separate hermetic compatibility and known-sample probe:

1. retain v1.3.0/commit `45c266...` as the release-parity candidate in a
   pinned legacy Julia 1.5 x64 container or equivalent sealed runtime;
2. preserve its license notice and freeze Julia, Project, Manifest, artifacts,
   depot, OS, architecture, BLAS, thread count, and source hashes;
3. reproduce a known Model1002/declared-subspec solve, likelihood/filter,
   posterior fixture, and multi-horizon predictive fixture before adapting
   data;
4. disable live FRED/data loaders and construct every observable from the
   project's authenticated origin-data builder;
5. separately investigate a maintained Julia 1.12-compatible upstream
   revision only after upstream tests and a clean resolution pass—never by
   silently relaxing dependencies; and
6. register a DSGE only after its source, exact subspec, observables,
   transforms, priors, estimation cadence, seeds, sampler, posterior draws,
   ELB/COVID treatment, conditioning policy, and visible failure rules are
   sealed.

Promotion additionally requires solution/stability and finite-likelihood
checks; independent-chain convergence diagnostics including R-hat, effective
sample size, acceptance/trace pathologies, and reproducibility; finite
posterior predictive draws; receipt-bound target × horizon outputs; and
explicit failed records for every nonconverged origin. A fixed 250,000-draw
paper-parity run may be a reproducibility experiment, not a substitute for
convergence evidence.

Two tracks remain non-interchangeable:

- a re-estimated `common_information` Model1002 run may eventually be ranked
  against the ABM/AR/VAR/BVAR only on the same authenticated origin; and
- archived New York Fed DSGE forecasts belong to `published_forecast`, with
  their own publication timestamps, concepts, and information set.

No equilibrium-model forecast, posterior, score, or accuracy comparison exists
at this checkpoint. The compatibility failure is a useful negative result: it
prevents an unverified package name from being presented as a validated DSGE
benchmark.

## 2026-08-06 - Historical-origin source survey and BLS source-use decision

### Literature rule retained

An independent source-by-source survey tested whether any historical date can
support the protocol's eight Tier-1 targets and all required structural
inputs. The answer is **no** under the current contract.

This conclusion follows the real-time-data distinction already adopted in the
protocol. Croushore and Stark construct dated information sets rather than
evaluating a forecast as if final revised observations had always been known:
[*A Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists: Does Data Vintage Matter for
Forecasting?*](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0). The
[Philadelphia Fed RTDSM](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/real-time-data-set-for-macroeconomists)
and its constructed
[first/second/third-release series](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/first-second-third)
are useful value cross-checks. Their snapshot dates do not authenticate an
intraday public-release instant or the byte identity of a source file.
Likewise, FRED/ALFRED
[`realtime_start`/`realtime_end`](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/realtime_period.html)
and [series observation vintages](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/series_observations.html)
are date-bounded real-time metadata, not proof of exact publication bytes.

The project therefore continues to distinguish:

```text
scheduled time
actual or embargo-stated release time
retrieved_at
vintage date/range
raw bytes and raw SHA-256
```

No one field may stand in for another.

### Candidate comparison and selected diagnostics

| Reference quarter | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| 2004Q1 | target-extraction/parser pilot only | Earliest practical post-2003 NIPA-layout macro slice; BEA and BLS release records are strong, but the later HMI8/Z.1 routes and other structural sequences are absent. The [BEA advance release](https://www.bea.gov/news/2004/gross-domestic-product-first-quarter-2004-advance-estimates) records the actual 2004-04-29 08:30 EDT embargo. |
| 2008Q3 | retain as coverage-gap probe | Economically important, but archive/layout risk and structural gaps make it a worse first end-to-end reconstruction. |
| 2019Q4 | **first broad reconstruction diagnostic** | Pre-pandemic, contemporary formats, after the approximate BEA HMI8 systematic-archive start and after Z.1 CSV availability. It is not an admitted forecast origin. |
| 2020Q1 | pandemic shock diagnostic | Useful only after the pre-pandemic parser path works; the [2020Q1 advance release](https://www.bea.gov/news/2020/gross-domestic-product-1st-quarter-2020-advance-estimate) records the shock-era event. |
| 2021Q2 | **pandemic/regime robustness diagnostic** | Later pandemic slice chosen to expose revision and regime sensitivity; it is not an admitted forecast origin. |

The survey proposed `2020-01-31T15:00:00Z` for 2019Q4 and
`2021-07-30T14:00:00Z` for 2021Q2 only as candidate one-business-day-after-
advance-GDP conventions. They are deliberately **not** stored as established
origin timestamps. Both pilots retain:

```text
evidence_class          = reconstructed_after_origin
origin_timestamp_status = NOT_ESTABLISHED
origin_timestamp_utc    = NOT_ESTABLISHED
admission_status        = CANNOT_RUN
runnable                = false
promotion_eligible      = false
```

`2019q4_reconstructed` was added as the sixth, sorted pilot in the sealed
historical-backfill plan. The existing 2021Q2 pilot purpose was narrowed to
pandemic/regime robustness. The plan's strict retrospective-origin count
remains zero.

### Source findings and global blockers

The official [BEA HMI7 discovery route](https://apps.bea.gov/histdata/core/data/Fea_DisplayChildrenC/?HistMainId=7&getFiles=false&getDirs=true)
is suitable for acquiring Section 1/2 release workbooks for nominal GDP, real
GDP, the GDP deflator, PCE prices, and core PCE prices. It does not remove the
need to freeze each workbook, validate each vintage-specific sheet/line/unit/
base-year mapping, and prove the event's availability.

The [BLS Employment Situation archive](https://www.bls.gov/bls/news-release/empsit.htm)
provides event-specific HTML/PDF releases for both unemployment and payroll
employment and explicitly warns that later releases may revise archived
values. The [CES vintage documentation](https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesvininfo.htm)
is a useful first-published-value cross-check. Neither route by itself proves
that today's server bytes are identical to the first state served at the
historical event.

The decisive target blocker remains the effective federal funds rate. The
[New York Fed reference-rate information](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates)
describes current approximate 09:00 ET publication and possible 14:30 ET
revisions, but this is not an event-by-event historical first-state archive.
The FOMC target rate is not substituted for the contracted EFFR observable,
and the 2016-03-01 methodology break remains explicit.

Structural blockers also remain: BEA HMI11 fixed assets, HMI8 industry/I-O,
the Federal Reserve [Z.1 historical archive](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/z1/release-dates.htm),
CPS structural controls, QCEW, Census SUSB, and USDA structural counts do not
yet have complete, registered, as-published byte and event-time chains. QCEW
is promising for later work because BLS publishes a
[release calendar](https://www.bls.gov/cew/release-calendar.htm), but BLS also
warns that QCEW downloads are revised and are
[not designed as a time series](https://www.bls.gov/cew/questions-and-answers.htm).

### BLS source-use policy resolved

The former `UNRESOLVED` source-use state on all four BLS routes was replaced
after reviewing two official policies on 2026-08-06:

- [BLS copyright information](https://www.bls.gov/opub/copyright-information.htm)
  says BLS publications are public domain except previously copyrighted
  photographs and illustrations, requests BLS citation, and prohibits
  unauthorized use of the registered BLS emblem.
- [BLS.gov developer terms](https://www.bls.gov/developers/termsOfService.htm)
  state that downloaded data have no end-use controls, require public-API
  access-date citation and the prescribed post-retrieval disclaimer, prohibit
  non-BLS logo use, and may change.

The plan now requires a fresh acquisition-time terms review, BLS/source/
access/release identifiers, file-specific third-party-image checks, no emblem
reuse, and the API access-date/disclaimer rules whenever the API is used. It
authorizes BLS byte acquisition under those constraints; it does not authorize
an origin or redistribution of excluded third-party material.

All four BLS source routes now carry:

```text
terms_review_status =
  REVIEWED_AS_OF_2026-08-06_RECHECK_BEFORE_ACQUISITION
redistribution_status =
  PUBLIC_DOMAIN_EXCEPT_PREVIOUSLY_COPYRIGHTED_PHOTOGRAPHS_AND_ILLUSTRATIONS_
  RECHECK_FILE_SPECIFIC_NOTICES
attribution_requirement =
  CITE_BLS_PRESERVE_SOURCE_ACCESS_AND_RELEASE_IDENTIFIERS_NO_EMBLEM
```

The sealed historical-plan content hash is

## 2026-08-06 - Date-specific timezone semantics close the interval-policy gap

### Superseding the provisional boundary

This section supersedes the “remaining blocker” in the earlier
release-availability entry. Date-only evidence no longer supplies its own UTC
offsets unchecked. Policy and evidence schemas are now v2 and bind a sealed
date-specific timezone artifact. For an evidenced local interval
`D_start:D_end`, the validator requires the exact artifact offset at local
midnight on `D_start` and at local midnight on `D_end + 1`. A fictitious
January daylight-saving transition therefore fails even if the evidence
object is internally rehashed.

The checked-in artifact covers `UTC`, `America/New_York`, and
`America/Chicago` from 1997-01-01 through a 2036-01-01 boundary sentinel. It
was generated from the primary
[IANA `tzdata2026c` archive](https://data.iana.org/time-zones/releases/tzdata2026c.tar.gz),
whose source SHA-256 is
`e4a178a4477f3d0ea77cc31828ff72aa38feff8d61aa13e7e99e142e9d902be4`.
IANA describes the database as the machine-readable history of local civil
time, UTC offsets, and daylight-saving rules on its
[Time Zone Database page](https://www.iana.org/time-zones).

Runtime validation does not consult the host timezone database. It accepts
only the sealed artifact identity and canonical digest:

```text
release-availability policy:
  6af185c5fa8be4404a064294a0053eec093ca1a59cbc29f1a0566ada3364de11
timezone semantic artifact:
  8ed940e6deb1a1aa0922369eb8b0ad327ecf52def3c37c7317f81b87afe7a174
```

All empirical-execution, production-scoring, origin-admission, and
inventory-mutation flags remain false. Passing this module establishes only a
conservative temporal threshold; it does not authenticate a release event,
raw bytes, or a complete historical information set.

### Independent reproducibility and adversarial review

An independent reviewer:

- verified the detached IANA source signature, including signing fingerprint
  `7E3792A9D8ACF7D633BC1588ED97E90E62AA7E34`;
- regenerated byte-identical artifacts with Python 3.9 and 3.12, the system
  `zic 2022g`, and `zic` built from the 2026c source;
- compared 42,735 allowlisted zone/date midnights and found no offset
  disagreement;
- passed 31 additional runtime adversarial probes; and
- found and closed two low-severity generator portability gaps.

The generator now verifies the upstream archive before extraction, rejects
POSIX and Windows absolute, drive-relative, UNC, rooted, and traversal paths,
rejects links and special members, and refuses to write an artifact whose
canonical digest differs from the module-sealed value. The Windows-path
hardening passed 13 additional cases under both Python versions. This protects
build reproducibility; it does not elevate regeneration into permission to
reseal the policy.

The checked-bounds Julia suite passes **540/540**, including legacy-v1
rejection, 2006/2007 U.S. DST-rule regressions, semantic boundary coverage,
tamper cases, and all fail-closed scope flags. The checked-in Python extraction

## 2026-08-06 - Trusted source-to-OriginData derivation seam

### Implemented boundary

`USTrustedOriginBuilder.jl` adds an isolated, synthetic-only seam between
source observations and the benchmark `OriginData` sample. Every output cell
must have exactly one derivation that binds:

```text
source artifact ID and SHA-256
source observation/series/period/vintage/value
output slot/key/column/value
transformation and operator ID/version
ordered input observation IDs and operator parameters
```

The v1 executable operator allowlist contains only exact `identity/v1` and
`weighted_sum/v1`. All artifacts, observations, derivations, output order, and
IEEE-754 values enter a typed, length-prefixed receipt hash. The built sample
also uses the existing authenticated-origin canonical sample hash, allowing a
future production integration to cross-bind the two receipts without changing
sample semantics.

The builder rejects output gaps and duplicates, unsupported operators,
nonfinite or non-`Float64` values, unknown or unused observations, artifact
hash aliases, period look-ahead, binding drift, and post-build sample or
receipt mutation. An independent adversarial review found one resealing path:
a manually constructed result could use an invalid `origin_id` because
`validate_built_origin_data` had not repeated the constructor's identifier
check. The validator now rechecks both `origin_id` and `origin_key`; the
self-consistently resealed counterexample fails. The focused suite passes
**24/24**, and the independent 13-case adversarial suite passes **13/13**.

This is not yet a production historical-data builder. The schema permanently
sets:

```text
evidence_class                    = synthetic_fixture_only
empirical_execution_authorized    = false
production_admission_authorized   = false
```

It performs no download, parser execution, release-availability proof,
target/truth validation, or scoring. The next extension must execute pinned
source parsers and audited target transformations against acquired,
availability-qualified bytes; merely supplying plausible cell values is not
enough.

## 2026-08-07 - First historical BLS byte capture proves a reissue, not a vintage

### Exact present-day capture

Direct command-line requests to the BLS archive returned HTTP 403, so the
official archive page was inspected through a normal browser session and its
exact PDF download was imported locally. This transport choice is recorded as
`LOCAL_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD_IMPORT`; it does not make the browser observation a
release timestamp.

The captured artifact is the official
[Employment Situation—December 2019 PDF](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_01102020.pdf)
linked from the
[BLS Employment Situation archive](https://www.bls.gov/bls/news-release/empsit.htm):

| Field | Captured value |
|---|---|
| reference period | 2019-12 |
| nominal historical release date | 2020-01-10 |
| present-day byte count | 356,586 |
| raw SHA-256 | `e9005e394f25ad62315817fcada7bfff102442290a995a13417f82f027ceb066` |
| content-addressed receipt self-hash | `efcea9fd2f2bc433b2b85e2467fc454c88c4714a77c99c4f8face1dd935db075` |
| receipt-file SHA-256 | `9c0aee2426914d64120b66556a516fc65e161501d0a6575a8e4d4a95b2a2e771` |

The raw PDF and receipt are stored below the ignored `data/us/raw` tree. They
are not checked into source control and were not added to the source-release
inventory.

### Decisive first-state finding

This exact PDF is **not** the January 10 first state. Page 1 says BLS reissued
the release on 2020-02-21 to correct table A-5. Its metadata reports:

```text
/CreationDate  D:20200106100753-05'00'
/ModDate       D:20200220142443-05'00'
document state REISSUED_CORRECTED_NOT_HISTORICAL_FIRST_STATE
```

The PDF's headline payroll change of +145 thousand and unemployment rate of
3.5 percent are retained only as hash-bound manual diagnostic annotations.
They are not parser outputs, origin observations, target transformations, or
score inputs. The correction reportedly affects a different table and leaves
the headline text unchanged, but that semantic fact cannot restore the lost
first-public byte identity required by the common-information contract.

This is a concrete counterexample to the tempting inference:

```text
historical-looking official URL
  != exact bytes first served at the historical event
```

It validates the literature-backed policy already adopted from Croushore and
Stark: a retrospective evaluation must reconstruct the information actually
available at the origin, not merely obtain a later official representation of
the same series. See
[*A Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists: Does Data Vintage Matter for
Forecasting?*](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0).

### Capture and source-use contract

`BLSEmploymentArchiveCapture.jl` accepts only the pinned URL/hash/byte identity
above through its public importer. It validates PDF boundaries and
content-addressed paths, records separate browser-observation and local-import
times, and refuses partial/writable/aliased/symlinked/tampered objects,
unexpected files, caller-overridden live identities or clocks, and
noncanonical receipt bytes. The raw object and receipt are immutable local
objects.

Every semantic and operational gate is hard-false:

```text
historical_first_state_verified
historical_availability_verified
origin_admissible
empirical_execution_allowed
inventory_mutation_authorized
redistribution_authorized
ready
```

The [BLS copyright policy](https://www.bls.gov/opub/copyright-information.htm)
and [BLS terms](https://www.bls.gov/developers/termsOfService.htm) were
re-reviewed on the 2026-08-07 capture date. The receipt preserves BLS
attribution, prohibits emblem reuse, records that no API was used, and leaves
redistribution false pending file-specific third-party-image review.

tested alternate live identities, fake host dates, writable objects,
