## 2026-08-07 - RTDSM selected as a research proxy; FRED/ALFRED gate retained

### Literature and source-use decision

The requested follow-up literature survey compared the two practical
real-time macro warehouses against direct release artifacts. The adopted
hierarchy is:

| Source | Permitted project role | Strict origin input? | Main limitation |
|---|---|---:|---|
| direct agency release artifact plus independently verified release event | primary source and truth ladder | yes, after all gates pass | surviving historical artifacts can be incomplete |
| Philadelphia Fed RTDSM | curated historical information-set proxy, value/revision cross-check | no | reconstructed and date/month-granular, not intraday first-byte evidence |
| FRED/ALFRED | manual inspection only pending written clearance | no | current service-use restrictions plus date/fallback provenance |
| current/latest values | descriptive revised-data diagnostic only | no | hindsight and a moving truth vintage |

The current [FRED service terms](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/legal/terms/)
apply to FRED, ALFRED, their API, and associated content. They require
attribution and preservation of source-specific rights, restrict caching,
archiving, redistribution, replication and non-API extraction, and broadly
prohibit use in connection with developing or training software and
machine-learning systems. The underlying BEA series being public domain does
not remove the service-level terms. The existing
`EXCLUDED_PENDING_WRITTEN_CLEARANCE` gate is therefore retained; no FRED or
ALFRED data are downloaded, cached, trained on, or added to the warehouse.

ALFRED also would not close the temporal evidence gap after clearance. Its
[help documentation](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/help) says observations
are typically added within one business day and explains that a release date
may fall back from a source date to a provider date and then to first FRED
availability. Its
[`realtime_start`/`realtime_end` model](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/realtime_period.html)
is valuable bitemporal metadata, but neither a validity date nor an ingestion
date proves intraday public availability or first-public bytes.

The Philadelphia Fed's
[online terms](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/about-us/privacy-notice)
allow website content for informational, educational, and research purposes,
while warning that some material can retain third-party copyright and
prohibiting logo or endorsement use. They do not grant a broad raw-data
redistribution license. The adopted RTDSM boundary is therefore:

```text
research capture to ignored content-addressed local storage      allowed
checked-in hashes, manifests and non-substitutive diagnostics     allowed
raw-workbook redistribution                                      not authorized
strict_origin_admissible                                         false
intraday_provenance                                              false
```

Terms must be re-reviewed at acquisition. Attribution, official page and
download URL, effective URL, retrieval clock, response headers, exact bytes
and hash must be retained. A later mutable file is a new retrieval artifact,
not an overwrite.

### Coverage and semantic limitations

The [RTDSM overview](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/real-time-data-set-for-macroeconomists)
describes the data as snapshots of the histories available on vintage dates,
updated at month-end. Its
[full-history index](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/real-time-data-set-full-time-series-history)
provides the following useful Tier-1 proxies:

| Protocol concept | RTDSM mnemonic | Current complete-vintage route | Important mapping caveat |
|---|---|---|---|
| real GDP | `ROUTPUT` | `ROUTPUTQvQd.xlsx` | GNP before the historical GDP transition; warm-up mapping must be dated |
| nominal GDP | `NOUTPUT` | `NOUTPUTQvQd.xlsx` | same GNP/GDP concept transition |
| GDP implicit price deflator | `P` | `PQvQd.xlsx` | `P` is the GDP chain-type price index from 1996 onward, not the implicit deflator; mandatory concept mismatch |
| PCE price index | `PCON` | `pconQvQd.xlsx` | constructed as `100*NCON/RCON`, not the direct chain-type PCE price index; mandatory concept mismatch |
| core PCE price index | `PCONX` | `PCONXQvQd.xlsx` | quarterly vintages begin 1996Q1 |
| unemployment rate | `RUC` | quarterly-vintage/monthly-observation workbook | curated mid-quarter information set |
| nonfarm payroll employment | `EMPLOY` | monthly-vintage/monthly-observation workbook | vintage day follows the BLS release, not a universal month date |

The [general RTDSM NIPA notes](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/-/media/FRBP/Assets/Surveys-And-Data/real-time-data/data-files/documentation/gen_doc_NIPA.pdf)
state that quarterly vintages represent information available around the
middle of February, May, August and November and generally include the latest
advance NIPA estimate. They are academically useful information-set proxies,
not proof of availability at a particular clock time.

The exact concept crosswalk also fails closed. RTDSM's
[specific `P` documentation](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/-/media/FRBP/Assets/Surveys-And-Data/real-time-data/data-files/P/specific_documentation_P.pdf)
states that `P` is the GDP chain-weighted price index beginning with the 1996
vintages; the older construction `100*NOUTPUT/ROUTPUT` does not make the
modern series an implicit deflator. BEA's
[table-numbering guide](https://www.bea.gov/index.php/help/faq/125)
distinguishes `.4` price-index tables from `.9` implicit-price-deflator
tables, and its
[implicit-deflator definition](https://www.bea.gov/help/faq/513)
is the ratio of current-dollar to chained-dollar GDP. Therefore `P` versus
HMI7 `T10109/A191RD` is `CONCEPT_MISMATCH`, never `SOURCE_CONFLICT`.
`PCON` versus the direct HMI7 chain-type PCE price row receives the same
classification because RTDSM constructs `PCON` as `100*NCON/RCON`. A derived
ratio can be checked against the HMI7 deflator within the rounding interval
implied by RTDSM's rounded nominal and real levels, but it cannot silently
replace the target series.

The updated
[first/second/third-release documentation](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/-/media/frbp/assets/surveys-and-data/real-time-data/data-files/documentation/documentation_first_second_third_release_values.pdf)
constructs release-specific series from the vintage matrix but does not infer
a release merely from its first, second or third appearance. Delays, skipped
or combined releases, government shutdowns, benchmark revisions and
unavailable values remain explicit. This supports the project's
missing-rather-than-guessed rule.

The methodological choice is consistent with
[Croushore and Stark (2001)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0),
[Stark and Croushore (2002)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0164-0704(02)00062-9),
[Koenig, Dolmas and Piger (2003)](https://doi.org/10.1162/003465303322369768),
[Aruoba (2008)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1538-4616.2008.00115.x),
[Jacobs and van Norden (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2010.04.010),
and [Croushore (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1257/jel.49.1.72): real-time
information sets and data revisions are part of the forecasting experiment,
not an incidental preprocessing choice.

### Truth ladder and dubious-category policy

The preregistered truth vocabulary is refined as follows:

```text
FIRST
  actual official advance-release artifact

THIRD_SCHEDULED
  actual official artifact for the scheduled third estimate

MATURE_60M
  latest official release available by a fixed 60-month cutoff
```

`MATURE_60M` is not called “final.” BEA's
[revision information](https://www.bea.gov/gdp-revision-information)
describes advance, second and third estimates at approximately 30, 60 and 90
days after quarter-end, followed by annual and comprehensive updates. A fixed
lag makes the estimand reproducible even though revision can continue.

Missing, delayed, skipped or combined estimates are not renumbered to fill a
slot. The planned warehouse uses explicit three-state availability and
evidence grade:

```text
availability_status =
  VERIFIED_AVAILABLE | VERIFIED_UNAVAILABLE | UNKNOWN

evidence_grade =
  SOURCE_EVENT | CURATED_RECONSTRUCTION | WAREHOUSE_FALLBACK | NONE

release_date_basis =
  SOURCE | PROVIDER | FIRST_SEEN | NOT_ESTABLISHED

anomaly_code =
  NONE | DELAYED | SKIPPED | COMBINED_RELEASE | SHUTDOWN |
  CONCEPT_CHANGE | CONCEPT_MISMATCH | SOURCE_CONFLICT | OTHER_DOCUMENTED
```

`OTHER_DOCUMENTED` requires an explanation and source citation. `UNKNOWN` is
not coerced to zero, unavailable or available; strict training/scoring
excludes it and reports the resulting attrition. `Used` remains a provenance
relation—an artifact or observation was used by a transformation—not an
availability or residual category. This follows the explicit provenance
approach in [W3C PROV-O](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/) and
[Data on the Web Best Practices](https://www.w3.org/TR/dwbp/).

### Implementation addition

The next acquisition slice is an **RTDSM research-diagnostic importer**, not
an origin builder. It will:

1. capture exact current workbooks only into ignored content-addressed
   storage with same-day terms review;
2. commit manifests and semantic fingerprints, not raw RTDSM workbooks;
3. reconstruct selected vintage columns and release-specific series with
   documented missingness;
4. cross-check the exact 2019Q4 and 2021Q2 BEA diagnostics, emitting
   `SOURCE_CONFLICT` for unexplained differences; and
5. keep every origin, empirical-execution, inventory, production, and
   readiness gate false.

Direct release artifacts remain the strict route. RTDSM can shorten the path
to research-grade benchmark diagnostics and revision analysis; it cannot
alone create the vintage-clean balanced sample required for an accuracy
claim.

## 2026-08-07 - First measured BEA cross-archive revision diagnostic

### Scope and evidence boundary

The exact 2019Q4 and 2021Q2 HMI7 semantic fingerprints are now joined by a
sealed revision-sensitivity diagnostic. It compares the common 1997Q1 through
2019Q4 histories for nominal GDP, real GDP, the GDP implicit price deflator,
the PCE price index, and the core PCE price index. Each target contains 92
level comparisons and 92 primary-transformation comparisons; 1996Q4 is used
only as lag support for the first transformation:

```text
annualized quarterly log change = 400 * ln(level_t / level_t-1)
revision = later archive observation - earlier archive observation
```

This is deliberately not called a standard within-definition revision
experiment. The later input is the
[2021Q2 advance release and annual update](https://www.bea.gov/news/2021/gross-domestic-product-second-quarter-2021-advance-estimate-and-annual-update),
whose revised history can incorporate annual-update source data, methods, and
seasonal factors. The artifact is therefore present-day sensitivity evidence,
not historical-availability evidence, first/third/mature truth, a forecast
origin, a score, or model-accuracy evidence. This separation follows the
real-time-data treatment of revisions as part of the evaluation estimand in
[Aruoba (2008)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1538-4616.2008.00115.x),
[Jacobs and van Norden (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2010.04.010),
and [Croushore (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1257/jel.49.1.72).

### Results

The relative-level RMSE is small but not zero, and the transformation effect
is large enough to matter when forecast models are separated by only a few
tenths of a percentage point. The figures below are descriptive revisions,
not forecast errors:

| Target | Relative-level RMSE (%) | Transform-revision RMSE (pp, annual rate) | Maximum absolute transform revision | 2019Q4 transform revision |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| nominal GDP | 0.213197 | 0.284100 | 1.406268 in 2018Q3 | -0.035879 |
| real GDP | 0.187916 | 0.282255 | 1.165380 in 2019Q2 | -0.186483 |
| GDP implicit price deflator | 0.081579 | 0.133376 | 0.443863 in 2018Q3 | +0.150665 |
| PCE price index | 0.132366 | 0.138785 | 0.389180 in 2008Q4 | +0.167027 |
| core PCE price index | 0.153917 | 0.156539 | 0.502852 in 2008Q4 | +0.028777 |

The practical addition to the scoring protocol is now evidence-backed:
forecast error against `FIRST`, `THIRD_SCHEDULED`, and `MATURE_60M` must be
reported separately, and the later-data revision component must never be
silently folded into model error. A ranking that changes across preregistered
truth vintages is a truth-sensitivity result, not robust model superiority.

### Reproducibility and hardening

All arithmetic uses 80-digit decimal precision with round-half-even. The
content-addressed artifact contains 460 complete level rows, 460 complete
transformation rows, hashes for all ten row vectors, and deterministic level,
relative-level, and transformation summaries. An independent non-importing
recalculation checked every row, vector hash, summary, comparison-profile
hash, and gate record; a separate 120-digit calculation agreed to roughly
`4e-77`.

The first independent review found that the original writer could replace a
dangling symlink or a destination created during an empty-target race. A
second adversarial pass found a narrower temporary-path swap between close
and link. Both were fixed before this entry: publication now retains and pins
the temporary descriptor, uses an atomic exclusive same-directory hard link,
verifies the linked inode and bytes, and validates the single-link destination
after cleanup. Regression cases cover dangling links, mismatched and
byte-identical destination races, and a swapped temporary source. The final
review found no remaining correctness, security, or reproducibility issue.

The final standard-library suite passes **26/26** on Python 3.12.1 and
**26/26** on Python 3.9.6. It is wired into the main test workflow and the
U.S. script command inventory.

At artifact, source, and target scope, all historical-first-state,

### Cross-source result and dubious-category treatment

The two selected RTDSM columns reproduce the three actually comparable BEA
targets:

- nominal and real GDP agree after converting BEA millions to billions and
  round-half-up to RTDSM's one-decimal source precision;
- core PCE agrees exactly at the published precision; and
- the BEA implicit GDP deflator falls within the closed rounding interval
  implied by RTDSM's rounded nominal and real GDP levels.

This is three direct comparisons plus one auxiliary derived-identity check,
supporting four of five targets by a direct or derived diagnostic. It is
**not** five direct comparisons. There are zero unexplained source conflicts.

The remaining two cases implement the literature-survey rule requested for
dubious categories. The Philadelphia Fed's
[`P` documentation](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/-/media/FRBP/Assets/Surveys-And-Data/real-time-data/data-files/P/specific_documentation_P.pdf)
says the modern series is a GDP chain-type price index, while
[BEA defines the implicit deflator](https://www.bea.gov/help/faq/513) as the
ratio of current-dollar to chained-dollar GDP. The Philadelphia Fed's
[`PCON` documentation](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/-/media/FRBP/Assets/Surveys-And-Data/real-time-data/data-files/PCON/specific_documentation_PCON.pdf)
says it is constructed as `100*NCON/RCON`, not the direct chain-type PCE
index. Both mappings therefore carry mandatory `CONCEPT_MISMATCH`, never
`SOURCE_CONFLICT` or an undocumented `Other`.

`Used` is encoded only as a provenance relation linking the two BEA
fingerprints to the selected semantic cross-check. It is not an availability,
quality, or residual bucket. `OTHER_DOCUMENTED` continues to require a reason,
source URL, and operator note. These choices follow
[W3C PROV-O](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/) and
[Data on the Web Best Practices](https://www.w3.org/TR/dwbp/), while the
separation of information sets, revisions, and evaluation truth follows
[Croushore and Stark (2001)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0),
[Koenig, Dolmas and Piger (2003)](https://doi.org/10.1162/003465303322369768),
[Aruoba (2008)](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1538-4616.2008.00115.x), and
[Croushore (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1257/jel.49.1.72).

## 2026-08-07 - Direct BEA 40-quarter archive route selected, with strict-origin boundary retained

### Read-only archive and literature survey

A delegated source audit tested whether the official BEA HMI7 archive can
scale beyond the two existing historical fingerprints. The answer is yes for
an **official retrospective research panel**, but no for a strict
point-in-time panel on the evidence currently available.

The 2026-08-07 read-only root response from the official
[BEA Data Archive](https://apps.bea.gov/histdata/) returned HTTP 200,
100,290 bytes, and transient SHA-256
`f818afb3d7c95e9a1534373a17fd479b53db569575083c41c3744d03ab988d3d`.
The response exposed 287 structurally recognized release directories, 97
reference quarters from 2002Q2 through 2026Q2, and 96 advance-family releases
from 2002Q3 through 2026Q2. The estimate-family inventory was 96
advance/first/initial, 94 second, and 95 third releases. Advance-family labels
are not uniform: the audit observed 67 `Advance`, 27 `1. Advance`, and two
`Initial` labels.

This metadata response has not yet been installed as a content-addressed
project artifact. The counts and transient hash are therefore discovery
evidence to be resealed by the acquisition implementation, not a new
registered source release.

### Selected evaluation window and rationale

The selected primary archive-snapshot window is **2011Q3--2021Q2**, the first
40 consecutive advance-family quarters for which a fixed 60-month mature
truth can also be constructed by August 2026. This is preferable to a recent
2016Q3--2026Q2 window because the recent block does not yet have a common
60-month truth horizon. The 2018Q4 government-shutdown `Initial` release is
retained with an irregular-release flag and must also be excluded in a
prespecified sensitivity run.

The panel must keep three truth definitions separate:

```text
FIRST
THIRD_SCHEDULED
MATURE_60M
```

This decision follows the real-time-data literature rather than treating
today's revised history as if it were known at every forecast origin.
[Croushore and Stark](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0)
construct dated information sets;
[Koenig, Dolmas, and Piger](https://doi.org/10.1162/003465303322369768)
show why the choice of data vintage and transformation matters;
[Aruoba](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1538-4616.2008.00115.x) documents that
revision behavior is not innocuous; and
[Fixler and Grimm](https://www.bea.gov/research/papers/2003/revisions-rationality-and-turning-points-gdp)
analyze GDP revisions and turning points. BEA itself explains that each
quarter receives advance, second, and third estimates as additional source
data arrive in its
[GDP explainer](https://www.bea.gov/resources/learning-center/what-to-know-gdp).

### Workbook coverage and semantic mapping

The selected 40-quarter window requires both legacy BIFF `.xls` and OOXML
`.xlsx` support. Metadata probes found `.xls` through the sampled 2017Q2
third release and `.xlsx` at the sampled 2017Q3 advance release. Sections 1
and 2 cover the five national-account targets in this window. Eight existing
mapping templates identify the major schema/base-year regimes, including the
December 2003, July 2009, July 2010, July 2013, October 2017, July 2018, and
September 2023 changes.

The stable economic identities are:

| Target | Table/line | Series code |
|---|---|---|
| nominal GDP | T10105 line 1 | `A191RC` |
| real GDP | T10106 line 1 | `A191RX` |
| GDP implicit deflator | T10109 line 1 | `A191RD` |
| PCE price index | T20304 line 1 | `DPCERG` |
| core PCE price index | T20304 line 25 | `DPCCRG` |

These identities are validation templates, not permission to infer an
uninspected workbook layout. Every release must still pass title, series-code,
concept, frequency, unit/base, physical-row, and quarter-column checks.
Growth and inflation will be calculated as
`400 * log(level[t] / level[t-1])` from adjacent levels in the **same**
workbook. Levels from different base-year regimes may never be joined.

### Why this is not strict release-time evidence

Present-day archive metadata reveal several counterexamples to an
availability shortcut:

- 2002Q3 workbooks have January 2017 `Last-Modified` values;
- a sampled 2017Q2 third-estimate archive is timestamped after its release
  event;
- for 2017Q3 advance GDP, Section 1 is dated October 27 but Section 2 is dated
  October 31, after the protocol's October 30 issue time;
- the official 2020Q1 advance release occurred April 29 while the archive
  folder is dated April 30; and
- shutdown releases use irregular labels and dates.

An official release page or Historical Comparisons PDF can authenticate the
event and terminal reported values. It does not prove that today's archived
workbook bytes existed before a historical issue time. Accordingly, the two
evidence classes remain distinct:

```text
OFFICIAL_BEA_HMI7_PRESENT_DAY_ARCHIVE_SNAPSHOT
STRICT_ORIGIN_AVAILABLE
```

The selected panel may use only the first class until contemporaneous hashes,
authenticated release-time captures, WARC records, or equivalent evidence
qualify the second. This is a deliberate deviation from the hoped-for strict
40-origin route, not a relaxation of the common-information-set contract.

### Implementation decision and remaining checks

The next bounded BEA slice will:

1. freeze all 40 quarters with official event time, estimate family,
   shutdown/update classification, HMI7 path/ID, and metadata identity;
2. acquire exact Section 1/2 pairs into quarantine with HTTPS-only,
   host-pinned, no-redirect, identity-encoding, size/content/magic checks and
   atomic pair publication;
3. use a pinned isolated BIFF parser for `.xls` and the generalized
   dependency-free OOXML parser for `.xlsx`;
4. emit a bitemporal long-form research panel containing release and issue
   timestamps, archive-snapshot class, target/reference period, source cell,
   unit/base, workbook hash, event-evidence hash, and availability class; and
5. require all `5 × 40` target-origin cells plus agreement with official
   Historical Comparisons PDFs and the BEA GDP--GDI vintage-history workbook
   for its covered GDP sentinels.

The discovery, mapping, capture, fingerprint, and revision-diagnostic suites
currently pass **489/489** checks. The existing generalized downloader is not
yet safe to reuse unchanged: its discovery layer permits redirects, its
acquisition layer is hard-coded to 2026Q2, and its parser handles OOXML plus
only two historical releases. No 40-quarter bytes were acquired in this
survey.

All admission, empirical-execution, promotion, and production gates remain
false. The registered source inventory remains byte-identical at
`110b4448db0b49e95cbc2fe1cf7019f6b877b3f391c6069a81c2e7c3c2a086ae`,
certified historical origins remain zero, and promotion-ready target coverage

## 2026-08-07 - EFFR vintage routes resolve value history but not common-panel admission

### Source and literature survey result

A delegated survey corrected two deliberately conservative assumptions in
the earlier source plan:

1. [ALFRED EFFR](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/series?seid=EFFR) preserves
   post-March-2016 value revisions by vintage date; and
2. pre-2016 historical EFFR states may be reconstructible from direct Federal
   Reserve Board H.15 issue PDFs enumerated through the
   [FRASER H.15 archive](https://fraser.stlouisfed.org/title/h15-selected-interest-rates-86).

Neither finding admits a forecast origin. ALFRED is date-level vintage
evidence rather than intraday or original-byte evidence, and its use remains
blocked pending a project-specific FRED/ALFRED terms and governance decision.
The H.15 route still needs exact issue-by-issue coverage, byte acquisition,
correction-state handling, and source parsing.

The resulting evidence hierarchy is:

| Period/use | Preferred source | Allowed evidence class now |
|---|---|---|
| current revised history | [New York Fed EFFR API](https://markets.newyorkfed.org/static/docs/markets-api.html) | current-state diagnostics |
| post-2016 origin-date values | ALFRED EFFR vintages | `DATE_LEVEL_VINTAGE`, governance blocked |
| pre-October-2016 historical states | direct Board H.15 issue PDFs located through FRASER | candidate exact event-file reconstruction |
| current cross-check | Board H.15 business-day series `H15/H15/RIFSPFF_N.B` | current cross-check only |
| future origins | prospective New York Fed 09:00 and 14:30 ET captures | strongest planned byte/time evidence |

This hierarchy follows common-information-set practice in
[Croushore and Stark (2001)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0),
[Stark and Croushore (2002)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0164-0704(02)00062-9),
and [Koenig, Dolmas, and Piger (2003)](https://doi.org/10.1162/003465303322369768).
[Anderson (2006)](https://files.stlouisfed.org/files/htdocs/publications/review/06/01/Anderson.pdf)
also motivates storing reproducible vintages rather than relying on a current
database view. Correction states, methodology changes, audit trails, and
record retention follow the governance logic in the
[IOSCO Principles for Financial Benchmarks](https://www.iosco.org/library/pubdocs/pdf/IOSCOPD415.pdf).

### Decisive revision probe and clean modern window

The bounded survey reproduced the known May 31, 2017 revision:

```text
ALFRED vintage 2017-06-01: 0.82
ALFRED vintage 2017-06-02: 0.83
current New York Fed API: 0.83, revision token "r"
```

This proves that ALFRED can recover distinct date-level values for at least
one documented EFFR revision. It does not prove the first intraday state. The
New York Fed says it normally publishes the prior business day's rate around
09:00 ET and posts qualifying same-day revisions around 14:30 ET, with later
extraordinary corrections still possible; see its
[EFFR description](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/effr)
and
[methodology/revision policy](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates).

A current-API probe through 2026-07-31 found 6,554 valid rows beginning
2000-07-03, 35 nonblank revision tokens, one post-break revised effective date,
and one reduced-volume footnote inside the clean candidate window. Exactly 40
complete post-break quarters run from **2016Q2 through 2026Q1**, with 61--65
published business-date observations per quarter.

March 1, 2016 is a concept break: the earlier rate used brokered trades and a
volume-weighted mean, while the current methodology uses FR 2420 transactions
and a volume-weighted median. The clean baseline therefore excludes mixed-
regime 2016Q1. A longer sample must carry a `CONCEPT_BREAK` flag and report
regime sensitivity.

### Pre-2016 H.15 route

The Federal Reserve Board's current Data Download Program is not a real-time
pre-revision archive. Its `.B` business-day series may be used only as a
current cross-check; `.D` contains calendar carries and must not be averaged
as if weekend values were native effective-date observations. See the
[Board H.15 release](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h15/) and
[Data Download help](https://www.federalreserve.gov/datadownload/help/).

FRASER enumerates weekly H.15 issues from 1966 into October 2016, and direct
Board PDFs remain available for many issue dates. Some are explicitly marked
“With Correction.” A defensible reconstruction must preserve ordinary and
corrected issues as separate states, select only the latest eligible issue at
each registered origin, require every completed-quarter business day, and use
FRASER OCR only for discovery—not as authoritative numeric evidence.

### Explicit treatment of dubious and unknown fields

The survey produced the following source-specific taxonomy. These labels
replace residual `Other`, implicit zero, or generic `Used` states:

| Raw/situation | Required classification |
|---|---|
| New York Fed raw `r` | `DOCUMENTED_REVISED_RAW_TOKEN_WITH_SCHEMA_MISMATCH` |
| footnote 1 | `DOCUMENTED_REDUCED_VOLUME` |
| footnote 2 | `DOCUMENTED_BROKER_CONTINGENCY` |
| footnote 3 | `DOCUMENTED_PRIOR_DAY_REPUBLICATION` |
| blank volume in a rate-only query | `NOT_REQUESTED_IN_THIS_REPORT_TYPE` |
| unsupported blank | `UNKNOWN_NOT_ZERO` |
| 2003-07-20 Sunday duplicate | `KNOWN_EXACT_DUPLICATE_ANOMALY` |
| current API row carrying `r` | `CURRENT_STATE_WITH_REVISION_FLAG_NOT_VINTAGE` |
| ALFRED observation | `DATE_LEVEL_VINTAGE` |
| FRASER OCR | `OCR_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE` |
| pre/post 2016-03-01 | `CONCEPT_BREAK` |
| Board `.D` weekend | `CALENDAR_CARRY_NOT_NATIVE_EFFECTIVE_DATE` |
| unreconciled mismatch | `VINTAGE_OR_CONVENTION_MISMATCH` pending matched-context review |
| wholly blank trailing CSV record | `TRANSPORT_EMPTY_RECORD` |

`SOURCE_CONFLICT` is allowed only after date, regime, vintage, and calendar
convention have been matched. A bare `Used` token is invalid. A typed
source-usage relationship is provenance rather than a quality flag, while
BEA's native `Used` accounting label remains a separate source concept. Any
source token otherwise mapped to `Other` must retain the raw token and carry a
source note, evidence reference, and adjudication status before it can enter a
transformation.

### Rights boundary and cross-window blocker

New York Fed use remains subject to its
[Terms of Use](https://www.newyorkfed.org/privacy/termsofuse), including
attribution, derivative labeling, non-endorsement, and non-disruptive access.
The Board says site information is generally public domain unless otherwise
indicated; Board attribution is required and seals/logos are excluded under
its [disclaimer](https://www.federalreserve.gov/disclaimer.htm).

ALFRED labels EFFR “Copyrighted: Citation Required,” and FRED requires API
access, attribution, and a non-endorsement notice while preserving third-party
rights. Until the
[FRED terms](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/legal/terms/) and
[API terms](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/terms_of_use.html) receive a
project-specific governance decision, ALFRED is classified
`TERMS_LOCAL_GOVERNANCE_BLOCKED_PENDING_REVIEW`.

There is now an explicit cross-window tradeoff. The BEA mature-truth window is
2011Q3--2021Q2; the clean post-break EFFR window is 2016Q2--2026Q1. A common
40-origin benchmark therefore requires either:

- verified pre-2016 H.15 reconstruction for the BEA window; or
- a later BEA window with a different, explicitly justified truth-maturity
  policy.

The overlap alone is not silently expanded or called a 40-origin panel. No
EFFR bytes, ALFRED vintages, H.15 issues, release events, or forecast origins
were registered by this survey. Source inventory identity, 0/8 promotion
coverage, and all empirical/production gates remain unchanged.

## 2026-08-07 - Registered semi-structural comparator scored on the revised-data core four

### Implemented comparison and scientific boundary

The registered fixed-parameter quarterly semi-structural state-space model is
now executable in a separate quarantined comparison against the ten existing
naive, AR, VAR, and BVAR models. It scores only the four targets native to the
semi-structural contract:

```text
real GDP growth
PCE price inflation
unemployment rate
effective federal funds rate
```

All eleven models use identical forecast cutoffs and realized
target/horizon/origin score cells. They do **not** use identical estimation
panels: the statistical models retain their registered eight-target panel,
while the semi-structural model retains its registered core-four panel. This
is therefore a native-input comparison, not an experiment that identifies the
effect of structural restrictions under common regressors.

The model carries potential growth, an output gap, natural unemployment, a
neutral real rate, an inflation anchor, inflation, the policy rate, and a
lagged output gap. Its fixed transition encodes IS, Phillips, Okun, and
Taylor-rule links, and an exact Kalman filter updates the latent state at each
origin. It is equilibrium-oriented but explicitly **not DSGE**: it has no
rational-expectations solution, microfoundation, parameter posterior,
origin-specific parameter fitting, regime switching, stochastic volatility,
or effective-lower-bound mechanism.

The run uses the existing current/revised mixed-vintage panel from 2000Q3
through 2025Q3, a 40-quarter minimum expanding window, and horizons 1, 2, 4,
8, and 12. It scores point forecasts only. The implementation can propagate
fixed-parameter state uncertainty, but this comparison consumes zero
predictive draws and contains no parameter uncertainty or density score.

### Deterministic descriptive result

The canonical one-thread run completed with:

```text
models                         11
comparison targets              4
forecast cells             12,452
model-origin diagnostics       671
score summaries                440
relative scores                440
weighted scores                 22
failures                         0
```

VAR(1) is the ratio anchor. Weighted values are macro-averages of 20
target-by-horizon cellwise ratios under equal target weights and the frozen
`0.30/0.25/0.20/0.15/0.10` horizon weights; they are not pooled-loss ratios.

| Track | Common observations h=1/2/4/8/12 | Semi RMSE ratio / rank | Semi MAE ratio / rank |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| all available | 61 / 60 / 58 / 54 / 50 | 0.7488895447345775 / 1 of 11 | 0.8856658629411573 / 2 of 11 |
| balanced h=12 | 50 / 50 / 50 / 50 / 50 | 0.7445969022111804 / 1 of 11 | 0.8730449475542831 / 2 of 11 |

AR(1) ranks second on weighted RMSE and first on weighted MAE on both tracks.
The semi-structural model has lower RMSE than VAR(1) in 19/20 all-available
cells and 20/20 balanced cells. The all-available exception is EFFR at h=1,
ratio `1.003388852007923`. Much of the aggregate gain comes from
unemployment, so first place on this macro-average is not uniform
target-by-target superiority.

The rank is first among the 11 models executed here, not all 15 registered
models. Seasonal naive and three direct-AR specifications remain unscored in
this diagnostic. VAR(1), the ratio anchor, is unstable at the 2010Q2 origin
(spectral radius `1.0342403057`, design condition number `8,747.39`); the
diagnostic exposes rather than filters that case. The semi-structural
coefficients/covariances are hash-bound, but that is reproducibility—not
literature or empirical validation of their numerical values.

These numbers are descriptive revised-data evidence. They are not
pseudo-real-time accuracy, production skill, an ABM result, a DSGE
comparison, paper parity, or proof that the semi-structural model is suitable
for forecasting.

- each of the 1,132 score cells contains exactly the same 11 models, actual,
  origin period, and target period;
- all 671 model-origin diagnostic keys are unique and training count equals
  origin index;
- semi-structural origins are contiguous from index 40 through 100;
- source inspection and future-row perturbation tests found no future-row
  leakage; and
- an independent aggregation from `forecast_cells.csv`, without importing
  the comparison module, reproduced every weighted value within
  `4.44e-16`.

The no-future-row result does not turn revised history into a real-time
information set. The panel itself still contains information revised after
historical origins.

### Material pandemic/regime sensitivity

The independent review performed an explicitly **post hoc, unregistered**
stress calculation excluding target realizations from 2020Q1 through 2021Q4.
It changed the semi-structural result to:

| Track | Observations h=1/2/4/8/12 | RMSE ratio / rank | MAE ratio / rank |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| all available | 53 / 52 / 50 / 46 / 42 | 0.9849208060 / 5 of 11 | 1.0546117447 / 7 of 11 |
| balanced h=12 | 42 / 42 / 42 / 42 / 42 | 0.9967595829 / 5 of 11 | 1.0647287406 / 7 of 11 |

Additional target-date partitions found ratio/rank
`1.0510079636 / 8` for RMSE and `1.1304875026 / 8` for MAE through 2019Q4,
versus `0.8939419676 / 1` and `0.9533515118 / 1` from 2022Q1 onward.

These slices were selected after the headline run, partition target dates
rather than rebuilding every origin/training regime, and contain no
HAC/bootstrap or multiplicity adjustment. They are audit warnings, not formal
alternative estimates and not a basis for sample selection. They demonstrate
that the headline first-place RMSE rank is materially regime-sensitive.

The next comparison step must freeze a literature-grounded regime matrix,
score common-core4 VAR/BVAR variants, and add horizon-appropriate formal
inference and multiple-comparison control. Until then, all origin,
promotion, production, ABM, DSGE, and superiority gates remain false.

## 2026-08-07 - Formal-inference and regime-design literature freeze for the next experiment

### Scope and non-retroactivity

This section freezes the design for a **new** comparison experiment. It does
not retroactively turn the opened revised-data semi-structural diagnostic
above into a confirmatory study. Its rankings and pandemic partitions remain
descriptive and post hoc. The new experiment must bind this design, its model
set, loss families, seed, source identities, origin set, and truth policy in a
manifest before its score tables are opened.

The current `dmtest_modified` implementation was reviewed line by line. It
does compute a squared-loss Diebold-Mariano statistic with a Bartlett
long-run-variance estimate through lag `h - 1`, applies the
Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold finite-sample multiplier, and uses a Student
`t(n - 1)` reference distribution. It does not yet provide loss-difference
effect intervals, absolute-loss inference, block bootstrap, joint
multiplicity control, a nested-model dispatch, or regime-aware inference.
Those absences are now explicit implementation requirements, not silent
features of the current result.

The primary sources for the design are Diebold and Mariano's
[predictive-accuracy test](https://doi.org/10.1080/07350015.1995.10524599),
Harvey, Leybourne, and Newbold's
[small-sample correction](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0169-2070(96)00719-4),
and Newey and West's
[positive-semidefinite HAC estimator](https://doi.org/10.2307/1913610).
Because overlapping multi-step errors and the small evaluation sample make
asymptotic reference distributions fragile, the design also uses the
Politis-Romano
[stationary bootstrap](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1994.10476870),
the Politis-White
[automatic block-length method](https://doi.org/10.1081/ETC-120028836),
and the Patton-Politis-White
[block-length correction](https://doi.org/10.1080/07474930802459016).

### Frozen loss differential, samples, and headline

For model \(m\), comparator \(b\), target \(v\), horizon \(h\), and eligible
forecast origin \(t\), the paired differential is frozen as

```text
d[t,m,b,v,h] = loss(error[t,m,v,h]) - loss(error[t,b,v,h])
```

Negative values favor model \(m\). Pairing must use the exact same forecast
origin, target date, truth value, target transformation, and availability
state. A result may not be created by combining separately aggregated RMSEs.
Every table must report the mean differential, a confidence interval, the
paired observation count, and the loss-ratio or relative-skill effect in
addition to a p-value.

The primary family is squared error on the complete headline sample, with
pandemic observations retained. Absolute error is a separately adjusted
secondary family. RMSE/MAE ratios and weighted ranks remain descriptive
effect summaries; inference operates on paired per-origin losses. The
small-sample HLN-DM test uses Bartlett HAC through `h - 1` as the transparent
reference analysis. The bootstrap analysis resamples the complete
origin-indexed vector of loss differentials jointly, preserving dependence
across models, targets, and horizons.

The bootstrap contract is:

- studentized stationary-block inference with 9,999 replicates and a frozen
  registry-derived seed;
- corrected Politis-White plug-in expected block length, with a lower bound
  of the forecast horizon;
- fixed block-length sensitivities of `h` and `2h`;
- no per-model or per-target reseeding; and
- visible failure when a series is too short, degenerate, non-finite, or has
  an unusable long-run variance.

The exact stationary-versus-moving-block primary choice remains an
implementation constant to be sealed before execution; it may not be chosen
after comparing p-values. If both are retained, one is primary and the other
is a labeled sensitivity.

### Multiplicity and nested comparisons

With ten challengers against the semi-structural model, four targets, and
five horizons, squared loss creates one frozen family of 200 hypotheses.
Romano and Wolf's
[stepdown max-statistic procedure](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-0262.2005.00615.x)
will control the familywise error rate at 5% using the same joint block
bootstrap. The 200 absolute-loss hypotheses form a separate family. No
unadjusted target-by-horizon star may be described as evidence of general
superiority.

A 90% Hansen-Lunde-Nason
[model confidence set](https://doi.org/10.3982/ECTA5771) is a secondary
within-cell summary. Twenty separately reported model-confidence sets do not
themselves control error across the 20 target-by-horizon cells. The primary
MCS and Giacomini-White
[conditional predictive-ability](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-0262.2006.00718.x)
analyses require a fixed rolling estimation window so that their loss
sequence has a defensible stable-rule interpretation. An expanding-window
MCS may be shown only as a labeled pseudo-MCS sensitivity. A
Giacomini-Rossi
[forecast-breakdown test](https://doi.org/10.1002/jae.1177) is deferred until
the common-information experiment has enough origins for its rolling local
windows.

Clark and West's
[nested-model adjustment](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2006.05.023) is
allowed only when the null is genuinely nested under the same target,
regressors, transformations, origin set, estimation window, and forecast
scheme. Potential eligible pairs are fixed AR(1) versus fixed AR(4), and
VAR(1) versus VAR(2) or VAR(3), after contract-level verification. It is not
valid here merely because one model is “simpler.” In particular it will not
be used for semi-structural versus VAR/BVAR, native-eight versus core-four
inputs, VAR versus BVAR, a lag-selected AR, or models fit under different
window rules.

### Frozen regime and information-set matrix

The following labels replace an informal “pandemic excluded” switch:

| ID | Index and rule | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `H0_FULL` | all eligible target dates and origins | sole headline |
| `PT_PRE` | target date at or before 2019Q4 | prespecified sensitivity |
| `PT_ACUTE` | target date 2020Q1--2021Q4 | prespecified sensitivity |
| `PT_POST` | target date at or after 2022Q1 | prespecified sensitivity |
| `PO_PRE/ACUTE/POST` | the same cuts applied to forecast-origin date | separate learning/information diagnostic |
| `NBER_2020` | target date in the NBER 2020Q1--2020Q2 recession | ex-post chronology annotation only |
| `WHO_EMERGENCY` | target date 2020Q1--2023Q2 | broader pandemic sensitivity |
| `ELB_ORIGIN` | FOMC target-range upper bound at the issue timestamp is at most 0.25% | policy-regime sensitivity |
| `POLICY_DIRECTION` | tightening, easing, or unchanged at the issue timestamp | policy-path sensitivity |
| `WIN_EXPANDING` | expanding window | headline estimation rule |
| `WIN_ROLL40/60` | fixed 40- or 60-quarter estimation window | stability and valid-rule sensitivity |
| `INFO_CORE4` | identical four-variable estimation information for semi, VAR, and BVAR | confirmatory mechanism comparison |
| `INFO_NATIVE` | each registered model's native input panel | secondary operational comparison |

The fixed 2020Q1--2021Q4 acute window is a study design convention, not an
official declaration of a pandemic endpoint. The NBER dates come from its
[Business Cycle Dating Committee](https://www.nber.org/research/business-cycle-dating)
and are ex-post labels, never information supplied to historical forecasts.
The WHO sensitivity follows the official
[end of the COVID-19 public-health emergency of international concern](https://www.who.int/news/item/05-05-2023-statement-on-the-fifteenth-meeting-of-the-international-health-regulations-%282005%29-emergency-committee-regarding-the-coronavirus-disease-%28covid-19%29-pandemic).
ELB and policy-direction states must be derived from timestamp-eligible
Federal Reserve decisions in the
[FOMC calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm),
not from a later reconstructed quarterly average.

Common-core-four VAR(1)--VAR(3) and BVAR(1) variants must therefore be
registered before the semi-structural restrictions can be credited for a
performance difference. Native-input models answer the operational question
“which complete registered system forecasts better?”; common-input models
answer the narrower mechanism question. Neither answer may be substituted for
the other.

The motivation for keeping the full sample primary and pandemic handling
explicit is Lenza and Primiceri's analysis of
[COVID-era macroeconomic outliers](https://doi.org/10.1002/jae.2895) and
Schorfheide and Song's
[real-time pandemic forecasting design](https://doi.org/10.21799/frbp.wp.2020.26).
Robust estimation, volatility breaks, observation down-weighting, or
pandemic dummies are new registered model variants with new IDs; they are not
quiet preprocessing changes to an existing model.

### Power and interpretation limits

The revised-data diagnostic has only 50 paired h=12 errors on its balanced
track—roughly four non-overlapping 12-quarter spans. The observed target-date
partitions have approximately 8 acute-pandemic observations, 15 post-2021
observations, and only 2 NBER-recession quarters; a post-period origin split
can leave as few as 3 h=12 forecast errors. HAC or bootstrap machinery cannot
manufacture information from these samples.

Formal superiority claims are therefore limited to the full sample unless an
exact-design Monte Carlo study, including overlap, estimation-window updates,
heteroskedasticity, and the registered missingness pattern, demonstrates
acceptable size and useful power for a regime-specific test. Small regime
tables otherwise report effect sizes, intervals where estimable, and counts
without accept/reject language. “Not significant” is not evidence of equal
accuracy, and rank one is not evidence of statistical superiority.

### Handling `Other`, `Used`, and unresolved states in inference

The frozen upstream design rule, not yet an implemented adjudication ledger at
this checkpoint, is that no unrecognized regime or availability token may be
coerced to a baseline. A bare `Used` token is invalid; a typed source-usage
relationship is provenance rather than a statistical regime, while BEA's
native `Used` accounting label remains a separate source concept. The planned
ledger retains unmapped raw values as
`REGIME_UNKNOWN_PENDING_ADJUDICATION`; they remain eligible for `H0_FULL` when
the underlying score cell is otherwise eligible, but are excluded from the
affected regime-specific contrast with an explicit count. A conflict between
official sources becomes `SOURCE_CONFLICT` only after timestamps, vintage,
concept, and calendar conventions have been reconciled. The sealed inference
geometry already rejects unresolved labels, but the upstream
retention/count/exclusion mechanism remains an implementation requirement.

### Visual audit against the Poledna reporting reference

The local Poledna, Miess, and Hommes paper was rendered and visually checked
at Section 3, Tables 2--4, and Appendix F.13 rather than relying only on text
extraction. The main experiment starts estimation in 1997Q1, evaluates
2010Q2--2016Q4, re-estimates each model quarterly, reports 1/2/4/8/12-quarter
horizons, prints an anchor model's absolute RMSE followed by percentage gains
or losses, and averages the ABM over 500 Monte Carlo simulations. Appendix
F.13 separately compares unconditional DSGE forecasts with VAR(1), and
conditional DSGE forecasts with VARX(1).

That is the table and disclosure grammar for the eventual U.S. report, not a
claim of replicated evidence. The Poledna conditional setup controls
exogenous paths and produces materially different outcomes; it must remain a
separate scenario/ex-post product. The U.S. headline remains
quarterly-unconditional and may use only information available at each
forecast issue timestamp.

No inferential result, new regime score, common-core-four model, origin,
truth record, or promotion evidence was created by this literature/design
freeze. Source inventory identity, 0/8 promotion coverage, and every
empirical, production, ABM, DSGE, and superiority gate remain unchanged.

## 2026-08-07 - Sealed 40-release BEA HMI7 metadata contract and independent audit

### Implemented exact release inventory

The previously surveyed 2011Q3--2021Q2 BEA window is now represented by an
offline, self-hashed metadata contract at
`scripts/us/forecasting/vintages/bea_nipa/advance_metadata_manifest/`.
It binds 40 consecutive earliest-complete quarterly GDP/Personal Income
release records to:

- the exact HMI7 directory ID, original-case internal archive path, label,
  and archive-folder date;
- the official event page, full-release PDF, release number, 08:30 New York
  embargo timestamp, and UTC conversion;
- the direct-child Section 1 and Section 2 workbook filenames;
- the `.xls`/`.xlsx` format transition;
- annual/comprehensive update classifications; and
- shutdown irregularities and archive-folder/event-date lags.

The manifest contains 39 Advance-family records and the 2018Q4
shutdown-related Initial estimate that replaced the cancelled Advance and
Second estimates. It contains 24 legacy `.xls` pairs through 2017Q2 and 16
`.xlsx` pairs beginning in 2017Q3. Update counts are 30 `none`, 3 annual
revision, 5 annual update, 1 comprehensive revision, and 1 comprehensive
update. There are 2 irregular releases and 15 nonzero archive-folder lags:
9 of one day, 4 of three days, and 2 of four days. The 2014Q3 archive path
preserves BEA's lowercase `q3`.

The official metadata anchors are the
[BEA HMI7 archive service](https://apps.bea.gov/histdata/core/data/Fea_DisplayChildrenC/?HistMainId=7&getFiles=false&getDirs=true)
and the
[BEA release sitemap](https://www.bea.gov/releases/sitemap.xml).

### Independent live source reproduction

### Post-validation mutability defect found and closed

The first independent code audit rejected the validator's return boundary
even though all 40 records were correct. `validate_manifest`,
`load_manifest`, and `manifest_artifact` returned the mutable parsed TOML
dictionary under the trusted digest. A caller could validate successfully,
then change a directory ID to `99999` while the returned `content_sha256`
still displayed the compiled pin. The public hash-stamping helper was also an
unnecessary footgun.

The accepted implementation now:

- returns only immutable nested named tuples and tuples;
- returns canonical content as immutable text rather than a byte vector;
- never exposes or aliases a raw `.manifest` dictionary;
- removes the hash-stamping helper from the module; and
- tests mutation of the caller's complete parsed TOML after validation.

A focused re-audit recursively scanned the trusted return graphs and found no
dictionary, vector, array, IO object, or byte buffer. Emptying every
caller-owned table/vector after validation did not alter the returned
artifact; tuple, row, contract, and canonical-content mutation attempts all
failed. No remaining safe-API bypass was found. Concurrent unsafe memory
mutation during a validation call is outside this contract.
