## 2026-08-07 - BLS 40-origin reconstruction survey and two-axis provenance decision

### Decision: separate economic vintage from byte provenance

A timeboxed independent source and literature audit found that a scalable
official BLS **reconstructed-value** panel is feasible, while an exact
retrospective **first-public-byte** panel is not supportable from BLS alone.
The BLS archive itself cautions that
[archived release data may have been revised later](https://www.bls.gov/bls/news-release/empsit.htm),
and the already captured December 2019 release proves that an event-looking
archive path can hold a later corrected artifact.

The BLS contract will therefore use two independent axes:

```text
economic_vintage_state
artifact_provenance_state
```

An official archive document can support an event-indexed reconstruction
without being the exact bytes first served at that event. “Official archive”
must never imply `FIRST_PUBLIC_BYTES_VERIFIED`. Conversely, lack of original
bytes does not require discarding a well-triangulated published value from a
research-only pseudo-real-time experiment. This is a documented addition to
the strict-byte plan and follows the real-time-data literature rather than
silently substituting revised-current series.

After its bytes, parser, cross-checks, and manifest are implemented, the
research track will be named:

```text
OFFICIAL_BLS_ARCHIVE_RECONSTRUCTED_VALUE_PANEL
```

It may become eligible for a separately labeled leakage-controlled
retrospective experiment. It cannot satisfy exact-byte provenance,
prospective capture, promotion, or production gates. No such panel or origin
was created by this survey.

### Exact 40-event candidate, 2015Q1--2024Q4

The official
[Employment Situation archive](https://www.bls.gov/bls/news-release/empsit.htm)
exposes same-stem HTML/PDF pairs of the form:

```text
https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_MMDDYYYY.htm
https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_MMDDYYYY.pdf
```

The reviewer opened every PDF for the 40 quarter-ending releases from 2015Q1
through 2024Q4. The exact date keys are:

```text
2015: 04032015 07022015 10022015 01082016
2016: 04012016 07082016 10072016 01062017
2017: 04072017 07072017 10062017 01052018
2018: 04062018 07062018 10052018 01042019
2019: 04052019 07052019 10042019 01102020
2020: 04032020 07022020 10022020 01082021
2021: 04022021 07022021 10082021 01072022
2022: 04012022 07082022 10072022 01062023
2023: 04072023 07072023 10062023 01052024
2024: 04052024 07052024 10042024 01102025
```

Each is the release date for the March, June, September, or December
reference month. Thus the January 10, 2025 document is the quarter-ending
release for 2024Q4. The event list is exact; surviving artifact state is a
separate question.

Each reviewed release states an 08:30 ET embargo. This will be stored as
`DOCUMENT_STATED_EMBARGO` and converted with `America/New_York` rules—normally
13:30Z for January events and 12:30Z for April/July/October events. It is a
documented not-before/scheduled-publication threshold, not proof of actual
first-byte delivery. Current retrieval time, `Last-Modified`, PDF creation or
modification time, archive-link date, and a current release calendar are all
forbidden substitutes for contemporaneous availability evidence.

### Reissue counterexample and treatment

The official
[December 2019 HTML](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_01102020.htm)
and
[PDF](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_01102020.pdf)
now state that BLS reissued the release on February 21, 2020 to correct Table
A-5 after incorrect population controls. They preserve the January 10, 2020
08:30 EST embargo text. The captured PDF is:

```text
bytes              356,586
SHA-256            e9005e394f25ad62315817fcada7bfff102442290a995a13417f82f027ceb066
PDF CreationDate   D:20200106100753-05'00'
PDF ModDate        D:20200220142443-05'00'
```

BLS says the correction affected veterans/nonveterans in A-5 and left the
text unaffected. That supports
`TARGET_SCOPE_STATED_UNAFFECTED` for headline unemployment/payroll, but
without the original bytes it cannot prove target-table equality
cryptographically. This event is classified
`REISSUED_CORRECTED`, retained in a disclosed sensitivity panel, and excluded
from a strict first-public-byte panel.

### Exact concepts and per-cell revision state

All monthly cells are preserved before quarterly transformation:

| Concept | Series/table | Required row and units |
|---|---|---|
| CPS unemployment | `LNS14000000`, Table A-1 | total age 16+, civilian unemployment rate, seasonally adjusted, percent |
| CES payroll | `CES0000000001`, Table B-1 | total nonfarm, all employees, seasonally adjusted level, thousands |

The payroll headline over-the-month change is not a substitute for the
seasonally adjusted level. At a normal quarter-ending release, reference
month `m` is the first preliminary CES estimate, `m-1` is second preliminary,
and `m-2` is the third/final sample-based estimate. Those states remain
attached to individual cells after quarterly aggregation.

HTML DOM is the primary semantic extractor; PDF is the official layout
artifact and independent extractor. Agreement is required on reference
month, USDL identifier, embargo, table and row, units, seasonal-adjustment
state, numeric cell, and preliminary marker. Era-specific layout profiles
must be registered. A schema mismatch is quarantined, never repaired with an
unscoped regular expression.

BLS's
[CES vintage-data documentation](https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesvininfo.htm)
says its tables contain every published value since the first preliminary
estimates for May 2003, index rows by Employment Situation release, index
columns by reference month, and expose first and third estimates. The
[vintage-file index](https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesvindata.htm),
[total-nonfarm workbook](https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesvin00.xlsx), and
[all-series archive](https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesvinall.zip) are
therefore the independent official value check for `CES0000000001`. A
workbook downloaded today is still a mutable provider reconstruction, not the
original release artifact; exact bytes, retrieval metadata, and hashes must
be captured before parsing.

The workbook's internal sheet structure was not inspected in this audit
because the spreadsheet dependency probe stalled. Only BLS's published
semantics are accepted at this checkpoint. Current flat files under
`download.bls.gov/pub/time.series` are revised-current series and are never
historical-origin vintages.

No analogous BLS CPS vintage matrix was found in the bounded survey.
Quarter-ending release tables provide the primary reconstructed unemployment
values; the Philadelphia Fed RTDSM unemployment vintage is an independent
research cross-check, not a replacement silently relabeled as BLS bytes.

### Revision mechanics that the model must retain

The BLS
[CES revision guidance](https://www.bls.gov/web/empsit/cesfaq.htm) states that
initial monthly estimates are revised in each of the next two months, then
reanchored through annual QCEW benchmarking. Seasonally adjusted CES
estimates are generally revisable for five years. BLS's explanatory article,
[*Why are there revisions to the jobs
numbers?*](https://www.bls.gov/opub/btn/volume-2/pdf/revisions-to-jobs-numbers.pdf),
explains that later estimates incorporate reports unavailable at the initial
release.

The
[CPS seasonal-adjustment methodology](https://www.bls.gov/cps/seasonal-adjustment-methodology.htm)
states that original sample estimates normally are not revised monthly, but
annual seasonal-factor estimation revises the previous five years.
Population-control changes can create permanent level shifts and are not
always backcast; the 2012 and 2022 control changes are explicit examples.

The economic-value vocabulary is therefore:

```text
FIRST_PRELIMINARY
SECOND_PRELIMINARY
THIRD_SAMPLE_BASED
ANNUAL_BENCHMARK_REVISED
ANNUAL_SA_REVISED
POPULATION_CONTROL_BREAK
UNKNOWN_REVISION_STATE
```

First-published target values are the primary real-time-perception estimand.
CES third-release and fixed-lag benchmark values are separate truth
sensitivities. CPS annual-SA-revised truth is allowed only when directly
reconstructed; a guessed 60-month mature CPS value is prohibited.

### Closed provenance and source-role taxonomy

The artifact-provenance enum is:

```text
FIRST_PUBLIC_BYTES_VERIFIED
OFFICIAL_ARCHIVE_RECONSTRUCTION
REISSUED_CORRECTED
UNKNOWN_FIRST_STATE
MISSING_ROUTE
SKIPPED_NOT_PUBLISHED
```

The source-role enum is:

```text
PRIMARY_VALUE_SOURCE
PRIMARY_ARTIFACT_EVIDENCE
CROSSCHECK_ONLY
NOT_USED
QUARANTINED
```

Bare `Used` and `Other` are not valid BLS source dispositions. They collide
with BEA commodity/accounting terms and erase the reason a source did or did
not enter a transformation. The archive supplies a real
`SKIPPED_NOT_PUBLISHED` case: BLS says the October 2025 Employment Situation
was not published because of the appropriations lapse. Missing is not zero
and is never imputed by copying an adjacent release.

Any unrecognized table row or flag retains its native text, code, sign,
coordinate, unit, seasonal-adjustment state, vintage, artifact hash, and
source locator. It becomes `UNKNOWN_REVISION_STATE` or `QUARANTINED` until
adjudicated; it is never mapped to BEA `Used`/`Other`, clipped, zeroed, or
assigned to an invented producer.

For clarity, the existing BEA accounting interpretation remains separate:
`Used` is scrap plus used/secondhand-goods transfers, while `Other` combines
noncomparable imports and a rest-of-world adjustment. Used-asset transfers,
dealer/transport/repair margins, imports, reclassifications, valuation
effects, byproducts, and unresolved discrepancies remain distinct typed
sidecars. The BEA
[industry-table crosswalk](https://apps.bea.gov/scb/issues/2018/08-august/pdf/0818-industry-tables.pdf),
[used-asset methods paper](https://www.bea.gov/sites/default/files/papers/WP2006-6.pdf),
and 2008
[System of National Accounts](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/nationalaccount/docs/SNA2008.pdf)
support that treatment.

### Acquisition contract and literature basis

The implementation sequence is frozen:

1. capture and hash the archive index;
2. bind paired HTML/PDF locators for all 40 keys;
3. capture each format separately with requested/effective URL, status,
   media type, headers, retrieval interval, exact bytes, and SHA-256;
4. parse release month, USDL ID, embargo, reissue/correction language, and
   PDF metadata;
5. independently extract A-1/B-1 and reconcile;
6. cross-check CES against the release-date row in the official vintage
   workbook;
7. require all three target months and preserve every cell's revision state
   before applying a registered monthly-to-quarterly rule; and
8. fail closed on duplicates, missing releases, future observations,
   SA/NSA or unit mismatches, layout drift, reissue ambiguity, and
   cross-source mismatch.

Nicholas Fett's BLS study,
[*Comparing with the original: a look at Current Employment Statistics
vintage data*](https://doi.org/10.21916/mlr.2015.12), explicitly motivates
vintage tables for analyses requiring estimates available at particular
points in time. The design also follows Croushore and Stark's
[real-time dataset](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0), Koenig,
Dolmas, and Piger's
[use and abuse of real-time data](https://doi.org/10.1162/003465303322369768),
Stark and Croushore's
[real-time forecasting study](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0164-0704(02)00062-9),
and Aruoba's finding that
[data revisions are not well behaved](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1538-4616.2008.00115.x).

The report must separate results by both truth vintage and artifact
provenance tier. Revised-current inputs may not be mixed into real-time
origins. At this checkpoint the route inventory exists only in this
literature/source survey: no 40-row BLS manifest, new archive bytes, parsed
cell, quarterly aggregate, origin, forecast, or accuracy score was created.
Source inventory SHA-256 remains
`110b4448db0b49e95cbc2fe1cf7019f6b877b3f391c6069a81c2e7c3c2a086ae`;
admitted origins remain zero and promotion coverage remains 0/8.

## 2026-08-07 - Hardened one-release BEA 40-route capture boundary

### Implemented boundary

`scripts/us/forecasting/vintages/bea_nipa/advance_capture/` now consumes the
compiled-pin validated 2011Q3--2021Q2 metadata artifact and derives all 80
exact Section 1/Section 2 direct URLs. It preserves component case, including
the exceptional lowercase `2014/q3` path. The public interfaces can seal one
release pair from supplied local response material or invoke a
caller-supplied fetcher for one pair after same-host-date review of the
[BEA data-use FAQ](https://www.bea.gov/index.php/help/faq/145).

There is no built-in `Downloads`/`HTTP` client, no bulk-capture entry point,
and no source-inventory mutation. This checkpoint did not invoke the
live-oriented function and acquired no BEA workbook or PDF byte.

For each supplied response, the v2 boundary requires:

- exact planned request headers, requested/effective official URL, HTTP 200,
  zero redirects, complete supplied headers, identity/absent content
  encoding, and exact `Content-Length` when present;
- 512--25,000,000 body bytes, bounded headers/URLs, ordered millisecond UTC
  timestamps, and two distinct raw hashes;
- a bounded OLE Compound File envelope for `.xls`, including alignment,
  directory/FAT, mini-FAT/DIFAT, and unique header FAT-sector checks; or
- a single-disk, non-ZIP64 `.xlsx` envelope with terminal EOCD, bounded
  advertised expansion, safe unique central names, matching local headers,
  and required `[Content_Types].xml`, `_rels/.rels`, and
  `xl/workbook.xml` entries.

These are transport/container-envelope checks. They do not decompress every
entry, validate CRCs, parse spreadsheets, identify worksheets, or establish
an economic concept. Content parsing, exact target mappings, and historical
availability remain separate gates.

The two objects and canonical receipt are installed under the receipt
self-hash with an exclusive atomic directory rename. The validator requires
the exact inventory, immutable permissions, no symlink, exactly one hard
link per file, exact bytes/hashes, the metadata semantic/file pins, pair
digest, structural envelope, and all false gates. Trusted returns contain
only immutable tuples/named tuples and scalar values.

### Audit correction: integrity is not authentication

The first implementation passed its 85-test hermetic suite, but independent
adversarial review rejected three claims/boundaries:

1. `200.0` and integer `1` could be coerced into integer HTTP status and
   Boolean header-completeness fields;
2. externally hard-linked receipt/object files still validated; and
3. a local-import receipt could be rewritten as a live-fetch receipt,
   self-rehashed, and accepted because an unkeyed self-hash authenticates
   neither the process nor the operator.

The audit also demonstrated that the original synthetic `.xlsx` fixture was
not a ZIP at all: it was an 800-byte array with ZIP magic and two plaintext
member-name substrings. Calling that `OOXML_ZIP` was a false positive.

The accepted v2 design:

- rejects coercive status/Boolean values;
- rejects receipt and object `nlink != 1`;
- replaces the fake fixtures with bounded structural OLE and ZIP envelopes;
- seals the 250,000,000-byte advertised uncompressed-size ceiling; and
- makes the epistemic limit explicit:

```text
source_mode_attested
terms_review_attested
attestation_authentication = UNAUTHENTICATED_LOCAL_PROCESS_ASSERTION
network_transport_verified = false
```

The self-hash provides deterministic integrity and content addressing only.
It is not a digital signature, keyed MAC, trusted timestamp, IAM assertion,
or proof that an injected function contacted the network. Rewriting and
rehashing a receipt can produce only another visibly unauthenticated local
assertion. It cannot set transport verification or any admission/readiness
gate true.

This distinction is essential to the real-time-data boundary: a reproducible
current archive observation is not evidence that the same bytes existed at a
historical forecast origin, consistent with
[Croushore and Stark](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0).

### Independent verification and source identities

The hardened checked-bounds, deprecation-error suite passes **99/99**.
Runic and `git diff --check` pass. An independent reviewer ran 10,000
randomized ZIP probes and 10,000 randomized OLE probes with no unexpected
exception or false acceptance, and reproduced rejection of traversal,
symlinked roots/bundles, collision symlinks, hard links, coercive types, fake
containers, verified-transport elevation, and gate elevation.

| Artifact | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `BEAHMI7AdvanceCapture.jl` | `6da4ad0bc4a458c05e6594448c23aea5c6ae3f25f743d74ae3507d27a8831339` |
| `test_bea_hmi7_advance_capture.jl` | `f6efcda3bc141b3ae0052ac74a6670b5c6cb7fcc2e4d11248238298febbf8a2e` |
| capture-boundary `README.md` | `6126cbf7b97bcb143a3c5079ac94c8b52d76c2d855a2bc77fc4cb446aff971b6` |

Read-only/single-link validation is a point-in-time local filesystem check,
not protection from a privileged concurrent owner or later permission
changes. Response-size enforcement also occurs after the injected caller has
materialized a byte vector, so any future in-module downloader needs its own
streaming transfer ceiling.

The test is wired into hermetic CI. Every historical-first-state,
historical-availability, strict-origin, inventory, empirical-execution,
promotion, production-scoring, and readiness gate remains false. The source
inventory remains
`110b4448db0b49e95cbc2fe1cf7019f6b877b3f391c6069a81c2e7c3c2a086ae`;
admitted origins remain zero and promotion coverage remains 0/8.

## 2026-08-07 - Exact-design inference-calibration protocol frozen

### Purpose and score firewall

The inference kernel still has no empirically validated primary block policy.
Before any new forecast loss is opened, its finite-sample size, coverage, and
power will be calibrated under a score-blind synthetic experiment. This
calibration evaluates `USForecastInference.jl`; it does not evaluate a
forecasting model.

No forecast error, loss, score, relative-skill estimate, rank, p-value, or
estimated covariance from the opened revised-data diagnostic may parameterize
a data-generating process, effect size, block length, missingness rule, or
selection criterion. The design follows the forecast-comparison issues in
[Diebold and Mariano](https://doi.org/10.1080/07350015.1995.10524599),
[Harvey, Leybourne, and Newbold](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0169-2070(96)00719-4),
and [West](https://doi.org/10.2307/2171956); the
[Politis--Romano stationary bootstrap](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1994.10476870);
and [Romano--Wolf stepdown control](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-0262.2005.00615.x).
Rolling-window cases follow
[Giacomini--White](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-0262.2006.00718.x);
instability stresses follow
[Giacomini--Rossi](https://doi.org/10.1002/jae.1177); pandemic variance
stresses are motivated by
[Lenza--Primiceri](https://doi.org/10.1002/jae.2895); and conditional
heteroskedastic cases are required by
[Gonçalves--Kilian](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2003.10.030).

### Rehearsal geometry and a newly visible joint-family constraint

Reading only origin/target identifiers, dates, and horizons from the current
diagnostic—not its forecasts, errors, losses, or scores—gives:

| Horizon | All-available paired origins | Origin range | Target range |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 61 | 2010Q2--2025Q2 | 2010Q3--2025Q3 |
| 2 | 60 | 2010Q2--2025Q1 | 2010Q4--2025Q3 |
| 4 | 58 | 2010Q2--2024Q3 | 2011Q2--2025Q3 |
| 8 | 54 | 2010Q2--2023Q3 | 2012Q2--2025Q3 |
| 12 | 50 | 2010Q2--2022Q3 | 2013Q2--2025Q3 |

The balanced track contains 50 origins, 2010Q2--2022Q3. Its origin-date
pre/acute/post partition is 39/8/3. Its target-date pre/acute/post counts by
horizon are:

```text
h=1   38 / 8 / 4
h=2   37 / 8 / 5
h=4   35 / 8 / 7
h=8   31 / 8 / 11
h=12  27 / 8 / 15
```

The current joint bootstrap requires a complete
`origin × hypothesis` matrix. It therefore cannot apply one valid shared
resample to the ragged `61/60/58/54/50` all-available family. A joint
200-hypothesis calculation must use the 50-row intersection, or wait for a
missingness-aware method with separately established validity.

The rolling-window rule also changes the evaluation geometry. With the
current 2000Q3 training start, rolling 60 would leave
`41/40/38/34/30` all-available origins and only 30 origins in the
horizon-balanced intersection. A rolling-60 result cannot be described as
matched to a 50-origin expanding/rolling-40 result unless eligible earlier
training history is admitted or all methods are restricted to the common 30
origins.

The new experiment must first seal a geometry artifact containing only
origin IDs/timestamps, target dates, horizon maturity, score-blind
model/target eligibility, estimation-window availability, and timestamped
regime labels. Its schema must reject forecast, truth, error, loss, score,
rank, p-value, and effect fields. The present geometry is a rehearsal, not a
historical-origin confirmation geometry.

### Frozen synthetic family and null generator

The synthetic joint family retains:

```text
10 model comparisons × 4 targets × 5 horizons = 200 hypotheses
targets: real GDP growth, PCE inflation, unemployment, EFFR
horizons: 1, 2, 4, 8, 12
```

Squared and absolute loss are separate families. One origin-index draw is
shared across all 200 hypotheses. The primary directional calibration uses
`alternative = :less` under the existing negative-favors-challenger
orientation. The future registry must still seal which concrete model is
challenger; signs may not be reversed after results are viewed.

The forecast-error null uses 11 exchangeable models: one common comparator
and ten challengers. Exchangeability makes expected squared- and
absolute-loss differentials exactly zero. Four target innovations use two
signed common factors:

| Target | Factor 1 | Factor 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| real GDP | 0.70 | 0.00 |
| PCE inflation | 0.40 | 0.40 |
| unemployment | -0.60 | 0.10 |
| EFFR | 0.30 | 0.50 |

The remaining independent loading is the positive value that makes each
target variance one. The outcome innovation for origin `t` and horizon `h`
is the normalized sum of the next `h` primitive innovations, producing the
analytical overlap correlation `(h-k)/h` at displacement `k<h`.

Model-estimation disturbances combine equal 0.5 loadings on global, target,
model, and idiosyncratic components. With initial estimation length 40, the
window average is scaled by `sqrt(40)/window_length`; forecast error is the
common outcome innovation plus `0.35*sqrt(h)` times that estimation
disturbance. Expanding, rolling-40, and rolling-60 windows are separate
registered designs. All future outcome innovations are disjoint from
estimation windows, and AR/GARCH primitives receive a 2,000-observation
burn-in. Both loss families must be constructed through the production
`loss_differential` function.

Mandatory stationary null designs are:

```text
N00_DIFF_IID       direct independent Gaussian differential
N01_FE_GAUSS_EXP   Gaussian forecast errors, overlap, expanding window
N02_FE_GAUSS_R40   same, rolling 40
N03_FE_GAUSS_R60   same, rolling 60
N04_FE_AR035_EXP   normalized AR(1), rho=0.35
N05_FE_T5_EXP      standardized Student-t5
N06_FE_GARCH_EXP   GARCH(1,1): omega=.05, alpha=.10, beta=.85
N07_FE_STRONG_EXP  AR(.35), 70% common-factor variance
```

Every mandatory design runs at complete `n=40` and `n=50`. Required boundary
stresses are stationary AR(0.75), an eight-quarter ninefold variance episode,
a permanent fourfold variance break, and a whole-sample-zero mean reversal.
A standardized Student-t3 squared-loss case is a negative control because
the required fourth moment does not exist; a finite software output cannot
make it scientifically eligible. Its absolute-loss version may be reported
only as a labeled boundary diagnostic.

### Missingness and strong-control designs

Missing values are never imputed. Calibration must cover complete data,
horizon-specific terminal maturity, a common four-origin outage, a
score-blind lagged-state mask, target-specific gaps, model-execution failure,
and forbidden outcome-dependent masking. Target-specific gaps abort the
joint family unless a global intersection was sealed in advance; a
model-origin failure aborts the primary family rather than deleting an
unfavorable cell. `Used` is never a missingness or regime state, and unknown
DGP/window/mask/policy values are fatal.

Power scales the selected challenger's estimation disturbance by
`q = 0.90, 0.75, 0.50`, leaving the comparator at one. This improves
expected loss without manufacturing a loss differential. False-null
patterns contain exactly 1, 5, 20, or 200 hypotheses:

```text
SINGLE   one target/model/horizon
TARGET5  one model × one target × five horizons
MODEL20  one model × four targets × five horizons
DENSE200 every hypothesis
```

Partial-null cases measure familywise error only among hypotheses that remain
true. This strong-control check is required; global-null size alone is
insufficient. No scientific smallest effect can be selected until a
score-blind SESOI is registered in training-sample or policy units. A general
superiority claim requires the lower 95% Monte Carlo power bound at that
SESOI to be at least 0.80.

### Candidate block policies and selection firewall

Screen the following joint-family designs:

```text
J01 FixedBlockLength(1),  :none
J02 FixedBlockLength(4),  :none
J03 FixedBlockLength(4),  :max_horizon  # effective 12
J04 FixedBlockLength(24), :none
```

The `FixedBlockLength(4)/:max_horizon` and
`FixedBlockLength(12)/:none` calculations must generate identical indices
and statistics at the same seed while retaining different policy metadata.
Horizon-specific 40-hypothesis sensitivity families may use `h` and `2h`;
they do not replace joint-family error control.

The corrected
[Politis--White selector](https://doi.org/10.1081/ETC-120028836) and
[Patton--Politis--White correction](https://doi.org/10.1080/07474930802459016)
remain excluded until independently implemented and reference-tested. A
univariate selector would also need a predeclared, literature-supported way
to reduce 200 column-specific lengths to one joint length; none is currently
frozen.

Screening discards a policy with a 99% FWER upper bound above 0.075 or any
numeric failure. Among survivors, minimize worst-case absolute size
distortion; within 0.002 choose higher worst-case power at `q=.75`; within
two power points choose the shorter block. The chosen policy is sealed before
independently seeded final validation. If final validation fails, the design
fails; screening is not reopened to choose a different winner.

### Replication counts, deterministic seeds, and gates

The master seed is:

```text
0x55534643414c4942  # ASCII USFCALIB
```

Outer and bootstrap seeds are domain-separated SHA-256 derivations over
stage, DGP, geometry, policy, and outer-replication ID. The DGP seed never
depends on block policy, enabling common random numbers. The bootstrap seed
never depends on model, target, horizon, or loss family. Shard scheduling
cannot change seed identity.

The stages are:

| Stage | Outer replications | Bootstrap draws | Scope |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| screening | 5,000 | 999 | four policies |
| final null validation | 20,000 | 9,999 | selected policy |
| power | 10,000 | 9,999 | baseline and worst passing DGPs |
| h/2h sensitivities | 5,000 | 9,999 | representative DGPs |

At a 5% rejection rate, 20,000 replications give Monte Carlo standard error
about 0.00154. All rejection, coverage, and power probabilities use exact
[Clopper--Pearson bounds](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/26.4.404).

At nominal 5%, a configuration is unsafe if its one-sided 99% FWER upper
bound exceeds 0.060. It is called well calibrated only if the full 99%
interval lies in `[0.040, 0.060]`; a lower result may be safe but must be
labeled conservative and evaluated for power. Additional gates require:

```text
99% lower bound on marginal 95% interval coverage >= 0.93
99% upper bound on strong FWER among true nulls <= 0.060
zero unhandled exceptions or accepted nonfinite results
100% typed rejection of forbidden missingness/unknown states
bit-identical merged output under any shard order
```

Full-sample inference also requires the acute and permanent variance stresses
to pass. If no policy passes, the result is
`NO_PRIMARY_STATIONARY_BOOTSTRAP_POLICY`; thresholds may not be weakened.

### Implementation and feasibility boundary

The next hermetic artifact is a synthetic-only calibration package under
`scripts/us/forecasting/inference/calibration/`, containing a module,
self-hashed protocol, runner, and tests. It will generate errors, call the
production inference kernel, shard by immutable outer-replication IDs,
compute exact binomial bounds, and emit only hash-bound synthetic summaries.
Its input receipt must prove that no score artifact was read.

A local hot-path benchmark at `n=50`, 200 hypotheses measured about 0.31 s
for `B=999` bootstrap plus 0.10 s for Romano--Wolf, and 3.50 s plus 1.35 s at
`B=9,999`, with roughly 0.35--0.40 GB peak process memory. The core final
grid is approximately 1,000--1,100 CPU-hours; screening and power add roughly
700--900 CPU-hours. Deterministic process sharding makes this feasible, but
it is a multi-day compute experiment and will not be launched before the
geometry and policy artifact are accepted.

Exact origin dates/counts, rolling-60 prehistory, regime masks, truth vintage,
availability, common-core model IDs, direction, SESOI, and any external
selector remain blocked on the common-origin/model registry. This protocol
creates no loss input, p-value, forecast score, origin, promotion evidence,
or superiority claim.

## 2026-08-07 - Forecast-comparison inference kernel implemented and hardened

### Implemented statistical boundary

`scripts/us/forecasting/inference/USForecastInference.jl` now provides a
dependency-free kernel for the future pre-specified comparison experiment.
It implements:

- exactly paired squared- and absolute-loss differentials with the frozen
  sign convention `challenger loss - comparator loss`, so negative values
  favor the challenger;
- Bartlett HAC long-run variance through lag `h - 1`, the
  Harvey--Leybourne--Newbold small-sample correction, a two-sided Student
  `t(n - 1)` p-value, and an effect confidence interval;
- circular Politis--Romano stationary-bootstrap origin indices shared
  jointly across all hypotheses;
- null-centered, horizon-specific, studentized bootstrap statistics and
  equal-tailed marginal intervals; and
- Romano--Wolf stepdown max-t multiplicity control with two-sided,
  challenger-better, and comparator-better alternatives.

The implementation follows the already frozen primary sources:
[Diebold and Mariano](https://doi.org/10.1080/07350015.1995.10524599),
[Harvey, Leybourne, and Newbold](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0169-2070(96)00719-4),
[Newey and West](https://doi.org/10.2307/1913610),
[Politis and Romano](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.1994.10476870), and
[Romano and Wolf](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-0262.2005.00615.x).
It does not load score data, select a model, decide a regime, infer whether a
pair is nested, or turn the revised-data diagnostic into a confirmatory
experiment.

The primary experiment remains fixed at 9,999 bootstrap replicates.
Inference and Romano--Wolf intake reject fewer than 999; that lower number is
only an API/test resolution floor. Raw index generation can deliberately use
fewer draws because it emits no p-value or interval. Every result retains the
seed, complete joint index matrix, hypothesis horizons, requested and
effective block lengths, policy, and provenance.

### Block-length correction to the earlier design freeze

This section explicitly supersedes the earlier automatic requirement:

```text
corrected Politis-White plug-in expected block length,
with a lower bound of the forecast horizon
```

That lower bound is **not** now an automatic or default rule. In a small
exploratory null audit at `n = 50` with three correlated hypotheses and 499
bootstrap draws, a maximum-horizon floor was anti-conservative in the
examined designs: estimated familywise rejection rates at a nominal 10%
were 0.174 for an IID design with length 12 and 0.200 for an AR(0.35) design
with length 12, versus 0.086 for IID length 1 and 0.158 for AR(0.35) length
4. The number of outer Monte Carlo replications was not retained, so these
figures are a design warning rather than a publishable calibration result.
They cannot establish the size of the final experiment.

The kernel therefore has no block-floor default. Every call must select and
record exactly one of:

```text
horizon_floor_policy = :none
horizon_floor_policy = :max_horizon
```

The exact registered origin count, horizons, cross-hypothesis dependence,
window updates, missingness, and null data-generating processes must be
simulated before scores are opened. That calibration will select the
primary policy and label the other as a sensitivity. A fixed `h` or `2h`
length is also a sensitivity until calibrated; it is not promoted by this
implementation.

The kernel deliberately does not claim to implement the corrected
Politis--White/Patton--Politis--White selector. The
[original automatic selector](https://doi.org/10.1081/ETC-120028836) and its
[published correction](https://doi.org/10.1080/07474930802459016) require a
full separately tested contract. Current external plug-in intake accepts
only a positive numeric result, a nonempty method ID, and provenance in the
exact form `artifact-sha256:<64 lowercase hexadecimal characters>`.

### Independent adversarial audit and verification

The first independent review reproduced the HLN/Bartlett formulas against
external reference values, checked null centering and the Romano--Wolf
stepdown order, and found three hardening issues:

1. a one-replicate inference result could produce a zero-width interval;
2. Julia `Bool` values could enter numeric paths; and
3. silently applying a maximum-horizon block floor had no calibrated size
   justification.

The accepted version rejects `Bool` observations throughout, requires at
least 999 inference replicates, makes floor policy mandatory and visible,
and retains 9,999 as the primary design. A follow-up review found that the
exported result structs allowed manually reconstructed block metadata whose
source, method ID, and provenance were not revalidated at Romano--Wolf
intake. The validator now enforces source-specific invariants:

- `:fixed` requires method ID `fixed` and no provenance;
- `:external_plugin` requires a trimmed nonempty method ID and the exact
  lowercase artifact digest grammar; and
- any other source is rejected.

Six forged-metadata cases now fail. The final checked-bounds,
deprecation-error suite passes **166/166**, Runic 1.7.0 passes both Julia
files, and the final independent re-audit found no remaining safe-API
defect.

## 2026-08-07 - Common-origin-window literature decision and sealed contract

### Why nominal 40-observation panels are not interchangeable

A focused literature and official-source review was commissioned because
labels such as `Used`, `Other`, or a generic "historical" source cannot
identify the information set that a real-time forecast experiment requires.
The governing distinction follows Croushore and Stark,
[*A Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists*](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0),
and Koenig, Dolmas, and Piger,
[*The Use and Abuse of Real-Time Data in Economic Forecasting*](https://doi.org/10.1162/003465303322369768):
an observation date, a release date, a captured artifact, and the later
revised truth are different objects. Fett's
[*Comparing with the original*](https://doi.org/10.21916/mlr.2015.12)
provides a source-specific warning that reconstructed CES vintages also need
explicit vintage semantics.

The review froze three **metadata or candidate** windows, not three admitted
forecast panels:

| Source route | Frozen candidate range | Quarter labels |
|---|---:|---:|
| BEA HMI7 GDP-release metadata | 2011Q3--2021Q2 | 40 |
| BLS quarter-end Employment Situation metadata | 2015Q1--2024Q4 | 40 |
| clean post-concept-break EFFR candidate | 2016Q2--2026Q1 | 40 |

Their independently reproduced intersections are:

| Intersection | Range | Quarter labels |
|---|---:|---:|
| BEA and BLS | 2015Q1--2021Q2 | 26 |
| BEA and EFFR | 2016Q2--2021Q2 | 21 |
| BLS and EFFR | 2016Q2--2024Q4 | 35 |
| all three | 2016Q2--2021Q2 | **21** |

The strict admitted all-three intersection is nevertheless **zero**. The 21
common quarter labels do not establish 21 common-information-set origins:
the required first-public bytes, timestamped availability decisions, parsed
values, truth-policy decisions, and origin manifests have not all passed.

The current clean EFFR route can extend one quarter further, from 2016Q2
through 2026Q2, for 41 labels. To prevent sample selection after results are
seen, the decision freezes 2016Q2--2026Q1 as the fixed-40 research candidate
and records 2026Q2 as an adjacent evaluation reserve whose holdout integrity
is unverified. Because 2026Q2 was already public by the 2026-08-07 freeze, it
is not prospective; a genuinely prospective reserve begins with 2026Q3 or
later. This does not make either set empirical-ready. A uniform 60-quarter
mature-truth policy would
also be unavailable for 19 of the 40 later EFFR candidate quarters as of the
freeze, so a truth policy cannot be silently borrowed from the older BEA
window.

### EFFR concept, vintage, and terms boundary

The clean EFFR panel begins after the March 2016 methodology transition
documented by the
[New York Fed EFFR description](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/effr),
[New York Fed methodology and revision policy](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates),
and [Federal Reserve Board H.15](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h15/).
Pre-2016 H.15 observations are therefore a different-concept sensitivity,
not interchangeable extra sample size. The
[FRASER H.15 archive](https://fraser.stlouisfed.org/title/h15-selected-interest-rates-86)
can help locate historical issues, but OCR is not authoritative value
evidence. A candidate ALFRED route has date-level vintage semantics, but
local use remains governance-blocked pending review of the
[FRED terms](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/legal/terms/) and
[API terms](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/terms_of_use.html).

The contract consequently seals four non-interchangeable tracks:

1. `STRICT_FIRST_PUBLIC_BYTES` permits no empirical conclusion until exact
   artifact, availability, terms, truth, and origin gates pass.
2. `OFFICIAL_ARCHIVE_RECONSTRUCTION` may support a separately labeled
   experiment only after its own declared gates pass; archive reconstruction
   is not first-public-byte evidence.
3. `CURRENT_REVISED_PROXY` supports descriptive revised-data diagnostics
   only. Current New York Fed and Board histories do not recreate historical
   vintages.
4. `MIXED_CONCEPT_AND_PROVENANCE_SENSITIVITY` is a disclosed sensitivity
   only and must retain the EFFR `CONCEPT_BREAK`.

Bare `Used` and `Other` values fail closed across source, provenance,
concept, blocker, and decision fields. A genuinely unresolved state must be
typed as unknown with a stated blocker; an inadmissible source must be
quarantined. Neither may flow through a default branch into the strict or
headline track.

### Release irregularities remain typed, not hand-edited away

The review also retained five consequential irregularities:

- BEA 2018Q4 used an Initial estimate in place of Advance and Second;
- the BLS 2019Q4 release was reissued corrected, as documented in the
  [official archive copy](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_01102020.htm);
- the BLS 2025Q3 panel release was delayed by the federal lapse, consistent
  with the [BLS shutdown documentation](https://www.bls.gov/cps/methods/2025-federal-government-shutdown-impact-cps.htm)
  and [delayed release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_11202025.htm);
- the [BEA 2025Q3 Initial estimate](https://www.bea.gov/news/2025/gross-domestic-product-3rd-quarter-2025-initial-estimate-and-corporate-profits)
  replaced canceled Advance and Second estimates, with the schedule change
  described by [BEA](https://www.bea.gov/news/blog/2025-12-10/economic-release-schedule-updates);
  and
- BLS October 2025 was not collected or published, but it is a non-panel
  month and is not counted as a missing quarter-end event.

These types preserve the event history without implying admission. The
underlying route anchors remain the
[BEA HMI7 archive](https://apps.bea.gov/histdata/core/data/Fea_DisplayChildrenC/?HistMainId=7&getFiles=false&getDirs=true)
and [BLS Employment Situation archive](https://www.bls.gov/bls/news-release/empsit.htm).

## 2026-08-07 - EFFR vintage, revision, and capture literature survey

### Decision and correction to the holdout label

A separate official-source and academic survey examined whether the EFFR
candidate could supply the monetary-policy target in a defensible real-time
competition. The decision is to retain 2016Q2--2026Q1 as the 40-quarter clean
post-concept-break **research candidate**, while admitting **zero** strict
historical origins. The current official histories do not prove the exact
first-public response bytes or the state visible within a publication day.

The survey also corrected an overclaim in the first common-window contract.
At the 2026-08-07 freeze, 2026Q2 was already public and the route had already
been inspected through July 2026. It is therefore
`ADJACENT_2026Q2_EVALUATION_RESERVE`, with
`holdout_integrity = UNVERIFIED`, not a prospective holdout. A genuinely
prospective reserve starts with 2026Q3 or later. No 2026Q2 result may be
presented as untouched holdout evidence unless an independent audit proves
that it never influenced model, feature, hyperparameter, policy, or reporting
choices.

### Official publication and concept semantics

The [New York Fed EFFR page](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/effr)
states that the prior business day's rate is normally published around 09:00
ET. Its
[methodology and revision policy](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates)
allows a qualifying recalculation around 14:30 ET when the rate changes by
more than one basis point, normally on the same day, while retaining the
possibility of extraordinary later corrections. The rate is a
volume-weighted median of FR 2420 transactions; percentiles and transaction
volume are separate published measures. Reduced-volume, broker-data, and
prior-day-republication contingencies must remain typed states rather than
being coerced to ordinary observations.

March 1, 2016 is a substantive concept break. The
[Board's March 2016 H.15 notice](https://www.federalreserve.gov/Releases/H15/20160307/default.htm)
distinguishes the earlier broker-supplied, volume-weighted mean from the
FR-2420 transaction-level, volume-weighted median first included for March 1
on March 2. Thus 2016Q1 is mixed concept and 2016Q2 is the first complete
clean post-break quarter. A longer pre-2016 series cannot be appended to the
headline panel merely to increase sample size.

### Four evidence routes and their limits

1. `STRICT_FIRST_PUBLIC_BYTES` is retrospectively blocked. Only future,
   timestamped New York Fed captures that preserve the 09:00 state and any
   later correction state can satisfy this track.
2. `OFFICIAL_ARCHIVE_RECONSTRUCTION` may use ALFRED `EFFR` date-level
   vintages after 2016 or exact Board/FRASER issue bytes before 2016, but only
   as separately labeled research evidence after its own gates pass.
3. `CURRENT_REVISED_PROXY` may use the current New York Fed API with the
   Board's current business-day H.15 series as a reconciliation check. It is
   descriptive revised-current evidence only.
4. `MIXED_CONCEPT_AND_PROVENANCE_SENSITIVITY` may combine a pre-2016 H.15
   reconstruction with post-2016 EFFR only if the 2016-03-01 concept break is
   explicit and the result is excluded from headline evidence.

The [New York Fed Markets Data API documentation](https://markets.newyorkfed.org/static/docs/markets-api.html)
does not describe a historical-vintage archive and warns that production has
no parallel versioning; a current response has no historical publication
timestamp or earlier byte state. A bounded one-date schema probe for
2017-05-31 also exposed why raw-schema pinning is necessary: the live rate
report returned `percentRate = 0.83`, percentiles, target bounds, and
`revisionIndicator = "r"`; the volume report separately returned
`volumeInBillions = 79`. Those field names and the revision token differ from
the OpenAPI examples. The
[Board H.15 correction notice](https://www.federalreserve.gov/feeds/H15.html)
independently records that 0.82 was published on June 1 and corrected to 0.83
on June 2. A permissive parser that silently accepts either schema would
erase precisely the distinction this experiment needs.

The Board's
[Data Download Program help](https://www.federalreserve.gov/datadownload/help/)
describes its output as currently published and says real-time, pre-revision
data are unavailable. Current [H.15](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h15/)
is also later in the day than the primary New York Fed release. It is a
cross-check, not first-public evidence. Use the native business-day series,
not its seven-day calendar-carry distribution, when checking a quarterly
business-date mean.

[ALFRED help](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/help),
[download semantics](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/help/downloaddata), and the
[FRED observations API](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/fred/series_observations.html)
support vintage dates, real-time periods, and an initial-release output
mode. But ALFRED normally loads source changes within a business day, and
its release-date fallback can reflect a source date, provider date, or first
FRED availability. Its initial observation is therefore the first
**date-level state ALFRED recorded**, not proof of the New York Fed response
visible at 09:00 before a 14:30 correction. The candidate is
[ALFRED series `EFFR`](https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/series?seid=EFFR),
sourced from New York Fed Federal Funds Data, not Board `DFF`, whose
distribution convention differs.

The [FRASER H.15 archive](https://fraser.stlouisfed.org/title/h15-selected-interest-rates-86)
and direct Board issues such as the
[2015-09-21 release](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/h15/20150921/)
can reconstruct later official Board publication states before 2016. They
cannot recreate the earlier New York Fed first-public response. FRASER OCR
is discovery evidence only; numeric evidence requires exact PDF bytes,
page/table locators, issue-level coverage, and ordinary-versus-corrected
state handling.

These boundaries implement the information-set principles in Croushore and
Stark,
[*A Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists*](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0);
Stark and Croushore,
[*Forecasting with a Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists*](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0164-0704(02)00062-9);
Koenig, Dolmas, and Piger,
[*The Use and Abuse of Real-Time Data in Economic Forecasting*](https://doi.org/10.1162/003465303322369768);
and Orphanides,
[*Monetary Policy Rules Based on Real-Time Data*](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.91.4.964).
In particular, revised-current RMSE or MAE must not be allowed to stand in
for the policy information set that actually existed.

### Implementation-ready receipt and aggregation boundary

A future raw capture must bind at least:

- source authority, source and series IDs, evidence track, and concept regime;
- exact URL and canonical query, report type `rate` or `volume`, and the
  captured OpenAPI SHA-256;
- effective date, scheduled publication window, request start/completion UTC,
  and a conservative availability upper bound;
- HTTP status, final host/URL, redirects, content type/encoding/length, raw
  SHA-256, receipt SHA-256, durable-storage receipt, and predecessor or
  supersession hash;
- exact raw rate, percentile, target-bound, volume, footnote, and revision
  fields; and
- terms URL, terms snapshot hash/date, review decision, attribution and
  disclaimer requirements, redistribution scope, and a secret reference
  that never stores the API key.

Rate and volume may be joined only after effective date, report type, and
revision state agree. First state, same-day revision, later correction,
ALFRED date state, and current state are separate records and may never
overwrite one another.

Quarterly EFFR is computed locally as the equal-weight arithmetic mean of
native published EFFR business effective dates. Weekends are not inserted,
Board/FRED calendar carries are not averaged, and daily rates are not
volume-weighted a second time. The derived record must carry all input
hashes, first/last effective date, expected and observed counts,
completeness, aggregation version, selected-state rule, revision count, and
truth-as-of date.

Strict admission requires every expected effective date, resolved rate and
volume pairing, resolved footnote/revision state, exact bytes and pre-origin
availability, approved terms, pinned parser/schema, independent official
reconciliation, immutable origin manifest, and the clean post-2016 concept.
One false or unknown gate keeps the origin unadmitted.

Closed classifications include:

```text
blank revision token  -> NOT_REVISED_RAW_EMPTY_TOKEN
r                     -> DOCUMENTED_REVISED_RAW_TOKEN_WITH_SCHEMA_MISMATCH
footnote 1 / 2 / 3    -> REDUCED_VOLUME / BROKER_CONTINGENCY /
                         PRIOR_DAY_REPUBLICATION
rate-report volume    -> NOT_REQUESTED_IN_REPORT_TYPE
unsupported blank     -> UNKNOWN_NOT_ZERO
current API flag      -> CURRENT_STATE_FLAG_NOT_VINTAGE
ALFRED value          -> DATE_LEVEL_VINTAGE_NOT_INTRADAY
FRASER OCR            -> OCR_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE
pre/post boundary     -> CONCEPT_BREAK
duplicate/conflict    -> QUARANTINED_PENDING_MATCHED_STATE_REVIEW
```

Bare `Used`, `Other`, generic `historical`, or a default enum branch is
rejected in source, provenance, concept, quality, and decision fields. The
raw token, blocker, evidence locator, and adjudication state must be
preserved.

The [New York Fed terms](https://www.newyorkfed.org/privacy/termsofuse)
permit non-disruptive automated access subject to attribution, derivative
labeling, and reference-rate disclaimer obligations. The
[FRED terms](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/legal/terms/) and
[API terms](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/terms_of_use.html) require a
registered key, attribution/non-endorsement language, preservation of
third-party rights, and monitoring of mutable terms. These are governance
obligations requiring review, not automatic authorization.

No bulk panel, archive byte set, source-inventory row, origin, score, or
promotion evidence was created in this survey. The inventory pin remains
unchanged, admitted origins remain zero, and promotion coverage remains 0/8.

## 2026-08-07 - Synthetic exact-design inference-calibration contract accepted

### Implemented boundary

The synthetic-only preparation package is now implemented at
`scripts/us/forecasting/inference/calibration/`. It turns the previously
frozen design into executable, hermetic primitives without running the
multi-day calibration experiment. The accepted package provides:

- a compiled-pin, self-hashed protocol for the 200-hypothesis family,
  squared/absolute loss separation, J01--J04 block policies, DGPs, stage
  replication counts, thresholds, and permanently false scientific gates;
- a score-field firewall and geometry schema for origin quarters,
  horizon-relative target dates, model/target/window eligibility, and closed
  regime assertions;
- deterministic SHA-256 domain-separated DGP and joint-bootstrap seeds;
- expanding, rolling-40, and rolling-60 no-future estimation windows;
- the frozen exchangeable 11-model forecast-error generator and production
  loss-differential routing;
- typed, no-imputation missingness with an explicit minimum retained-origin
  requirement;
- exact 1/5/20/200 false-null masks and unambiguous
  `comparison1`--`comparison10` mappings from comparator position 1 to
  challenger positions 2--11;
- exact beta-inversion Clopper--Pearson bounds; and
- schedule-independent shard identities and deterministic merge validation.

Protocol v2 resolves an ambiguity in the earlier design text:
`N00_DIFF_IID` now means a matrix of fully independent standard-Gaussian
columns with theoretical cross-hypothesis correlation zero. The protocol
semantic pin is:

```text
c291c975bac7a419eb47d46841c79ec9eaf31399694ea4296078c3e884e61463
```

The calibration package still imports only the production inference kernel.
It does not import the revised-data diagnostic or read forecasts, truths,
errors, losses, scores, ranks, p-values, or effects.

### Why the first passing suite was rejected

The initial implementation passed 284/284 unit tests but failed independent
adversarial review. A changed geometry could be self-rehashed and authorize
an expensive stage because no out-of-band expected digest was required.
After self-rehash, the validator also accepted impossible or pre-origin
target dates, invalid timestamps, contradictory or incomplete regime sets,
empty eligibility, `Bool` horizons, placeholder IDs such as `Used` and
`Other`, and missingness masks that retained zero origins. Hypothesis labels
were off by one relative to tensor positions, and the nominally
"independent" direct null used a shared factor with cross-hypothesis
correlation 0.5.

Those are contract defects even though every scientific gate was false.
The initial hashes and 284-test result are therefore superseded and must not
be cited as an accepted calibration boundary.

The first hardening pass added real calendar parsing, explicit
`origin_quarter`, exact quarter-end horizon mapping, mutually exclusive
regime families, reserved-token rejection, external geometry pinning,
minimum retained sample size, comparison mappings, and independent N00
columns. A second audit then found three residual semantic weaknesses:
eligibility order was not canonical, `[1, 12]` was accepted as a mature
horizon set, and documentation overclaimed that the validator itself derived
NBER and policy regimes from timestamps.

The accepted geometry schema v3 now:

- requires eligibility arrays to be nonempty ordered subsequences of their
  registries;
- requires mature horizons to be a nonempty downward-closed prefix of
  `(1, 2, 4, 8, 12)`;
- binds exact `EXTERNALLY_REVIEWED_SCORE_BLIND_ASSERTIONS`; and
- states plainly that schema validation enforces closed/exclusive labels but
  cannot reproduce NBER or FOMC/policy state. Substantive score-blind review
  and the external geometry digest are the acceptance boundary.

An internal geometry digest remains only an integrity check. Any expensive
stage requires a separately supplied expected semantic SHA-256; rewriting a
geometry and recomputing its internal hash does not pass under the earlier
external pin. Smoke mode rejects both a geometry path and geometry pin.

### Verification and exact non-result

An independent final reviewer reproduced 5,025 protocol canonical bytes,
matched the declared and compiled semantic pin, reran all previously
successful seed/window/block/binomial/shard checks, and found no residual
defect in the focused re-audit. The checked-bounds, deprecation-error suite
passes **343/343**, Runic 1.7.0 passes, `git diff --check` passes, and the
suite is wired into hermetic CI.

| Artifact | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `USForecastInferenceCalibration.jl` | `7cd037ac9550d8bbbdc4f81317679acabd230ae3f1458ed53936b024f8324b37` |
| `test_forecast_inference_calibration.jl` | `a5fc9feab48ffc790c8bcc61395ff7f7811ca348a489a84f86c7c99fa87d946e` |
| calibration `README.md` | `020d5aded7e5531a79faef134e3a3668af8f52521d148fbc86008177e8ab6a04` |
| physical protocol TOML | `4ce856e2ecc3edfbd43588aa7de04a2841c5872e7a749928975a942d8cc2f721` |

There is deliberately no full runner and no accepted external geometry
artifact. No outer Monte Carlo replication was launched, no J01--J04 policy
was selected, and no size, coverage, strong-FWER, power, p-value, empirical
origin, score, promotion, superiority, readiness, or production evidence was
created. Unit-test success validates software behavior only.

## 2026-08-07 - Hardened EFFR one-effective-date receipt boundary

### Offline contract derived from the source survey

The EFFR source decision is now implemented as an in-memory, hermetic
receipt contract at
`scripts/us/forecasting/vintages/effr/capture_contract/`. It converts the
[New York Fed publication and revision policy](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates),
[Markets Data API boundary](https://markets.newyorkfed.org/static/docs/markets-api.html),
[terms obligations](https://www.newyorkfed.org/privacy/termsofuse), and
[March 2016 concept break](https://www.federalreserve.gov/Releases/H15/20160307/default.htm)
from the literature survey into closed validation rules.

For one effective date, rate and volume receipts remain separate until both
bind:

- the exact authority, post-2016 EFFR concept, evidence track, endpoint,
  canonical one-date query, requested/final URL, and report type;
- effective and publication dates, New York UTC offset, request/header/body
  timestamps, and conservative availability upper bound;
- status, host, redirects, complete headers, content metadata, raw response
  SHA-256, captured OpenAPI SHA-256, content-addressed storage locator, and
  durable-storage receipt;
- raw rate, percentiles, target range, volume, footnote, revision indicator,
  and current-state fields;
- append-only predecessor/supersession pointers; and
- terms snapshot hash/date/review, closed attribution and disclaimer
  profiles, redistribution scope, and public-endpoint secret state.

The publication clock is operational rather than descriptive. For the
post-2016 U.S. Eastern DST rule, first-state request/header/completion times
must all fall in `[09:00, 14:30)` New York time and same-day revisions in
`[14:30, 24:00)`. The publication date must be a weekday and one to four
calendar days after the effective date. A 2017 value fetched in 2026 can be
`CURRENT_STATE` only; it cannot be relabeled as a first-public capture.
Later corrections and current-state lookups retain distinct, non-intraday
claims.

The contract preserves the survey's raw-token classifications for blank and
`r` revision indicators, footnotes 1/2/3, absent rate-report volume,
unsupported blanks, current-state flags, schema mismatches, and matched-state
quarantine. It rejects aliases, numeric strings, `Bool` coercions,
nonfinite values, generic defaults, `Used`, `Other`, and unknown states. A
complete rate row must satisfy:

```text
p1 <= p25 <= EFFR <= p75 <= p99
targetRateFrom <= targetRateTo
```

An internal receipt digest is only an integrity check. Validation also
requires an out-of-band expected SHA-256. Changing a receipt and recomputing
its embedded digest fails under the earlier external pin.

### Governance and pair-level fail-closed rules

The terms snapshot may be no more than 31 days old and must not postdate the
publication. Approved internal-research and public-derived decisions have
distinct exact attribution, disclaimer, and redistribution profiles.
Pending and rejected decisions carry `TERMS_REVIEW_PENDING` or
`TERMS_REVIEW_REJECTED`, prohibit redistribution, and cannot produce a
joined pair.

Pairing requires exact agreement on effective date, raw revision token,
state class, publication date/offset, pair key, OpenAPI digest, terms
snapshot hash/date/decision, attribution, disclaimer, and redistribution
scope. A difference returns a typed quarantine with no joined record.
Even an exact joined pair is a validated receipt pair only; it is not a
parsed or admitted historical observation.

### Why two passing intermediate suites were rejected

The first version passed 124/124 tests but failed independent audit. It
accepted a retrospective 2017 observation captured in 2026 as
`FIRST_0900_STATE`, accepted first/revision captures outside the declared
09:00/14:30 windows, allowed rate and volume receipts with different OpenAPI
or terms contexts to join, and treated rejected terms as nonblocking.
Scalar bounds also allowed impossible percentile and target-range ordering.
That version is superseded.

The first hardening expanded the suite to 176/176 and closed those defects,
but a focused re-audit found one residual decision fall-through:
`APPROVED_FOR_BOUNDED_CAPTURE + PROHIBITED` could borrow the rejected-use
profile and join. Governance dispatch now has an explicit `REJECTED` branch
and fails every unregistered decision/scope combination. Direct receipt and
pair-path regressions prove that the forged approved/prohibited combination
cannot validate or join.

The final independent focused audit passes, the checked-bounds and
deprecation-error suite passes **178/178**, Runic 1.7.0 passes, scoped
`git diff --check` passes, and the test is wired into hermetic CI.

| `test_effr_capture_contract.jl` | `6356f2f8ae4efb74ecbd063fb962f82a423d36c665276449679da3b197af3197` |

## 2026-08-07 - ABM competition feasibility and validation-protocol literature decision

### Current scientific verdict

A focused repository audit and an independent literature survey were run
before attempting an ABM-versus-benchmark score. The result is a negative
feasibility finding, not a negative finding about the model's eventual
forecast skill: **a scientifically meaningful ABM accuracy comparison is not
yet runnable**.

The decisive blockers are:

- zero admitted forecast origins and 0/8 promotion-ready Tier-1 observation
  operators;
- no executable U.S. DSGE comparator;
- no authenticated historical structural/state panel;
- no validated ABM observation operators for PCE or core-PCE inflation, CPS
  unemployment, CES payroll employment, or EFFR;
- a current U.S. calibration object that uses one 2024 annual structure across
  mechanically available 2024Q1-2026Q1 dates; and
- unresolved opening-accounting and scale-convergence gates.

The existing two-quarter U.S. holdout cannot repair these omissions. Its
outcomes have already been opened, it is current/revised rather than
vintage-clean, its levels were reanchored, it uses legacy class-H correction
machinery, and it has no common-information challenger. It remains an
engineering diagnostic and cannot support an accuracy or suitability claim.

The Austrian experiment from the reference paper also cannot presently be
reproduced. The repository has a frozen 2010Q1 parameter/state object and
recent 2024/2026 objects, but not the complete rolling 2010Q2-2016Q4
calibration inputs or an authenticated implementation of every paper
convention.

### Origin-firewall and observation-operator audit

The current U.S. calibration code estimates dynamic processes through a
requested origin and initializes quarterly balance-sheet controls at that
origin. It nevertheless returns structural, dynamic, and state quantities in
monolithic dictionaries rather than separately hashed artifacts. In
particular, returned `C_G`, `C_E`, and `Y_I` arrays can contain observations
after the requested origin. The base model currently consumes only element
`T_prime`, but post-origin values still cross the byte-level state-artifact
boundary. They must be truncated, and future-row mutation invariance must be
proved, before this can qualify as a forecast-origin builder.

Initial microstates are constructed randomly inside `Model`; they are not yet
persisted as an origin-state artifact or separated from future process
innovations. The model records real and nominal GDP, expenditure components,
wages, sector GVA, and its internal central-bank rate. That internal
`euribor`/policy-rate field is not an approved EFFR bridge. Real-GDP growth
and GDP-deflator inflation, derived from real GDP and
`nominal_gdp / real_gdp`, are the smallest plausible operator candidates, but
both remain pending validation.

### Exact Poledna-parity branch

The local 63-page Poledna, Miess, and Hommes paper was re-rendered and visually
checked at Section 3 and Tables 2-4. Its main experiment:

- estimates initially over 1997Q1-2010Q1;
- evaluates quarterly forecast origins from 2010Q2 through 2016Q4 and
  re-estimates each model every quarter;
- evaluates horizons 1, 2, 4, 8, and 12 quarters;
- averages 500 ABM Monte Carlo paths for the point forecast; and
- reports RMSE levels and gains/losses against AR or VAR anchors.

The paper separately evaluates unconditional forecasts and an ex-post
conditional experiment that uses realized external paths. Those products must
remain separate. The U.S. project will retain a paper-parity branch with the
same 500-path mean and table grammar, but it will be labeled a revised-data
methodological comparison rather than a real-time replication. This decision
follows [Poledna, Miess, and Hommes](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.euroecorev.2022.104306);
the journal article was published in 2023 from the reviewed 2020 preprint.

### Stronger U.S. ABM evaluation protocol

The primary U.S. branch will be stricter than paper parity:

1. **Simulation precision.** Five hundred paths are retained only for parity.
   The proposed confirmatory design starts with 10,000 independent paths per
   model-origin, in 20 deterministic batches of 500. Before scores are
   opened, the common count increases to 20,000 or 40,000 if batch/jackknife
   Monte Carlo standard error exceeds 1% of the target's origin-specific
   training standard deviation for the ensemble mean, median, or reported
   interval endpoints. If unresolved at 40,000, the result is retained with
   `MC_PRECISION_UNRESOLVED` and cannot support a close-rank superiority
   claim. The exact 10,000/1%/40,000 thresholds are a **project
   preregistration proposal**, not values dictated by the literature. The
   literature-backed requirement is to design, report, and control Monte
   Carlo error explicitly
   ([Morris, White, and Crowther](https://doi.org/10.1002/sim.8086);
   [Koehler, Brown, and Haneuse](https://doi.org/10.1198/tast.2009.0030)).

2. **Loss-consistent point forecasts.** The ensemble mean is the point
   functional for squared-error/RMSE loss and the ensemble median for
   absolute-error/MAE loss. Both may be reported, but neither is used to claim
   optimality under the other's loss
   ([Gneiting](https://doi.org/10.1198/jasa.2011.r10138)).

3. **Density evaluation.** CRPS is the primary proper ensemble score, with a
   fair finite-ensemble correction when required
   ([Gneiting and Raftery](https://doi.org/10.1198/016214506000001437);
   [Ferro](https://doi.org/10.1002/qj.2270)). Log score is secondary and is
   admissible only after a training-only density construction, support
   transform, bandwidth/tail policy, and treatment of parameter uncertainty
   are frozen. PIT/rank diagnostics, central 50%/80%/95% coverage, interval
   width, quantile scores, and WIS will accompany point losses
   ([Diebold, Gunther, and Tay](https://doi.org/10.2307/2527342);
   [Gneiting, Balabdaoui, and Raftery](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9868.2007.00587.x);
   [Christoffersen](https://doi.org/10.2307/2527341);
   [Bracher et al.](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1008618)).

4. **Multi-horizon construction.** Each ABM path runs freely once from the
   origin through quarter 12; horizons are extracted from that joint path
   without restarting from realized intermediate outcomes. Iterated
   AR/VAR/BVAR forecasts are the primary comparison, with prespecified direct
   statistical forecasts as a sensitivity
   ([Marcellino, Stock, and Watson](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jeconom.2005.07.020)).

5. **Origin-by-origin competition.** Every model is recalibrated at each
   origin using only the sealed information set. Transformations, variable
   selection, tuning, priors, and postprocessing stay inside the origin.
   Common-core-information and native-input tracks are both reported, with
   identical targets, transformations, issue timestamps, truth policy, and
   scoring code. Failed paths and failed model-origins remain visible.

6. **Inference and uncertainty.** Paired loss is
   `challenger - comparator`, so negative favors the challenger. The frozen
   HAC/block-aware Diebold-Mariano, Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold,
   Romano-Wolf, and secondary Model Confidence Set protocol applies.
   Clark-West is used only for genuinely nested predictive regressions.
   Monte Carlo uncertainty across ABM paths remains separate from sampling
   uncertainty across origins.

7. **Seeds and common random numbers.** Seeds are domain-separated by
   experiment, model version, origin, path, and purpose. Failed paths are not
   replaced by opportunistic seeds. Common random numbers are reserved for
   compatible paired ABM variants sharing the same stochastic primitives,
   never imposed across unrelated model laws.

8. **Regimes and dubious tokens.** The full sample stays primary. Pandemic,
   NBER-recession, ELB, and other masks are frozen before ABM scores are
   opened. A bare `Used` token is invalid. A typed source-usage relationship
   is provenance, not a regime; BEA's native `Used` accounting label remains
   a distinct source concept. `Other`, unknown, contradictory, or unmapped
   values retain their raw token, enter
   `REGIME_UNKNOWN_PENDING_ADJUDICATION` or the applicable typed conflict,
   and are excluded from the affected regime contrast with an explicit
   count; they are never coerced to the baseline group. Pandemic-specific
   modeling remains a sensitivity
   ([Lenza and Primiceri](https://doi.org/10.1002/jae.2895);
   [Schorfheide and Song](https://doi.org/10.21799/frbp.wp.2020.26)).

9. **Vintage and truth layers.** Promotion evidence uses vintage-clean
   origins. First-release, fixed-maturity, and latest-revised truth layers are
   frozen separately. Paper-parity and latest-revised results remain
   diagnostics, and revision-induced score/rank changes are reported
   explicitly
   ([Croushore and Stark](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0);
   [Koenig, Dolmas, and Piger](https://doi.org/10.1162/003465303322369768)).

10. **Model-card separation.** Calibration moments, identification limits,
    stochastic mechanisms, parameter uncertainty, initialization, convergence,
    failures, and empirical features used for calibration versus validation
    are disclosed
    ([Fagiolo, Moneta, and Windrum](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10614-007-9104-4)).

## 2026-08-07 - Day-zero prospective EFFR acquisition path prepared

### Time-sensitive contract finding

The 2026Q3 prospective draft requires an EFFR first-state receipt manifest
covering New York Fed publication days from 2026-08-07 through 2026-10-30 and
a same-day revision-check manifest through 2026-10-29. This makes 2026-08-07
the non-reconstructible first day of the campaign. The publication date is
2026-08-07 and the effective date is 2026-08-06.

A minimal runner now exists at
`scripts/us/forecasting/vintages/effr/prospective_acquisition/`. It permits one
first-state transaction during `13:00:00Z-13:15:00Z` and one revision-check
transaction during `18:30:00Z-18:45:00Z`, then refuses the date/window forever.
Each phase performs exactly six direct, no-redirect, unauthenticated GETs:

1. the exact all-rates one-date JSON route with `type=rate`;
2. the exact all-rates one-date JSON route with `type=volume`;
3. the official Markets API documentation HTML;
4. the `markets-api.yml` bytes discovered from that HTML;
5. the New York Fed terms page; and
6. the official holiday-schedule page.

Every completed response body, including a completed non-200 or unexpected
media-type body, is retained before semantic validation. The importer requires
exactly one raw `type="EFFR"` row in the multi-rate envelope, records its JSON
pointer, one-based index, raw identity, and raw key set, and rejects zero or
multiple matches. It never selects row one by convention or substitutes the
series-specific CSV route.

### Live-schema discrepancy handled without imputation

Two stdout-only, write-free capability probes for the older 2026-08-05
effective date found that the official live EFFR rows and current OpenAPI
schema omit `currentState`. The offline one-date receipt contract requires
that field. Filling it with `false` would turn an inference into a claimed raw
field, so the day-zero importer now refuses to do so.

For the currently observed schema, a successful first-state network capture
will therefore install full raw bytes and a self-hashed local bundle with:

```text
status =
  RAW_CAPTURE_COMPLETED_NONADMITTING_ONE_DATE_CONTRACT_INCOMPATIBLE
raw_capture_complete = true
one_date_receipt_validated = false
failure_code =
  ONE_DATE_CONTRACT_RAW_CURRENT_STATE_FIELD_ABSENT
```

That status is successful raw evidence and must not trigger a duplicate
request. It creates no one-date receipt or rate-volume pair. A later,
versioned normalization contract may adjudicate the absent field without
changing the captured bytes.

The 14:30 phase validates the predecessor raw bundle. Byte-identical rate and
volume bodies with empty revision tokens produce an immutable
`BYTE_IDENTICAL_NO_REVISION_RECEIPT_CREATED` check. Changed bytes without the
closed `r` token are quarantined. Only a raw `r`, at least one changed body,
and an otherwise valid linked pair may create
`SAME_DAY_1430_REVISION` receipts. An unchanged lookup is never forged into a
revision.

### Storage, scheduling, and verification boundary

Installation is append-only and atomic. A private deterministic journal is
created and containment-checked before network access. Each request receives
an immutable start event; every completed response body is exclusively
created, file- and directory-synced, read back, and verified in two local
copies before response or semantic validation and before the next request.
Attempted, completed, validated, and failed request identities remain
distinct. All existing ancestor components, the date/state directories, the
journal, and the final candidate reject symbolic links, and real-path
containment is rechecked immediately before and after atomic publication.
Hard links, path traversal, overwrites, tampered manifests, tampered
predecessor bytes, and mismatched local-storage receipts also fail closed.
The bundle binds its preflight and attempt-event files as well as the exact
acquisition source, project, manifest, prospective-contract, and
receipt-contract identities.

These local replicas and self-generated pins are integrity aids only. They do
not establish two externally durable copies, an external timestamp, retention
through 2031, an independently attested clock/transport, a machine-validated
holiday calendar, a precommitted OpenAPI trust pin, a complete daily-manifest
verifier, prospective-contract approval, or authorization from the still-false
historical-backfill acquisition gate. All inventory, empirical, admission,
accuracy, promotion, production-scoring, and readiness gates remain false.

## 2026-08-07 - Ambiguous-token provenance and regime boundary accepted

### Literature and standards decision

A focused literature/standards survey and repository audit were run for bare
`Used`, `Other`, unknown, contradictory, and otherwise dubious values. The
sources support four scoped principles:

1. W3C PROV-DM defines usage as a typed relation between an activity and an
   entity, not as a free quality or regime status
   ([W3C PROV-DM](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/)).
2. Detailed, source-bound provenance and domain-relevant standards are part of
   reusable-data practice
   ([Wilkinson et al.](https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18)).
3. BEA `Use`, `Other`, scrap, used, and secondhand-goods concepts belong to
   their native input-output accounting context and must not be reinterpreted
   as generic forecast-regime states
   ([BEA I-O concepts and methods](https://www.bea.gov/sites/default/files/methodologies/IOmanual_092906.pdf)).
4. Transparent missing/classification counts and explicit exclusions are
   preferable to silent deletion or baseline coercion
   ([STROBE](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.0040296)).

The resulting project rule is therefore scoped, not lexical: a bare `Used`
regime/status is invalid; a typed source-usage relation is provenance; and a
native BEA `Used` label remains a distinct accounting concept. `Other`,
unknown, and dubious raw values are retained with evidence and a typed
disposition, never mapped silently to zero or the baseline. The exact
BeforeIT status names, exhaustive three-contrast grid, and
affected-contrast-only exclusion rule are project protocol decisions; none of
the cited sources mandates those particular encodings.

### RTDSM provenance validation hole closed

The audit found that the RTDSM fingerprint generator constructed the intended
typed provenance but its compact-artifact validator originally required only
the top-level `provenance` key. A first repair validated the nested object but
was independently rejected because an attacker could change a cross-check BEA
hash and its matching `used` hash together, or swap the two releases, while
preserving internal consistency.

The accepted validator now reloads the locally SHA-pinned RTDSM profile,
derives the exact ordered reference-period-to-BEA-fingerprint mapping, checks
each cross-check's period, vintage, hash, and annual-update caveat against that
mapping, and then binds each ordered lowercase `used` relation to the
profile-derived hash. It rejects bare `Used`/`Other`, coercive unknown
policies, malformed or reordered records, coordinated double rebinds, and
swapped-release provenance.

Independent verification passed:

```text
RTDSM acquisition Julia assertions                         196 / 196
native BEA special-account Julia assertions                227 / 227
Used/Other evidence-ledger Julia assertions                225 / 225
independent adversarial provenance mutations rejected       19 / 19
```
