### Minimum-cut decision: pursue the prospective 2026Q3 origin

The post-preflight evidence audit selects the prospective route rather than
relabeling a retrospective artifact. The earliest currently specified strict
candidate is
`origin.2026q3.prospective-capture-candidate.v2` at
`2026-10-30T14:00:00Z`. The preserved 2017Q3 HMI7 pair is useful for official-
archive reconstruction, but its Section 2 workbook carries a
`2017-10-31T15:29:36Z` current-server `Last-Modified` value after the nominal
October 30 cutoff, historical first-state EFFR bytes are absent, and all six
structural catalogs remain empty. The 2026Q1 ABM package is a revised/current-
vintage negative control: it was retrieved after 2026Q2 advance GDP was
public, so its h=1 path cannot be treated as an unseen forecast.

The dependency-ordered pilot remains substantial: a frozen no-truth forecast
protocol; 21 prospective requirements and 107 selector-resolved profiles; a
complete source inventory and structural-as-of receipt; an 8/8-block,
9/9-gate, 7/7-mapping runnable origin package; origin-bound GDP/PCE/EFFR
training data; five empirical executable model registrations; and a common
path/convergence contract, followed by a forecast seal before truth access.
The smallest plausible software pilot cell is real-GDP growth at h=2, because
h=1 crosses the ABM opening-to-flow basis break. That cell would test pipeline
closure only; it would not satisfy the full h=1/2/4/8/12 protocol or establish
accuracy.

The first atomic prospective cut is EFFR. The existing v2 profile expects a
daily first-state and revision manifest, whereas the accepted observed-state
v3 contract proves that `currentState` is absent from the pinned OpenAPI and
captured wire and keeps the estimand decision pending. For a prospective
forecast input, the scientifically relevant alternative is a separately
governed `PRE_ORIGIN_OBSERVED_ENDPOINT_VINTAGE`: the latest endpoint values
actually observed before the origin, without calling them first-public,
atomic, or final. An additive, fail-closed EFFR endpoint/estimand profile is
therefore the next implementation; it must require distinct owner/validator
approval and complete evidence-bound daily coverage, and it must emit
`CANNOT_RUN` until those conditions exist.

The prospective-v2 retention rule also contains a material horizon error. It
retains origin evidence only through `2031-10-30T14:00:00Z`, five years after
the origin. But h=12 from a 2026Q3 origin targets 2029Q3, whose 60-month mature
truth boundary is no earlier than `2034-09-30`. V2 remains frozen historical
evidence; any active successor must co-retain origin, forecast, receipt, and
truth bytes through the last required mature-truth receipt, not merely origin
plus 60 months.

The real-GDP operator audit found a separate three-contract conflation. The
official target is BEA NIPA `T10106:1/A191RX`, transformed within one coherent
release/vintage as `400 * (log(level_t) - log(level_t_minus_1))`. Core-three
`real_gdp_growth` is only an identity alias of that already transformed
column and must not be transformed again. The ABM measurement equation is a
different question: its constructor row is a model-implied normalized-price
initialization, whereas rows 2+ are completed-period additive real flows.
Constant scale, chained-dollar base, and SAAR factors cancel in log changes
only within one measurement basis; they cannot repair h=1. Rows 2+ are
same-basis model diagnostics but are not yet validated as BEA Fisher-chain
real GDP.

The transform label must also remain exact. BEA's [NIPA Handbook chapter
4](https://www.bea.gov/resources/methodologies/nipa-handbook/pdf/chapter-04.pdf)
and [quarterly-growth
FAQ](https://www.bea.gov/help/faq/122) define the published headline annual
rate by compounding the quarterly level ratio, while this project deliberately
uses the continuously compounded `400 * delta-log` transform. Both are valid
annualizations, but they are not numerically identical and the latter must not
be described as reproducing the BEA headline percent change. BEA also states
that percent changes for chained-dollar measures are calculated from quantity
indexes. The future bridge must therefore bind the exact A191RX level selector
and same-vintage adjacent levels, identify the project log transform as its
own preregistered observable, and reject simple growth, compounded-headline
growth, or independently selected numerator/denominator vintages as aliases.

This separation follows the real-time-data evidence rather than only source
arithmetic. The Philadelphia Fed's [Real-Time Data Set for
Macroeconomists](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/real-time-data-set-for-macroeconomists)
retains complete vintage histories as level snapshots, and Stark and
Croushore ([2002](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0164-0704(02)00062-9)) show that
forecast-error measures can change materially with latest-available versus
real-time data and with the chosen realization. Consequently each adjacent
level pair must come from one coherent information-set snapshot; a pair built
from separately selected latest values is not an origin-valid growth
observation.

Accordingly, `abm-to-bea-real-gdp.v1-draft` remains unapproved. A later
`real_gdp_bridge_decomposition.v1` should separately seal the BEA
level-to-growth transform, the core-three name/unit alias, and the ABM
measurement candidate; accept ABM growth only when both adjacent rows are
typed completed-period flows; and reject silent burn-in, horizon shifting,
double transformation, or treating an origin anchor as concept equivalence.
This decision prevents an easy numerical alignment from masquerading as the
official observation bridge.

### Common-origin acquisition v3 composition-verifier design

A separate read-only design audit confirms that prospective v2 cannot be
wrapped or relabelled into readiness. Its frozen 21-requirement/107-profile
tuple is internally complete, but `evaluate_requirement_completion` always
returns `verifier_attested=false`, `complete=false`,
`origin_admissible=false`, and `ready=false`. The canonical sorted tuple of
requirement ID, profile ID, selector, capture ID, and completion date has
SHA-256
`9fa271ea0bc646c8f3789084d8c61e04e2b31c4c5e4eeb6b551a217499ac75fb`.
That identity is a coverage baseline, not a proof that any evidence exists.

The required successor is an additive, standard-library-only
`common_origin_acquisition_v3` composition verifier. It will have two
separate levels: a module-pinned immutable policy containing exact legacy
bindings, dispatch rules, claim ceilings, and retention semantics; and a
per-origin evidence manifest whose exact hash becomes the downstream
`origin_information_set_sha256`. The composition module may hash but never
execute leaf-verifier source. It must not `include`, `eval`, dynamically
dispatch a function named in data, open truth, import a model or scoring
module, perform network I/O, or write evidence.

The policy needs an exact 21-entry dispatch table keyed by receipt schema,
requirement ID, source ID, and evidence role. Every entry must freeze the
qualified leaf-verifier source/test identities, allowed profile IDs, claim
schema, independent validation-receipt type, media types, and artifact roles.
There is no wildcard or prefix dispatch. Each of the 107 parent rows may only
bind its legacy and active profile IDs, exact dispatch ID, receipt path/hash,
and an exact semantic-supersession decision where needed. Readiness must be
rederived from raw and receipt hashes, selector/catalog closure, pre-origin
availability, two genuinely independent durable replicas, an external
timestamp over the exact subject hash, distinct owner and validator
signatures, and the corrected custody covenant. Local self-hashes, HTTP/local
timestamps, duplicated files on one inode/object/storage domain, or status
strings are not independent evidence.

EFFR requires an explicit three-profile semantic supersession rather than an
alias. `effr_daily_history` becomes a separately approved complete endpoint-
history universe with a justified start. The legacy first-state and revision
profiles become 58 morning endpoint observations and 57 later endpoint
observations, plus 57 same-day comparison decisions, under the accepted
58/57/115 restart geometry. These receipts must never claim first-public,
`currentState`, final-state, or no-later-revision semantics, and they cannot
borrow the irrecoveribly absent August 7 later observation. The current
84-date July 1--October 29 draft is a candidate profile only: frozen v2 does
not imply that start date, it is probably too short for common-information
AR/VAR estimation, and it lacks accepted ownership, validation, lineage, and
custody evidence.

An official-source recheck makes that history gap decisive. The New York Fed
[EFFR page](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/effr) states
that it publishes the prior business day's rate at approximately 9:00 a.m.;
its [reference-rate methodology and revision
policy](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/reference-rates/additional-information-about-reference-rates)
states that the EFFR data source and calculation method changed with the
March 1, 2016 rate. The current core-three mechanics require at least 60
quarterly training observations and the revised diagnostic panel begins in
2000Q3. Therefore an 84-business-day Q3 campaign cannot by itself satisfy the
model-input history obligation. A successor must freeze an economically
justified start date, prove enough pre-origin quarters for every model, and
specify how the 2016 regime break is represented. Until then,
`daily_history_selector_start_approved` and
`training_history_length_sufficient` remain false.

Retention is derived from target geometry. A 2026Q3 origin with h=12 targets
2029Q3, whose 60-month minimum boundary is
`2034-09-30T23:59:59Z`. Release/deletion is permitted only after both that
calendar boundary and the completion, external timestamping, and durable
replication of the last required mature-truth receipt; a later date such as
October 30 may be a cushion but is not the derived boundary. Pre-seal
verification checks the custody covenant without loading future truth.

Minimum adversarial acceptance includes exact 21/107 bijection; rejection of
missing, extra, duplicate, narrowed, wrong-source/capture, post-origin, or
unknown receipt types; proof that a referenced candidate `.jl` file cannot
execute; physical/source/receipt restamp and race attacks; link/path and
replica-domain attacks; exact EFFR geometry and exclusions; corrected h=12
retention; and deterministic exhaustive blockers from unrelated working
directories. Synthetic fixtures may emit only `CANNOT_RUN`; a fully valid
nonsynthetic parent may emit at most
`READY_FOR_FORECAST_SEAL_NO_TRUTH_LOADED`. Origin admission, inventory
mutation, forecast execution, truth access, scoring, accuracy, promotion, and
production remain impossible in this layer.

contract
`b24ff0c40172d2a23991fbe75c2fe42c6ba6c6c1f5fd46d079ac6d51429bf98f`,
and semantic identity
`5d1e7f34eea0470877c7bed096d8b2fb26590f95bd06febb90813faf6063708a`.

### Historical-state decision: quarantine, not origin admission

The official event page identifies BEA 17-56 as the 2017Q3 advance estimate,
embargoed until 08:30 EDT on October 27, 2017, and explicitly says that the
advance estimate used incomplete source data subject to revision
([BEA 17-56](https://www.bea.gov/news/2017/gross-domestic-product-3rd-quarter-2017-advance-estimate)).
The preserved Section 1 response reports `Last-Modified: Fri, 27 Oct 2017
17:34:50 GMT`, but Section 2 reports `Last-Modified: Tue, 31 Oct 2017
15:29:36 GMT`. Inside the files, Section 1 says `File created Oct 26 2017
2:25PM`; Section 2 says `File created Oct 29 2017 1:23PM` even though both
display `Data published Oct 27 2017 8:30AM`. Thus this exact pair cannot be the
atomic bytes available at the October 27 release instant. Current headers and
local capture time also remain unauthenticated. The receipt's
`PRESENT_DAY_HMI7_ARCHIVE_RETRIEVAL_NOT_HISTORICAL_FIRST_STATE` boundary and
all false origin/empirical/promotion gates are therefore substantively
confirmed, not merely inherited labels.

workbook remained CPU-bound for about eight minutes and was interrupted
without producing a render or touching the raw bundle. This is an importer

dependency-free OOXML primitives in
`historical_fingerprints/fingerprint_historical_releases.py` then validated

The PCE and core-PCE calculations round to the event page's published 1.5%

Unlike the later 2019 and 2021 HMI7 profile, all ten inspected Q2/Q3 target
cells are stored as OOXML shared strings with `General` style, including
comma-grouped dollar levels, rather than numeric cells with numeric number
formats. The frozen later-era parser correctly rejects that representation
under its own closed profile. It must not be weakened globally or silently
strip commas. A separately specified and tested 2017-era profile must
establish exact lexical grammar, numeric conversion, formatting,
complete-history rules, and mapping identity before this workbook can enter
even a reconstructed-value panel.

A full 283-quarter row scan further bounded that profile. Nominal GDP, real
GDP, the GDP deflator, and the PCE price index are shared-string/`General`
cells without formulas at every quarter. The two level rows use exact
three-digit comma grouping, and the two index rows use exactly three decimal
places. Core PCE has the same cell type/style but carries the literal source
missing token `.....` for 1947Q1--1958Q4 (48 cells) and three-decimal values
for 1959Q1--2017Q3 (235 cells). The period axis is complete even though the
source series is not. The new profile must therefore represent these 48
cells as typed source-missing observations, require the first numeric core-PCE
value at 1959Q1 and no later gaps, and reject every other blank, dot count,
`NA`, locale, whitespace, or numeric alias.

This live pilot advances raw-byte preservation and reveals the next parser
work, but it creates no historical first state, admitted origin, approved

## 2026-08-08 - Vintage uncertainty and dubious-field literature rule refined

A focused literature and official-methods review found that one Boolean
`real_time` flag collapses scientifically distinct facts. The warehouse and
final report must instead retain five orthogonal axes:

| Axis | Closed project vocabulary | Decision rule |
|---|---|---|
| byte observation | `PROSPECTIVE_BYTES_OBSERVED`, `PRESENT_DAY_ARCHIVE_RETRIEVAL`, `EXACT_HISTORICAL_BYTES_INDEPENDENTLY_PROVEN`, `NO_BYTE_EVIDENCE` | a hash created at retrieval proves fixity from then forward, not historical byte identity |
| information-set construction | `CONTEMPORANEOUS_REAL_TIME_INFORMATION_SET`, `RECONSTRUCTED_REAL_TIME_INFORMATION_SET`, `PSEUDO_REAL_TIME_RELEASE_LAGS_ONLY`, `FINAL_REVISED_PSEUDO_OUT_OF_SAMPLE`, `MIXED_VINTAGE_DIAGNOSTIC`, `UNKNOWN_INFORMATION_SET` | real-time includes release lags and revisions; a lag calendar applied to latest data is only pseudo-real-time |
| release availability evidence | independent `release_identity`, `content_match`, `basis`, timestamp `precision`, and `first_public` fields | vintage date, first-public status, and intraday availability are not interchangeable |
| concept match | `EXACT_SOURCE_CONCEPT`, `SOURCE_RESIDUAL_PRESERVED`, `HIERARCHICAL_PARTIAL_MATCH`, `NO_EQUIVALENT_CATEGORY`, `ANALYST_IMPUTED_MAPPING`, `UNRESOLVED_CONCEPT` | source categories, source quality flags, and analyst crosswalk judgments remain separate |
| use/admission decision | `ORIGIN_ADMISSIBLE`, `PSEUDO_REAL_TIME_ONLY`, `DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY`, `QUARANTINED_PENDING_EVIDENCE`, `EXCLUDED` | admission is derived from evidence on the other axes and is never treated as provenance itself |

This structure follows the central real-time-data result of
[Croushore and Stark (2001)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-4076(01)00072-0):
historical information sets can be scientifically reconstructed from old
published sources when the reconstruction enforces what was actually known
at each date. It also follows the ECB's explicit distinction between
real-time vintages, which reflect both publication delay and revision, and
pseudo-real-time vintages, which simulate delays while retaining revised data
([Bańbura and Saiz 2020](https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/economic-bulletin/articles/2020/html/ecb.ebart202002_02~47da9ba4f7.en.html)).

The resulting admission rule is conjunctive. A historical observation may be
`ORIGIN_ADMISSIBLE` only when its contemporaneous or reconstructed
information set is established; exact release identity, semantic content,
and availability are independently evidenced; the conservative latest
possible availability does not exceed the forecast cutoff; concept, units,
valuation, seasonal adjustment, and source status are preserved or mapped by
a frozen crosswalk; and every required transformation was available and
frozen at the origin. Date-only availability is conservatively assigned to
the end of that source-local day and cannot establish same-day intraday
eligibility. `first_public=PROVEN` always requires separate evidence.

This does not make retrospective bytes contemporaneous. Later-retrieved
official archive bytes remain `PRESENT_DAY_ARCHIVE_RETRIEVAL`. They can
support `RECONSTRUCTED_REAL_TIME_INFORMATION_SET` only if exact historical
release identity, content, and availability are corroborated independently;
otherwise their information set stays `UNKNOWN_INFORMATION_SET` and their use
is diagnostic or quarantined. The 2017Q3 HMI7 pilot is therefore presently:

```text
byte_observation_mode = PRESENT_DAY_ARCHIVE_RETRIEVAL
information_set_construction_mode = UNKNOWN_INFORMATION_SET
release_identity = ASSOCIATION_ONLY
first_public = UNKNOWN
concept_match_status = EXACT_SOURCE_CONCEPT for the five parsed rows
use_admission_decision = QUARANTINED_PENDING_EVIDENCE
```

Its Section 2 post-release creation and `Last-Modified` evidence rules out an
atomic October 27 first-byte claim. Exact concept mapping cannot repair that
vintage-provenance gap. The current RTDSM capture receives the same byte mode;
its curated vintage columns may become a reconstructed research information
set only at the exact evidence tier supported, never contemporaneously
observed bytes. The Philadelphia Fed's own change history illustrates the
required fail-closed behavior: delete observations when an unobserved
revision likely occurred and retain explicit missing values when source pages
are unavailable ([RTDSM changes](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/changes-to-the-real-time-data-set),
[missing-data register](https://www.philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/data-needed-real-time-data-set)).

Recursive estimation must also preserve the vintages of regressors already
observed at the historical origin rather than mixing first-release dependent
variables with mature right-hand-side histories. The recommendation follows
[Koenig, Dolmas, and Piger (2003)](https://doi.org/10.1162/003465303322369768),
while its preference for first-release targets remains a hypothesis to test
against this project's separate truth layers, not an assumption. All models
must use the same declared information set and truth definition. Results will
be reported separately against `FIRST_RELEASE`, a fixed-lag realization,
`PRE_COMPREHENSIVE_REVISION`, and `LATEST_AS_OF_FREEZE`; the last is never
called ground truth. BEA likewise states that true NIPA values cannot be
known and evaluates reliability through revision patterns
([Fixler, de Francisco, and Schaaf 2024](https://apps.bea.gov/scb/issues/2024/08-august/0824-revisions-to-gdp-gdi.htm)).

### Consequence for Poledna parity and model selection

The peer-reviewed Poledna et al. experiment remains the template for
recursive recalibration, multiple horizons, ABM Monte Carlo paths, RMSE
comparisons, and benchmark/inference tables. The paper explicitly states,
however, that its expanding-sample exercise used final-revised Eurostat data,
that vintage data would be preferable, and that genuine real-time evaluation
was left for future work. Its evidence and this project's analogous Stage-2
exercise are therefore labeled `FINAL_REVISED_PSEUDO_OUT_OF_SAMPLE`, never
real-time accuracy
([Poledna, Miess, Hommes, and Rabitsch 2023](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.euroecorev.2022.104306);
[official reproducibility-package record](https://www.oar-rao.bank-banque-canada.ca/record/1682?ln=en)).
The project also records
`model_selection_timing = FROZEN_BEFORE_EVALUATION |
RETROSPECTIVE_HINDSIGHT_SELECTED`; a hindsight-selected specification cannot
be relabeled as prospective performance.

### Consequence for `Other`, `Used`, unknown, and dubious fields

Three fields remain separate:

```text
source_observation_status
concept_match_status
transformation_review_status
```

The UN classification guidance requires categories to be clear, mutually
exclusive, exhaustive, and versioned; a source residual or “not elsewhere
classified” category is substantive, while vague responses should be coded
only to the supported hierarchy or left unidentifiable
([UNSD 2022 classification guidelines](https://unstats.un.org/unsd/classifications/bestpractices/Best_practice_Oct_2022.pdf)).
The SDMX observation-status vocabulary likewise separates a value from its
quality, unusual, provisional, break, or missing status
([SDMX `CL_OBS_STATUS`](https://sdmx.org/sdmx_cdcl/)). BEA's `Used` is a
native commodity concept—such as `S00402`, “Used and secondhand goods”—not an
unknown-data marker
([BEA Industry Economic Accounts tables](https://apps.bea.gov/scb/2018/08-august/pdf/0818-industry-tables.pdf)).

Accordingly, source `Other` is `SOURCE_RESIDUAL_PRESERVED`, native BEA `Used`
keeps its source-named concept, and an analyst's crosswalk gap becomes
`HIERARCHICAL_PARTIAL_MATCH`, `NO_EQUIVALENT_CATEGORY`,
`ANALYST_IMPUTED_MAPPING`, or `UNRESOLVED_CONCEPT`. A dubious transformation
uses a typed `DUBIOUS_<reason>` review status, is versioned and sensitivity
tested when possible, and is otherwise quarantined. No unknown is forced into
`Other`, zero, or a baseline category.

This literature decision changes the project vocabulary and claim ceilings;
it does not promote the HMI7 or RTDSM captures, create an origin, run a model,
or open a score. Counts remain **0 admitted origins** and **0/8
promotion-ready targets**.

## 2026-08-08 - Historical ABM structural look-ahead found before scoring

A read-only audit of the next revised-data ABM comparison path found that the
current `get_params_and_initial_conditions` helper selects annual structure
with

```text
year(min(calibration_date, max_calibration_date))-12-31
```

(`src/utils/calibration.jl`, current lines 765--768). Both inspected local
calibration objects report `max_calibration_date = 2024-12-31` and
`estimation_date = 1997-03-31`. Consequently, a requested 2024Q1, Q2, or Q3
origin selects the complete 2024 annual FIGARO/accounting cross-section. That
cross-section is dated after the quarterly origin; its historical release
availability is also unbound. Final-revised data permit later revisions to
observations that existed by the origin, but they do not permit an observation
period that had not yet occurred. The current helper therefore cannot support
even a clean `FINAL_REVISED_PSEUDO_OUT_OF_SAMPLE` label for those ABM origins.

The required repair is an explicit, receipt-bound structural-as-of selector:
each origin must use the latest annual structure whose observation period and
release timestamp are eligible at the declared cutoff. A deliberately
hindsight-selected structural sensitivity may remain separate under
`RETROSPECTIVE_HINDSIGHT_SELECTED`; it cannot enter the primary pseudo-
out-of-sample comparison. Quarterly dynamic histories must still end at the
origin, and structural age must be recorded for every model-origin.

This audit did not modify calibration code or objects, run a model, read
truth, or compute a score. It adds a prerequisite to the planned 2024Q1--
2025Q2 exploratory ABM comparison and prevents that exercise from being
mistaken for honest out-of-sample evidence. Counts remain **0 admitted
origins** and **0/8 promotion-ready targets**.

## 2026-08-08 - Small New Keynesian equilibrium benchmark design frozen in scope

A focused literature and implementation survey chose an isolated
three-observable linearized New Keynesian DSGE as the first executable
equilibrium challenger. Its eventual model class and panel are deliberately
narrow:

```text
model_class = small_new_keynesian_dsge
target_panel_id = quarterly_nk3_aggregate_pce_contract_v1
targets = real_gdp_growth, pce_inflation, effective_federal_funds_rate
```

This is an additive low-cost equilibrium benchmark, **not** a renamed version
of the existing backward-looking semi-structural LGSSM and **not** the
canonical Smets--Wouters/Poledna comparator. Poledna et al. use a modified
two-country Smets--Wouters/Breuss--Rabitsch system with 13 observables and
quarterly Bayesian re-estimation; Smets and Wouters' U.S. model itself uses
seven observables, seven structural shocks, and substantially richer nominal
and real frictions
([Smets and Wouters 2007](https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.97.3.586)). The full
Smets--Wouters and Poledna-parity workstream therefore remains open.

The selected small model follows the An--Schorfheide consumption Euler
equation, New Keynesian Phillips curve, and monetary-policy rule, with
technology-growth, government-spending/demand, and policy innovations. This
is a genuine rational-expectations equilibrium system that remains small
enough for a native, auditable Julia implementation
([An and Schorfheide 2007](https://doi.org/10.1080/07474930701220071),
[Herbst and Schorfheide 2012](https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2012/201211/index.html),
[pinned FRBNY equilibrium equations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FRBNY-DSGE/DSGE.jl/v1.3.0/src/models/representative/an_schorfheide/eqcond.jl)).
In quarterly log deviations its structural core is:

```text
y_t = E_t[y_(t+1)] + g_t - E_t[g_(t+1)]
      - tau^(-1) * (R_t - E_t[pi_(t+1)] - E_t[z_(t+1)])
pi_t = beta * E_t[pi_(t+1)] + kappa * (y_t - g_t)
R_t = rho_R*R_(t-1) + (1-rho_R)*psi_1*pi_t
      + (1-rho_R)*psi_2*(Delta y_t + z_t) + epsilon_R_t
z_t = rho_z*z_(t-1) + epsilon_z_t
g_t = rho_g*g_(t-1) + epsilon_g_t
```

Observed GDP growth is not substituted for the latent output gap. The
aggregate-PCE adaptation uses annualized quarter-over-quarter units:

```text
gdp_growth_t = 4 * (gamma_bar + y_t - y_(t-1) + z_t)
pce_inflation_t = pi_star + 4*pi_t
effr_t = pi_star + r_A + 4*gamma_bar + 4*R_t
beta^(-1) = 1 + r_A/400
```

The source model uses real GDP per capita and CPI. Aggregate GDP and PCE are
therefore a declared adaptation whose trend absorbs population/labor-force
growth; it cannot be called an exact An--Schorfheide replication. An exact
per-capita variant needs an origin-eligible population series. The
measurement identities are based on the
[pinned FRBNY measurement source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FRBNY-DSGE/DSGE.jl/v1.3.0/src/models/representative/an_schorfheide/measurement.jl).

The solver contract is the Sims generalized-Schur system
`Gamma0*s_t = Gamma1*s_(t-1) + C + Psi*epsilon_t + Pi*eta_t`. Complex QZ
roots are classified from `T_ii/S_ii` with a frozen `1e-6` exclusion band
around the unit circle; coincident zeros and numerically ambiguous roots are
rejected. Root counts or the Taylor principle alone are insufficient. The
implementation must apply the expectational-error subspace/SVD existence and
uniqueness tests and accept only `eu == [1,1]`, then verify finite effectively
real matrices, equation residuals, and the stationary reduced transition
([Sims 2002](https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1020517101123),
[FRBNY gensys documentation](https://frbny-dsge.github.io/DSGE.jl/v1.2/algorithms/)).
The mandatory external regression fixture is the official FRBNY v1.3.0
`AnSchorfheide()` `Gamma0/Gamma1/C/Psi/Pi -> G1/C/impact/eu` test, converted
once to reviewable hexadecimal Float64 text with both inputs and outputs
hashed
([official test](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FRBNY-DSGE/DSGE.jl/v1.3.0/test/solve/gensys.jl),
[official solver](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FRBNY-DSGE/DSGE.jl/v1.3.0/src/solve/gensys.jl)).

Three observables and three mutually independent structural shocks satisfy
the necessary shock-count condition, but not automatically full-rank
identification. Every likelihood evaluation must additionally require
positive shock scales, full numerical rank of the one-step innovation
covariance, exact Cholesky factorization without jitter, and finite Kalman
recursions. Base measurement error is exactly zero; no failure may silently
add noise. Any later measurement-error sensitivity is a separately versioned
model because fixed source-model errors are not automatically transportable
from per-capita GDP/CPI to aggregate GDP/PCE
([Fernandez-Villaverde, Rubio-Ramirez, and Schorfheide](https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w21862/w21862.pdf)).

Implementation is staged to keep mechanics separate from empirical evidence:

1. A fixed-parameter, unregistered component builds canonical matrices,
   solves QZ/gensys, constructs measurements, computes stationary moments,
   filters synthetic observations, propagates joint shock paths, and
   reproduces the frozen FRBNY fixture. Its maximum status is
   `FIXED_PARAMETER_DSGE_MECHANICS_VALIDATED_NO_EMPIRICAL_EVIDENCE`.
2. Before registration or scoring, an estimated successor must fit each
   origin independently from `y_train` only, with frozen normalized priors and
   Jacobians, four dispersed chains, bounded adaptive warm-up followed by a
   fixed proposal, rank-normalized folded split R-hat no greater than 1.01,
   and bulk/tail ESS of at least 400 for every parameter and named forecast
   functional. Failure at the sealed draw cap is visible, not repaired by
   retuning
   ([Vehtari et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1214/20-BA1221)).
3. Each retained parameter draw must resolve determinacy, refilter the
   origin-only sample, draw one terminal state and one coherent structural-
   shock path through the maximum horizon, and map that same path to all
   targets/horizons. Density semantics include parameter, terminal-state,
   and future-shock uncertainty, but exclude model-class, data-revision,
   stochastic-volatility, regime-switching, ELB, and measurement-error
   uncertainty in the base version.

The linear base model does not contain an effective-lower-bound mechanism,
shadow rate, pandemic volatility, outlier law, or unconventional-policy
block. It will retain all observations in a revised-data diagnostic and show
prespecified ELB and pandemic/reopening slices only as misspecification
diagnostics; no slice selects or repairs the primary model. Its eventual
comparison must use new panel-bound AR/VAR/BVAR variants on the identical
core-three data and origins. Comparing it with the existing eight-variable
VAR would instead confound equilibrium restrictions with different inputs.

The present 101-row revised/mixed-vintage panel can support mechanics and a
later descriptive comparison, but not pseudo-real-time accuracy or forecast
suitability. With a 60-quarter minimum it offers only 41/40/38/34/30
candidate origins at horizons 1/2/4/8/12, with 30 balanced through h=12;
none is currently an authenticated as-of origin. This design checkpoint did
not implement the solver, register a model, read truth, or compute a score.
Counts remain **0 admitted origins** and **0/8 promotion-ready targets**.

The [BEA GDP-by-industry and input-output archive metadata](https://apps.bea.gov/histdata/core/data/Fea_DisplayChildrenC/?HistMainId=8&getFiles=false&getDirs=true)
response was 40,651 bytes with SHA-256
`3ec9431c62fa419595f6acbe485c683adb1ebba67924862f5677271eb8d51a1e`.
Its own description states that input-output statistics were **not archived
before the January 23, 2014 release**, and that quarterly GDP-by-industry
archives begin with April 25, 2014. The response contained 73 dated release
directory leaves matching annual, advance, comprehensive, quarterly, or
benchmark labels across the included archive families. Earlier annual
GDP-by-industry directories do not substitute for the missing as-published
input-output component.

Consequently, the official HMI8 route cannot supply an archived I/O release
for the planned 2010Q2--2013Q4 paper-analogue origins. The earliest *possible*
strict origin for the I/O component is after January 23, 2014, and even that
is not an eligible origin until exact files, mappings, availability evidence,
and the other five structural components pass independently. This is an
evidence-driven sample-boundary change, not a decision to treat January 2014
as admitted.

The labor and firm-count routes have different but equally important vintage
limits. BLS exposes QCEW downloadable data back to 1975, but its
[program history](https://www.bls.gov/opub/hom/cew/history.htm) documents
irregular early releases, a 2018 split between the news release and full-data
update, and later process changes. The current
[QCEW release calendar](https://www.bls.gov/cew/release-calendar.htm) explains
that current-year full data are preliminary until the following first-quarter
release; current downloadable history therefore does not by itself identify
the bytes available at an older origin. Census states that SUSB is a
consistent annual series since 1988 but that its internet history is
incomplete and limited older data require a request
([SUSB data page](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/susb/data.html)); its
[download page](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/susb/data/datasets.All.html/page/1.html)
offers U.S. and state annual datasets from 1997 onward without establishing a
complete as-published release-time sequence.

No response was written under `data/us/raw`, no source event was added, and
the frozen current inventory remained byte-identical at
`110b4448db0b49e95cbc2fe1cf7019f6b877b3f391c6069a81c2e7c3c2a086ae`.
The practical next catalog pilot is therefore 2014-or-later, with exact
intraday event evidence and per-release bytes still required. Counts remain
**0 admitted origins** and **0/8 promotion-ready targets**.

## 2026-08-08 - First small-NK mechanics candidate rejected and repaired for re-audit

The first fixed-parameter small-New-Keynesian mechanics bundle was
independently **rejected** even though its root and unrelated-directory suites
both passed 83/83 and its official FRBNY numerical oracle was correct. The
rejected exact identities were module
`74107c486f296a9d330d521edd58a99c4d10da4c29644b1eeddff8ed5ec7359b`,
tests `8252eed472caec685c44903069742d6432ad659551c0f3f29a7f2adb764c61c4`,
fixture `ec0a4a891e49e518ab5e08b98fdeda6b828f1b611600a3ddf4e198d0c70bc89e`,
README `778472aa9ad24d66b7dbc1609e201cd0146b7dd74af106cfdae44c894d1e33ae`,
and notice
`27715239cbcea140f39752880985cbaa80ae3745ae8515d8a60bb45e4d13bbbc`.

The audit verified the difficult numerical core: complex-QZ root orientation,
Sims/FRBNY existence and uniqueness algebra, canonical equations, bitwise
HDF5-to-TOML conversion, six upstream source hashes and commit, the aggregate
GDP/PCE/EFFR measurement adaptation, stationary moments, the no-jitter Kalman
filter, and the BSD-3-Clause notice. Rejection instead exposed four contract
failures that the original tests missed:

1. the fixture's 13 parameter fields were not decoded and bit-bound to
   `reference_parameters()`, so five fields that do not affect the matrix
   oracle could drift silently;
2. the README's general scaling-invariance claim was false because
   Schur-zero, SVD-rank, and equation-residual cutoffs were absolute;
3. public downstream functions accepted indeterminate solutions, malformed
   filtered states, or swapped correlated/noisy measurements; and
4. the apparent cross-horizon RNG prefix held only for one path. With three
   paths, the path-outer draw order changed paths two and three when the
   requested horizon changed.

The repaired bundle is frozen as a new candidate pending a fresh independent
audit:

| Artifact | Repaired candidate SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `USSmallNKDSGEMechanics.jl` | `2750a95581ba83bdac8578ccdc2cd290a265fa1968d74ddc3d10cfc56e26248a` |
| `test_small_nk_dsge_mechanics.jl` | `89119bb52a1d0db424edb2214db72ac02a62ddb977fe3fe748586cfa27938076` |
| `frbny_gensys_reference.toml` | `ec0a4a891e49e518ab5e08b98fdeda6b828f1b611600a3ddf4e198d0c70bc89e` |
| `README.md` | `37f9f69fff367d33bd1097d2d5bc6bb50457bfe613ff5ebea29596e249fc7478` |
| `NOTICE.md` | `27715239cbcea140f39752880985cbaa80ae3745ae8515d8a60bb45e4d13bbbc` |

The solver now normalizes the entire finite canonical system once before QZ,
SVD, and residual checks. Uniform scales from `1e-12` through `1e12` reproduce
the same solution within `1e-12`; this is explicit whole-system normalization,
not a claim that arbitrary equation-by-equation rescaling is harmless. The
fixture loader enforces exact parameter and upstream-metadata keys, bit-checks
all 13 defaults, and binds its stake to exactly `1 + UNIT_ROOT_BAND`.

Shared validators now require determinate, finite, correctly shaped, strictly
stationary solutions; the sealed normalized residual; independent positive
structural shocks; zero measurement error; and finite positive-semidefinite
eight-state filter evidence with full-rank innovations at every public
operational boundary. Builders reject nonfinite derived matrices even when
their primitive parameters were finite. Predictive paths use a SHA-256
domain-separated Mersenne-Twister stream per path, so both horizon and
path-count prefixes hold for multi-path calls. The mechanics fingerprint now
binds the tolerance constants, fixture hash, state/shock/observable names,
upstream metadata, and RNG scheme; its repaired fixed identity is
`d45d4432c7e24bbe78e03c2953bd02cba52a89f942d45d9d6f11ad0fbc540e21`.

The expanded suite passed **224/224** from the repository root and **224/224**
from `/private/tmp`; Runic 1.7.0, diff, whitespace, regular-file, and link
checks passed. These are authored repair results, not an acceptance
disposition. The model remains unregistered, fixed-parameter, synthetic-only,
nonempirical, nonadmitting, and unsuitable for any accuracy claim pending
independent re-audit and later origin-wise estimation. Counts remain **0
admitted origins** and **0/8 promotion-ready targets**.

files. Files remained regular, single-linked, timestamp/inode/size stable,

The audit rederived rather than trusted the stored numerical evidence. It
matched all 18 upstream metadata fields, all 13 parameter IEEE-754 bit
patterns, and the exact `1 + 1e-6` stake. FRBNY-reference maximum deviations
were `3.464e-14` for `G1`, zero for the constant, and `3.642e-14` for impact;
the normalized source-system equation residual was `2.027e-15` with six
stable and two unstable roots. The adapted model had spectral radius `0.8`
and residual `5.393e-16`. Uniform whole-system scales from `1e-12` through
`1e12` preserved the six/two root count; maximum root drift was `4.476e-16`,
maximum solution-matrix drift `6.877e-16`, and maximum normalized residual
`1.011e-15`.

malformed, nonfinite, unstable, wrong-root/count/residual, noisy, correlated,

## 2026-08-08 - First core-three AR/VAR/BVAR candidate rejected; common-panel probe quarantined

The first isolated aggregate-PCE core-three autoregressive candidate was
independently **rejected**. Its frozen identities were module
`8b0dc0d9ccd7ec4186046d02d20d960c4692661a50a69daad6ad8627a5b5c014`,
tests `ffc385cc4f35003a97ba52358556f9e3d8fb6b3b25fb9c76f1e42a444da8e118`,
and README
`7922795c2bd1bf5558e5397755aaae97294d548f377a1b34319db9a7f82314fb`.
The frozen model-contract identities were AR(1)
`0d33cbebb614794097f31f215fe8dd628a85120c0a198d429216bc37af771842`,
VAR(1) `2860c9e0fe1e76e72e365cca1a93559d5adfb1b95755d27b3256ef48c987fc5c`,
and fixed-prior MNIW BVAR(1)
`32c9c0c6409f521ba2e919b7bc2b36bc8a47e5217c5aedc6b0bbe019b6470fd6`.

The difficult numerical mechanics were not the reason for rejection. Root and
unrelated-CWD suites each passed 272/272; all 303 selected values matched the
pinned eight-target CSV's real-GDP, aggregate-PCE, and EFFR columns bit for
bit; AR/VAR algebra agreed with an independent calculation within `3.0e-15`;
and the MNIW posterior, Cholesky orientation, first predictive path,
multi-path horizon/draw-count prefixes, and global-RNG isolation reproduced.
Unstable fitted means were also retained honestly rather than silently
truncated.

The decisive defect was an evidence-binding gap. A directly constructed
`Core3Sample` needed only to repeat the four expected source-hash strings;
validation did not prove that its quarter axis and training matrix were the
exact prefix of the pinned 101-by-3 panel. The auditor changed one training
cell by `+123` and, separately, supplied an unrelated 1980--1999 matrix while
retaining the pinned hashes. Both samples ran and their deterministically
replayed forecasts validated successfully. A local content hash therefore
authenticated neither the claimed source nor the information set. The
candidate is rejected even though every admission and accuracy Boolean was
false. The repair must reload the pinned panel before every revised-track
execution and bit-compare the exact prefix, origin, and following forecast
labels; coordinated self-rehashing must not help.

Before that audit result arrived, a read-only engineering probe combined the
candidate's normal `revised_core3_sample` constructor with the independently
accepted fixed-parameter small-NK mechanics. All four models received the
same three-column training prefix in this exact order:

```text
real_gdp_growth, pce_inflation, effective_federal_funds_rate
```

No future value was passed to any model. Realized values were copied only
after all forecasts existed and used in a separate temporary scoring loop.
At the 2022Q3 origin, for 2022Q4--2025Q3, the descriptive 12-quarter RMSE
vectors were:

| Historical engineering result only | Real GDP growth | PCE inflation | EFFR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| fixed-parameter small NK | 25.711 | 0.953 | 0.805 |
| univariate AR(1) | 1.596 | 0.748 | 3.133 |
| OLS VAR(1) | 1.628 | 0.757 | 3.004 |
| fixed-prior MNIW BVAR(1) | 1.637 | 0.837 | 3.079 |

A balanced 30-origin expanding-window probe used origins 2015Q2--2022Q3 and
outcomes through 2025Q3. Its horizon-one and pooled-across-horizons RMSEs
were:

| Historical engineering result only | h1 GDP | h1 PCE | h1 EFFR | pooled GDP | pooled PCE | pooled EFFR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| fixed-parameter small NK | 59.226 | 1.817 | 1.894 | 29.142 | 2.204 | 2.625 |
| univariate AR(1) | 12.736 | 1.715 | 0.493 | 9.635 | 2.269 | 2.219 |
| OLS VAR(1) | 12.984 | 2.488 | 0.681 | 9.588 | 2.962 | 2.961 |
| fixed-prior MNIW BVAR(1) | 10.429 | 2.143 | 0.519 | 8.684 | 2.406 | 2.156 |

These values are deliberately quarantined from the accuracy tables. They use
final-revised, mixed-vintage data; the AR/VAR/BVAR software bundle was later
rejected; there is no immutable score artifact; and there is no admitted
origin. Their disclosure also fixes
`model_selection_timing = RETROSPECTIVE_HINDSIGHT_EVALUATION_DESIGN_EXPOSED`
for any successor that uses this same panel and evaluation window; repairing
software without changing numerical model specifications cannot restore
blinding. They do, however, identify a modeling hazard to retain in the next
design. With zero measurement error, the fixed small-NK filter carried the
extreme pandemic state forward and produced implausibly negative GDP-growth
forecasts long after 2020. The largest statistical-model GDP errors likewise
clustered in 2020Q2--Q3. Full-sample results must therefore remain primary,
with pre-pandemic, acute-pandemic, and post-pandemic slices frozen as
sensitivities before any accepted scores are opened; the equilibrium
benchmark must not be promoted on theoretical pedigree alone.

No result in this section is an admitted forecast, accepted score, superiority
finding, or suitability claim. Counts remain **0 admitted origins** and **0/8
promotion-ready targets**.

The verifier safely reopens and reconstructs the complete evidence closure.
It exact-compares legacy and active profile identities, source and capture
bindings, rank-one catalog selection, release and selected locators,
reference/capture/catalog/resolution chronology, raw/replica bytes and hashes,

approvals, and all downstream hard-false gates. `validate_result` requires an
explicit evidence root, replays the complete parent, and exact-compares the
result; it is not a local self-hash checker.

Resource and filesystem checks are part of the accepted narrow behavior.
Parent-wide metadata preflight occurs before raw or replica reads. The policy
freezes 16 MiB metadata/token, 512 MiB individual raw/replica, 1/2 GiB
per-profile raw/replica, and 64/128 GiB parent ceilings with overflow-safe
addition. Exact integer typing rejects Boolean and floating aliases. Relative
paths, roots, ancestors, regular files, inodes, objects, and replica identities
are checked; traversal, symlinks, hard links, reused objects, root replacement,
and internal races fail closed. These checks are not kernel-atomic protection
against a malicious same-user process, so that attestation remains false.

Independent adversarial probes rejected a coordinated `READY` restamp
(`gate_elevation`), integer-overflow result (`resource_limit`), changed child
with reused custody (`binding_mismatch`), stale result
(`result_replay_mismatch`), unsafe paths and links, type aliases, oversized
tokens, and root/internal mutations. A fully rebuilt, self-consistent metadata
closure can validate structurally, but only as `CANNOT_RUN` with
`current_v3_authenticated_trust_roots_absent`. This is the intended exact
ceiling: local hashes, opaque signature references, hashed timestamp tokens,
and a caller-supplied `PROSPECTIVE_NONSYNTHETIC` label do not authenticate
provenance.

The missing successor trust layer must pin accepted keys, anchors, and actual
signature/timestamp validators. [NIST FIPS 186-5](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/186-5/final),
[NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Revision 5](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/57/pt1/r5/final),
and [RFC 3161](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc3161/) describe relevant
digital-signature, key-management, and timestamp-authority boundaries; v3
claims no conformance to them and implements no substitute cryptography.

EFFR remains a blocking overlay rather than a semantic alias. Restart geometry
is exactly 58 morning observations, 57 later observations, 115 total slots,
and 57 complete pairs, while all three supersession decisions remain
`UNAVAILABLE_NOT_FROZEN`. The missing August 7 later observation, unjustified
daily-history start, insufficient 84-business-day model history, and unmodeled
March 2016 methodology boundary cannot be borrowed or relabelled. First-public,
raw `currentState`, final-state, and no-later-revision claims remain false.

Retention is correctly derived from the h12 target: 2029Q3 ends
`2029-09-30T23:59:59Z`; adding 60 months gives
`2034-09-30T23:59:59Z`. Deletion additionally requires later completion,
external timestamping, durable replication, and independent audit of the last
mature-truth receipt. The verifier checks that covenant without opening future
truth.

than silently substituting net stock or depreciation for investment.

The latest page-visible finalized HMI11 release is the September 26, 2025
annual update, directory ID `14195`, with internal path
`/Inetpub/wwwroot/website/website/HistData/Files/Releases/FA\2024\AnnualUpdate_September-26-2025`.
The [official HMI11 release page](https://apps.bea.gov/histdata/fileStructDisplay.html?theID=14195&HMI=11&oldDiv=National%20Accounts&year=2024&quarter=&ReleaseDate=September-26-2025&Vintage=AnnualUpdate)
and [Fixed Assets landing page](https://www.bea.gov/itable/fixed-assets)
identify that release and its 2020--2024 update span. The future 2026 annual-
update directory ID, internal path, release date, and member names are not yet
published or resolved and must not be guessed.

Exact historical member casing also remains unresolved. The current mutable
download interface exposes `Section3All_xls.xlsx`,
`Section5All_xls.xlsx`, and `Section7All_xls.xlsx`; historical examples often
use `ALL`, but the 2025 HMI11 `Filearray3` response body was not preserved.
Consequently a release-scoped URL ending in `Section3ALL_xls.xlsx` or
`Section3All_xls.xlsx` is only a candidate until exact files metadata is
captured. Ordinary official-page navigation caused the archive UI to issue its
own metadata XHR, but the survey did not preserve that response body and made
no direct workbook, ZIP, TXT, API-data, HEAD, Range, or raw-data request.

The fail-closed HMI11 discovery sequence is now explicit:

1. preserve the exact root response from
   `Fea_DisplayChildrenC/?HistMainId=11&getFiles=false&getDirs=true`, including
   `MainName`, `FolderPattern`, and every `FileArray` entry;
2. resolve the selected exact internal path through `UrlPath_getID`, requiring
   one record and a decimal `Theid`;
3. reverse-resolve that ID through `getPath/<id>` and require literal path
   equality;
4. preserve `Fea_DisplayChildrenC/?HistMainId=11&thePath=<encoded-path>&getFiles=true&getDirs=false`
   and treat its case-sensitive `Filearray3` as the file-name authority; and
5. derive an official URL only for an exact child of the selected release,
   percent-encode each path component, require HTTPS on exact host
   `apps.bea.gov`, and preserve the requested and final effective URIs.

This establishes catalog membership, not bytes. HEAD is at most routing
evidence and may behave differently from GET; Range retrieves source bytes.
Neither can replace the exact body hash. The current credential-free mutable
routes are the official [Section 3](https://apps.bea.gov/national/FixedAssets/Release/XLS/Section3All_xls.xlsx),
[Section 5](https://apps.bea.gov/national/FixedAssets/Release/XLS/Section5All_xls.xlsx),
[Section 7](https://apps.bea.gov/national/FixedAssets/Release/XLS/Section7All_xls.xlsx),
[all-sections ZIP](https://apps.bea.gov/national/FixedAssets/Release/ZIP/FixedAssets.zip),
[text file](https://apps.bea.gov/national/FixedAssets/Release/TXT/FixedAssets.txt),
and [flat-files ZIP](https://apps.bea.gov/national/FixedAssets/Release/TXT/FlatFiles.ZIP).
They are current mutable locators, not immutable HMI11 release evidence.

The API alternative is also unsuitable for exact-byte origin capture in the
current pipeline. The official [BEA API guide](https://apps.bea.gov/api/_pdf/bea_web_service_api_user_guide.pdf)
requires one FixedAssets `TableName` per request, hence eight responses. The
API echoes `UserID`, while `USPipeline.jl` replaces that credential with
`[REDACTED:BEA_API_KEY]` before hashing and storage. The stored bytes therefore
are not the transport body. `Frequency=A` is not a FixedAssets request
parameter, and existing diagnostics expose a `UNIT_MULT="6"` versus published
billions description that requires an explicit workbook-unit and
billions-to-millions transform receipt.

BEA's [Open Data page](https://www.bea.gov/open-data),
[linking/public-domain policy](https://www.bea.gov/about/policies-and-information/linking),
[FAQ 145](https://www.bea.gov/help/faq/145), and
[posting-content policy](https://www.bea.gov/about/policies-and-information/priorities-and-schedules-posting-content)
provide publisher, reuse, attribution, and schedule context. They do not prove
an exact file's intraday availability. API terms do not automatically govern
the direct-file route; capture-time page and file notices must be preserved
separately.

The implementation choice is therefore a new offline HMI11 discovery/profile
validator followed later by a set-valued, release-scoped three-workbook
capture. It must preserve all discovery responses and all three workbook
bodies, resolve every profile by exact table/sheet/year/row and literal units,
store raw literals plus typed transforms, and reconstruct selector receipts
from raw bytes. The future common-origin schema must represent three physical
objects once and permit the intentional 3/3/2 profile references; duplicating
one workbook into eight invented objects is not evidence independence.

Current decision: mutable locator discovery **GO**; present directory/ID
resolution **GO**; exact historical member URLs **NO-GO**; future 2026 release
identity **NO-GO**; current API exact-byte path **NO-GO**; live prospective
acquisition now **NO-GO**; admission, model use, promotion, and scoring
**NO-GO**. Counts remain **0/8 qualified fixed-assets profiles**, **0 admitted
origins**, and **0/8 promotion-ready targets**.

### First HMI11 discovery implementation rejected at its public replay boundary

The first isolated HMI11 implementation was independently audited and
**REJECTED** despite reproducing its authored mechanics. Its exact rejected
identities are:

| module | `7da6084e16b563fecdd0fef3cda81548aafc4d307ee674f39e2690b8e7f8a136` |

| tests | `5eaf16b144599299fddbb964a4c933208291fcfa69b4fb57fd6cbfdd464c6ced` |
| README | `bad0aa1ecdb62157cb88b52c14d1affbe153d2100432f3f2b01bf4876ed41495` |

The strict root and unrelated-CWD suites each passed 173/173; all twelve
physical pins and six applicable semantic pins matched; the eight selectors
and 3/3/2 table mapping matched prospective v2; and the valid-input JSON,
release ranking, path encoding and file-case mechanics agreed with the
accepted HMI7 pattern. The module remained stdlib-only, offline, nonwriting,
and its normal builder returned `CANNOT_RUN`. Those positive facts are retained
only as rejected engineering evidence.

Four public-boundary defects defeated acceptance:

1. exported directory/file URL helpers encoded arbitrary paths. They produced
   official-looking HMI11 URLs for `/outside`, and the file helper accepted an
   HMI7 release because it checked only the broad `HistData` root;
2. the workbook parser trusted a caller-constructed `ReleaseDirectory` and
   accepted a forged `\2098\not-a-release` directory rather than replaying the
   canonical HMI11 release grammar and fields;
3. public default constructors permitted a fabricated `DiscoveryPlan` with
   `READY`, `PRODUCTION`, and true gates, while no result validator rebuilt and
   exactly compared the plan; and
4. the builder accepted four naked bodies without binding each one to its
   derived requested/effective URI, response role, order, or selected
   path/ID lineage. Body-text equality alone was labelled a reverse-path check.

The repair must narrow the public API, validate the canonical selected release
at every URL and parser boundary, require exact-child file derivation, bind
typed response envelopes to their request/effective URIs and lineage, and
strictly replay the complete plan. Until a repaired candidate passes a fresh
independent audit, the HMI11 route remains design-only: **0/8 qualified**, no
capture authorization, no current member-case evidence, no origin admission,
and no model use.

## 2026-08-08 - BLS CPS six-profile survey: release event and final structural snapshot must remain separate

A read-only repository and official-source survey resolved the acquisition
boundary for the six `bls_cps_structural` profiles. It made no API or static-
data request and wrote no raw evidence. The inspected local bindings remained:

The exact profiles are:

| Profile | Series | Native concept |
|---|---|---|
| `cps_population` | `LNU00000000` | civilian noninstitutional population, monthly NSA, thousands |
| `cps_labor_force` | `LNU01000000` | civilian labor force, monthly NSA, thousands |
| `cps_employed` | `LNU02000000` | employed, monthly NSA, thousands |
| `cps_unemployed` | `LNU03000000` | unemployed, monthly NSA, thousands |
| `cps_inactive` | `LNU05000000` | not in labor force, monthly NSA, thousands |
| `cps_unemployment_rate` | `LNS14000000` | civilian unemployment rate, monthly SA, percent |

The [CPS data page](https://www.bls.gov/cps/data.htm) identifies the LN
database, series reports, series-ID list, and flat files. BLS's
[definitions](https://www.bls.gov/cps/definitions.htm) establish the population
and labor-force partitions and say CPS annual averages use NSA data. The SA
unemployment rate remains a distinct published statistic governed by the
[CPS seasonal-adjustment methodology](https://www.bls.gov/cps/seasonal-adjustment-methodology.htm);
it must not be reconstructed from the five NSA counts.

The official [Employment Situation schedule](https://www.bls.gov/schedule/news_release/empsit.htm)
currently places the September 2026 release at October 2, 2026, 08:30 New York
time (`2026-10-02T12:30:00Z`). The schedule is mutable and must be revalidated.
More importantly, BLS's [API feature page](https://www.bls.gov/bls/api_features.htm)
documents a one-day lag between publication and API availability. An API
response at 12:30Z therefore cannot prove that September observations were
available at the release instant. A stale response would have to be preserved
without retry and could not be relabelled.

The local contract independently forbids substituting that fixed event. All
six structural profiles use capture ID `final_structural_pre_origin` with no
override, whose window is `2026-10-29T13:30:00Z` through
`2026-10-30T13:45:00Z`, before the 14:00Z origin. The October 2 Employment
Situation bundle is separate target-release evidence; the late-October CPS
database state is the structural snapshot. One October 2 response cannot
satisfy both roles.

The exact API endpoint is
`POST https://api.bls.gov/publicAPI/v2/timeseries/data/`. BLS's
[API FAQ](https://www.bls.gov/developers/api_faqs.htm) limits unregistered
access to 25 daily queries, 25 series per query, and ten years per query;
registered v2 allows 500, 50, and 20 respectively. All six IDs fit in one
request, but their provider-complete history does not. The selector currently
fixes only a terminal month, not a begin period, so choosing an arbitrary
start would be silent truncation.

The recommended secret-free capture set is eight exact unregistered queries,
each issued once, for the same ordered six IDs over 1948--1957, 1958--1967,
1968--1977, 1978--1987, 1988--1997, 1998--2007, 2008--2017, and 2018--2026.
In the same transaction preserve the official LN catalog/lookup files
`ln.series`, `ln.footnote`, `ln.seasonal`, `ln.periodicity`, `ln.lfst`,
`ln.ages`, `ln.tdat`, and `ln.txt` from the
[official LN directory](https://download.bls.gov/pub/time.series/ln/). The
adapter must first derive each true begin period from `ln.series`, then prove
no gap, overlap, duplicate `(series,year,period)`, wrong seasonal code, unit,
frequency, universe, or missing terminal `2026/M09`. `M13` annual averages are
separate from monthly completeness.

This is necessarily a selected **object set**, not one artifact. Current
common-origin v3 permits JSON/CSV only and selects one `raw_artifact_id` per
leaf. It cannot honestly encode eight API chunks plus catalogs or the shared
one-object/many-profile flat-file alternative. A successor must own each raw
object and its replicas once in a parent catalog, rank one closed object-set
candidate, bind ordered `selected_object_ids`, and attach six exact profile
projections with no-gap/no-overlap proofs.

The very large `ln.data.1.AllData` static file is a useful independent
completeness cross-check, but not the first operational path. The observed
directory listing described it as about 389 MB and `ln.series` as about
15 MB; those mutable size labels are not preserved identities. The transfer
has greater exactly-once failure risk, an uncertain atomic-update boundary,
and likely TSV/plain-text media not allowed by v3. It may be added only under a
bounded, separately accepted parser and media policy.

Current `USPipeline.jl` is not prospective evidence machinery. It permits
retries, uses arbitrary 1996-based chunks, omits `catalog=true`, accepts broad
success shapes, uses ordinary duplicate-losing JSON parsing, lacks body/depth/
collection ceilings, stores one local body, does not preserve all footnotes,
has no durable no-retry journal/quarantine/replica/selector/timestamp/approval/
custody closure, and interpolates the published-missing October 2025
unemployment rate downstream. The July rehearsal is also fixed to two series,
one past window, and polling. Neither can be relabelled as the final adapter.

Missing values and revisions remain typed source facts. BLS's
[2025 shutdown methodology](https://www.bls.gov/cps/methods/2025-federal-government-shutdown-impact-cps.htm)
states that October 2025 CPS data were not collected, 2025 annual averages use
11 months, and a reliable 2025Q4 estimate could not be produced. The `-` value
and footnote 9 are missing, never zero or interpolated. The
[March 2026 population-control revision](https://www.bls.gov/cps/notices/2026/population-control-revision-2026.htm)
and [April 2025 corrections](https://www.bls.gov/bls/errata/cps-corrections-april-2025.htm)
also prove that captured histories are database state as of receipt, not
historical first-public states. Raw footnotes, seasonal state, correction
notices, and capture time must be retained.

Operational capture needs the accepted single-object envelope's time gates,
no-retry journal, invalid-response quarantine, response-header validation,
fsynced/reread copies, and link rejection, extended by one transaction-wide
set controller and two genuinely independent durable storage domains. Exact
six-series membership, empty BLS message vector, bounded duplicate-safe JSON
and TSV parsing, catalog reconciliation, terminal-month evidence, and
independent receipt reconstruction are mandatory. Any partial transport,
non-200, nonempty message, stale terminal period, invalid body, or catalog
drift ends in quarantine without retry.

BLS's [copyright guidance](https://www.bls.gov/opub/copyright-information.htm),
[API terms](https://www.bls.gov/developers/termsOfService.htm), and
[automated-retrieval policy](https://www.bls.gov/bls/blsterms.htm) require
source citation, access-date/post-retrieval disclaimer, no emblem misuse,
official hostnames, and restrained coordinated traffic. They do not
authenticate future bytes, time, storage, or operator identity.

Decision: offline adapter and set-controller design **GO**; live capture now
**NO-GO**; a single release-time response **NO-GO**; final multi-artifact
transaction **YES IN PRINCIPLE**; current dispatch qualification **NO-GO**;
origin admission, inventory mutation, scoring, and promotion **NO-GO**. Counts
remain **0/6 qualified CPS profiles**, **0 admitted origins**, and **0
origin-aligned comparison cells**.

#### Official-documentation survey confirms that the LN layout ceiling is real

A separate official-source survey made no data/API/catalog-body request and
confirmed that the accepted adapter must not guess its way past the remaining
ceiling. The [CPS data page](https://www.bls.gov/cps/data.htm) describes the
LN series list as tab-delimited and links the flat-file collection, but does
not freeze the 2026 header names, order, encoding, BOM, line endings, blank
lines, trailing fields, whitespace, row widths, or extra columns. BLS explains
through its [flat-file documentation
practice](https://www.bls.gov/opub/hom/soii/presentation.htm) that each survey
directory's `.txt` file supplies the series/mapping formats and data-element
dictionary. For LN, that authority is the live, mutable `ln.txt` object in the
[LN directory](https://download.bls.gov/pub/time.series/ln/)—one of the eight
objects that still must be captured.

The HTML evidence supports only partial semantics. `series_id`,
`series_title`, and begin/end fields have documented analogues, and a generic
BLS catalog example uses `periodicity_code`. It does not establish raw LN
columns named `seasonal_code`, `tdat_code`, `lfst_code`, or `ages_code`.
Another program's [LABSTAT
guide](https://www.bls.gov/cex/labstat/ce-labstat-getting-started-guide.htm)
uses raw `seasonal` and establishes only a program-specific ASCII/tab/header
convention, while the separate [API JSON
contract](https://www.bls.gov/developers/api_signature_v2.htm) uses
`seasonality`. None proves LN's physical bytes. The same applies to the seven
lookup/text objects: code/text roles may be plausible, but exact headers,
order, grammar and labels are unknown. Directory modification times differ,
so directory co-location is not an atomic publisher snapshot.

The next reviewed version therefore requires an eight-body, metadata-only
prospective transaction. Each complete response must be preserved twice
without normalization and bind requested/effective URI, redirect policy,
times, duplicate-preserving headers, status, size and hash. Its receipt must
record BOM/ASCII predicates, LF/CRLF/CR counts, final terminator, blank-line
ordinals, tab counts, exact header bytes/order, row widths, trailing fields,
whitespace, duplicates and all code-label bytes; then parse captured `ln.txt`
and compare its declared format against each physical object. A separate
mapping receipt may map proven provider names to internal aliases. HEAD or a
directory listing cannot close this gap, and the accepted synthetic candidate
must not be restamped after the fact.

The directory timestamp is a mutable server listing without an evidenced time
zone, not an authenticated release timestamp. The official table page and
[AIES press release](https://www.census.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026/main-release-of-aies-data.html)
identify February 26, 2026 as the main-release date. They do not prove that a
specific later-retrieved ZIP is byte-identical to the first release. The
[AIES FAQ](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/aies/faq.html) explicitly
instructs users to download the ZIP and open its `.dat` member. That resolves
the route and expected packaging, but the required exact member name, CRC,
body hash, row universe, and literal fields still have to be captured and
rederived from the preserved bytes.

The current five-profile selector is materially consistent with the official
product partition: AIES00 carries receipts and total inventories; AIES31,
AIES42, and AIES44 carry total, LIFO, and LIFO-reserve inventory statistics;
and AIES51 carries total, finished-goods, work-in-process, and materials
inventories. The official release describes the AIES universe as domestic,
private-sector, nonfarm employer businesses in the nineteen in-scope 2017
NAICS sectors. This is not the whole economy and must not be relabelled as
government, farm, or nonemployer coverage. Values, flags, CVs, and CV flags
must remain separate typed fields; suppression or estimate flags may not be
coerced to zero or silently imputed.

The SUSB direct locator already present in `sources.toml` is also exact:
[`us_state_6digitnaics_2022.txt`](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/susb/tables/2022/us_state_6digitnaics_2022.txt).
The official [2022 SUSB dataset page](https://www.census.gov/data/datasets/2022/econ/susb/2022-susb.html)
labels it the complete U.S.-and-states, six-digit-NAICS file by enterprise
employment size, using 2017 NAICS, and records disclosure-review approval.
The [2007-present record layout](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/susb/technical-documentation/record_layout_us_and_state_2007_to_present.txt)
defines `STATE`, `NAICS`, `ENTRSIZE`, `FIRM`, `ESTB`, `EMPL`, payroll,
receipts, descriptions, and suppression/noise flags; `STATE=00` is the U.S.
geography. The project selector correctly needs every published `ENTRSIZE`
code, not only code `01`. The existing `collect_susb!` therefore remains
semantically incomplete because it keeps only `STATE=00, ENTRSIZE=01` and
drops the size distribution and published flag surface.

The SUSB page also demonstrates why a locator is not an immutable origin
artifact. It records a July 22, 2025 correction to a different 2022 MSA
dataset and says the remaining estimates were unchanged. That notice supports
the current U.S.-and-states object's scope, but not its first-public bytes or
availability time. A prospective capture must preserve the dataset page,
record layout, direct body, response metadata, and any contemporaneous errata,
then verify all U.S. rows, all published size codes, uniqueness, additivity,
suppression/noise flags, and the required `FIRM/ESTB/EMPL` projections.

The public-use review removes the earlier blanket assertion that Census data
retrieval is wholly unreviewed, while retaining a strict evidence ceiling.
Census's [Open Government page](https://www.census.gov/about/policies/open-gov.html)
states that its public data are open data available for public use and reuse,
and its [citation policy](https://www.census.gov/about/policies/citation.html)
requires source, file/table, vintage, URL, and access date and makes the
analyst responsible for derived conclusions. The separate
[Data API terms](https://www.census.gov/data/developers/about/terms-of-service.html)
permit retrieval and analysis, prohibit re-identification and false
representation, require a no-endorsement notice for API products, and reserve

direct-file transaction. Capture-time website policies and file notices must
still be preserved, requests must be restrained, and the local review remains
a research-policy assertion rather than legal advice or publisher approval.

recheck; API substitution is **NO-GO** because it requires a key and changes
the source object; live acquisition now is **NO-GO**; current common-origin

### Census logical-schema audit resolves semantics and exposes selector collisions

A follow-up official-documentation audit made no ZIP, TXT, CSV, or Census API
data request. Its result is **6/6 logical schemas resolved, 0/6 physical
layouts qualified**. The exact AIES ZIP member names, CRCs, delimiter,
encoding/BOM, header bytes/order/case, quoting, newlines, null lexemes, row
order and membership remain body facts. The SUSB record layout documents
comma delimiting and logical fields, but its physical header, encoding,
newlines, blanks, nulls, row order and the presence of the discontinued
`EMPLFL_R` column likewise require the actual body.

The current AIES selectors omit dimensions needed for unique national rows.
All five require the common structural fields
`GEO_ID,GEO_ID_F,INDLEVEL,NAICS,NAICS_F,NAICS_LABEL,NAME,SECTOR,YEAR`.
The additive repairs are:

| Profile | Additional required dimensions/labels |
|---|---|
| `AIES00INV` | `TAXSTAT,TAXSTAT_LABEL,TYPOP,TYPOP_LABEL` plus all common labels |
| `AIES31INV` | the common geography/code labels |
| `AIES42INV` | `TYPOP,TYPOP_LABEL` plus common labels |
| `AIES44INV` | `INDGROUP,SUBSECTOR` plus common labels |
| `AIES51INV` | `TAXSTAT,TAXSTAT_LABEL` plus common labels |

This is not optional metadata. `AIES00INV` needs candidate key
`(GEO_ID,YEAR,NAICS,TYPOP,TAXSTAT)`, `AIES42INV` needs
`(GEO_ID,YEAR,NAICS,TYPOP)`, and `AIES51INV` needs
`(GEO_ID,YEAR,NAICS,TAXSTAT)`; the others use
`(GEO_ID,YEAR,NAICS)`. Without `GEO_ID`, the asserted U.S. geography cannot be
rederived; without `TYPOP`, wholesale rows collide. The exact field families,
types and labels are documented in the official group dictionaries for
[`AIES00INV`](https://api.census.gov/data/timeseries/aies/inv/groups/AIES00INV.html),
[`AIES31INV`](https://api.census.gov/data/timeseries/aies/miscsector/groups/AIES31INV.html),
[`AIES42INV`](https://api.census.gov/data/timeseries/aies/miscsector/groups/AIES42INV.html),
[`AIES44INV`](https://api.census.gov/data/timeseries/aies/miscsector/groups/AIES44INV.html),
and [`AIES51INV`](https://api.census.gov/data/timeseries/aies/miscsector/groups/AIES51INV.html).
Every value must retain its value flag, CV and CV flag; `D`, `N`, `S`, `Z`,
`v`, and `w` are typed publication states, never zero-fill instructions. The
[2023 AIES methodology](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/aies/technical-documentation/methodology/2023-aies-methodology.pdf)
also fixes the company/firm reporting unit and private-sector nonfarm employer
universe.

The SUSB audit confirms the canonical file name
`us_state_6digitnaics_2022.txt` and the exact documented logical fields
`STATE,NAICS,ENTRSIZE,FIRM,ESTB,EMPL,EMPLFL_R,EMPLFL_N,PAYR,PAYRFL_N,RCPT,RCPTFL_N,STATEDSCR,NAICSDSCR,ENTRSIZEDSCR`
from the official [record
layout](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/susb/technical-documentation/record_layout_us_and_state_2007_to_present.txt).
The [enterprise-size
codes](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/susb/technical-documentation/enterprise_codes_2017.txt)
are overlapping: `01` total; disjoint bins `02,03,04,06,07,09`; subtotal
`05=02+03+04`; subtotal `08=05+06+07`. Therefore `ALL_PUBLISHED_CODES`
means retain and hash every observed `STATE=00` row whose code is in `01:09`;
it never means sum all nine. The model's current `ENTRSIZE=01` view may be a
separately hashed total-only projection, but cannot replace the all-code raw
view or the acquisition contract.

A second SUSB issue is model-material. The 2022 product assigns establishments
to establishment industries and classifies size by enterprise employment.
One enterprise can own establishments in several industries, so `FIRM` is not
an additive unique-enterprise count across model NAICS rows; the current
`susb_sum(..., :firms)` can double-count a multi-industry enterprise. Census's
[SUSB glossary](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/susb/about/glossary.html)
and [methodology](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/susb/technical-documentation/methodology.html)
support treating it only as an `industry_firm_presences` proxy unless an
allocation/deduplication ontology is validated. `ESTB`, `EMPL`, `PAYR`, and
`RCPT` are more naturally additive only over mutually exclusive NAICS rows,
with hierarchical-overlap and suppression/noise controls. `S`-flagged numeric
zero is a withheld unknown included in broader totals, not an observed zero.

Implementation consequence: revise the five AIES selectors additively before
writing a parser; retain all SUSB size rows and derive the total-only view by
lineage; preserve raw lexemes/flags and enforce the profile-specific keys; and
add SUSB firm-count nonadditivity sensitivity to the eventual forecasting
report. Exact physical qualification still requires the six bodies and their
documentation snapshots through the prospective object-set envelope. No
semantic resolution changes the current **0/6 physical qualification** or
zero-origin state.
