## 2026-08-08 - Authenticated common-origin v4 trust design: implementation GO, readiness NO-GO

A read-only trust-boundary audit examined the accepted
`common_origin_acquisition_v3`, its Julia environment, the required 21/107
closure, and the two already-known shared-object cases. It changed no source,
inventory, raw evidence, key, signature, timestamp request, or timestamp
response. The exact v3 identities remained module
`9654eb61b92b2655391b00952ed4cbee0e9fa58224339f1fb0440c51570e719e`,
policy
`0deff5e3e6c950b5682bba96fcefa1fa2304bbbadae6227a940376dc7699bd3e`,
parent schema
`cf4060554a6c53de079d728c2a2ac179309e9a7b888edc3bfa0a931ced5442a2`,
leaf schema
`6bcd6f26efba67bb92053dabdc20c08f6b36d9c3569a92a5e980c5117265a4cd`,
custody schema
`94eb2a1bdbd1346b4918d63bdf1befcf506a8b6d39c6eeaa1b50e87eb2c79598`,
tests
`e3ee90a943e26fd6ce5db37644035c4dff3edfdb1f364921ea1353e782cded53`,
and README
`a93226a2fed8bf25d611472483b46a15dfa8c695853026439cd5e9dd0323b631`.
Its strict suite again passed 223/223. It remains permanently `CANNOT_RUN`:
all 21 dispatches covering 107 profiles are unqualified, all three EFFR
supersession decisions are unavailable, and its signature strings and token
hashes are explicitly unauthenticated metadata.

The minimum honest successor is a separately versioned v4 with an immutable
trust bootstrap provisioned outside both repository and evidence tree; an
exact role-key registry; detached ECDSA P-256/SHA-256 verification over
reconstructed domain-separated, typed, length-prefixed binary subjects; and
one RFC 3161 timestamp over the complete signed origin closure. A local
self-hash, nonempty signature field, timestamp-token hash, self-signed trust
update, or caller claim of nonsynthetic provenance can never elevate status.

NIST states that digital signatures can authenticate a signatory and detect
modification, while algorithm selection alone does not establish an
implementation's standards conformance
([FIPS 186-5](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/186-5/final)); the curve
parameters are specified separately in
[SP 800-186](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/186/final)). NIST's
[SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/57/pt1/r5/final)
makes trust-anchor authenticity foundational and requires explicit key
lifecycle, compromise, revocation, and verification-period semantics. The
bootstrap must therefore pin governance, model-owner, independent-validator,
and custody-operator SPKI identities, active/retired/revoked/compromised
states, role and origin scopes, registry epoch/predecessor, TSA roots and
policy, and the accepted verifier release. Governance-root rotation requires
a separately accepted bootstrap/release; an in-band cross-signature is not a
new root of trust.

The canonical signed subject must not be TOML text or a bare hexadecimal
label. The proposed envelope has a fixed ASCII domain, schema and field count,
closed field IDs/order, one-byte type tags, unsigned 64-bit big-endian lengths,
raw 32-byte hashes, ASCII-only identifiers, and canonical times. Every
signature binds subject kind, origin ID/time, v4 policy/schema/release
identities, trust-registry epoch/content, evidence-material hash, role,
signer/key, closed decision, and all zero-truth/model/scoring gates. Stored
subject bytes must equal a fresh reconstruction before signature verification.

The final `origin_evidence_closure_v1` is constructed only after raw evidence,
leaf results, custody manifests, owner signature, and validator signature.
Its RFC 3161 request must preserve exact DER, SHA-256 imprint, nonce, requested
TSA policy, and `certReq=true`; the response must preserve exact DER,
certificates, chain, and frozen CRL or independently qualified OCSP status
evidence. Offline replay must verify both the request/response relationship and
the original closure bytes, extract one cryptographically bound token time,
and require it strictly before the origin. [RFC 3161](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3161.html)
requires status, signature, certificate identifier, imprint, algorithm,
nonce/timeliness, certificate status, and TSA-policy checks; it proves that
the closure existed no later than the token time, not that an official
publisher served the bytes. SHA-256-era signer identification follows
[RFC 5816](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5816.html), certificate paths and
status follow [RFC 5280](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5280.html), and a
future OCSP profile would need all signed status-time semantics in
[RFC 6960](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6960.html).

The preferred runtime is an isolated Julia project with `OpenSSL_jll` as a
direct exact dependency. The current `scripts/us/Project.toml` and
`Manifest.toml` hashes are
`72cec6cb6dc64dc71b9e342890b78afbf8fd66cb97dd8603e4fe905ad137dc1c` and
`c2e596cf8452c5b890bb0ef66c05bc72a57fa25ab6f8fe790f8db4600b035263`.
`OpenSSL_jll` is only transitive there, so `using OpenSSL_jll` under that
project fails. The resolved transitive package is OpenSSL 3.5.7+0, package
tree `d8cce34295c55f47be683580f44791716045b8fe`, Apple-arm64 artifact tree
`5ffc993d703fa0051405cb562c49d46328b8d5f3`, and artifact tarball SHA-256
`7e8ca981c934d7b7ecce259bcc7f1b658b202f055585e76c114553caab5366ac`.
Installed `openssl`, `libcrypto.3.dylib`, and `libssl.3.dylib` hashes were
`00292fe08c00550afd97d692c47a2a4a41ee56b136f52f3f63124df97db928c4`,
`b40cc0d4fd13fc9a32849fedf18d2fde97694efb5ac19573bd1ba5c40d941644`,
and `b8ecb15e077227cf89a5a077335395c9db4bbea978253b7f6d96329f634f30fc`.
The release must pin and rehash its Julia distribution, Project/Manifest,
module/schemas/tests, JLL package/artifact/products/provider/config, platform,
and every leaf verifier, reject overrides/preferences, invoke the absolute
JLL executable without a shell under a sanitized environment, and impose

[verification options](https://docs.openssl.org/3.5/man1/openssl-verification-options/).

V4 must also replace leaf-owned raw objects with a parent-level canonical
`raw_object_catalog_v1`. Each physical object and replica occurs once;
profiles reference ordered `selected_object_ids` sets plus exact projections.
This represents the fixed-assets 3/3/2 sharing without inventing eight files
and the BLS history as an ordered multi-chunk candidate with exact coverage,

version, and attestation identities are globally unique catalog entries;
intentional cross-leaf references are allowed and byte totals count each

but each object needs two distinct registered operators, SPKIs,
administrative domains, backends/accounts, and provider versions, and no
attestation may be reused. This authenticates custody assertions and byte
equality, not physical independence or future durability.

The mandatory adversarial suite includes canonical-subject reorder/type/
length/domain attacks; wrong/reused/retired/revoked/compromised role keys;
bootstrap replacement and registry rollback/fork; malformed or wrong-policy,
wrong-nonce, wrong-imprint, wrong-chain, wrong-time, or stale-status RFC 3161

with network trapped and zero writes. Truth access, model construction,

Implementation of this synthetic-only trust kernel and its schemas is **GO**.

until immutable external bootstrap distribution, independently controlled

#### Literature and industry practice for the dubious farm-to-firm mapping

The follow-up survey rejects both tempting shortcuts: treating every farm as
an ordinary Census enterprise, or replacing the farm count with SUSB/County
Business Patterns. Census's [County Business Patterns
methodology](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/cbp/technical-documentation/methodology.html)
defines an establishment as one physical business location, excludes
nonemployers, and explicitly excludes crop and animal production (NAICS 111
and 112). The [Business Dynamics Statistics release
note](https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/bds/updates/bds2019-release-note.pdf)
confirms the same 111/112 exclusion. BEA's published [Industry Economic
Accounts classification](https://apps.bea.gov/scb/2018/08-august/pdf/0818-industry-tables.pdf),
by contrast, defines `111CA Farms` as crop production plus animal production
and aquaculture, NAICS 111-112. A SUSB/CBP substitution would therefore erase
the very production industries the model row represents.

International statistical practice also requires an explicit unit choice.
The [Eurostat-OECD Manual on Business Demography
Statistics](https://doi.org/10.1787/9789264041882-en) recommends the enterprise
as the business-demography unit, distinguishes it from establishment/site
counts, and notes that agriculture is outside the manual's normal register
coverage. The FAO [World Programme for the Census of Agriculture
2020](https://www.fao.org/fileadmin/templates/ess/documents/meetings_and_workshops/WCA_2020_expert_meeting_2014/WCA2020_Volume_1_full_24102014.pdf)
instead defines the agricultural holding as the economic unit of agricultural
production under single management, regardless of title, legal form, size,
or whether its land is contiguous. That concept is close to a production
agent, but is not automatically an enterprise, legal unit, company, employer,
or establishment.

Nor is the count distribution innocuous. USDA ERS reports that in 2024
[small family farms were 86 percent of farms but produced only 17 percent of
output](https://ers.usda.gov/data-products/charts-of-note/114161), while
large-scale family farms were 5 percent of farms and produced 50 percent.
ERS's [farm-structure overview](https://ers.usda.gov/topics/farm-economy/farm-structure-and-organization/farm-structure-and-contracting)
also separates family/nonfamily ownership, income-size classes, and contract
production. A model that creates equal or exchangeable agents from the raw
1.88-million count would misrepresent production concentration even if its
total count were exact.

Best-practice decision: retain 1,880,000 only as the candidate 2024 count of
NASS agricultural holdings for BEA 111CA's NAICS 111-112 scope. A future
mapping receipt must state the model-agent statistical unit; reconcile
holding, enterprise, establishment, employer/nonemployer, ownership, contract
production, and scope; and either reproduce a preregistered size/production
weight distribution or prove why the model does not require one. It must also
keep forestry, fishing, hunting, and agricultural support (NAICS 113-115) out
of `111CA` unless a separate BEA mapping explicitly assigns them. Until that
receipt is independently validated, the configuration's `DUBIOUS` status is
the correct one.

This is a model-material ambiguity, not a descriptive-label issue. The pinned
pipeline assigns the configured NASS value directly to `firms[111CA]` in
`scripts/us/USPipeline.jl` (SHA-256
`ce4d8138a1c07fdc9509d7560f307f226dc314eb0a4394270ef1e1014b9ca14d`).
The calibration code then applies the common simulation scale and rounding to
that vector and sets `I_s = firms` in `src/utils/calibration.jl` (SHA-256
`d64933c524b72906eb5f8749350d52c79ca4a67b49a0c2636afe2aec5de8f3dc`).
Finally, `src/model_init/init_firms.jl` (SHA-256
`65ffa48432db22a5b20b72e1dd93ce67cc5f87af11fabee349b9cd91d1b96baf`)
uses `I_s` as the sectoral firm counts and their sum as the number of simulated
firms. Consequently, the statistical-unit choice changes the model's agent
population after scaling; it cannot be waived merely because aggregate output
or employment is calibrated elsewhere. A qualifying mapping must therefore
test the induced 111CA agent count and concentration, not only the raw source
value and code label.

## 2026-08-08 - Present-day structural bodies expose two logical-contract mismatches

The first lossless parse of the current Census structural bodies and the
current BEA/Census classification workbooks produced a useful negative
result: the official physical representations do not exactly satisfy the two
already-accepted synthetic logical contracts. The correct response is a
versioned successor contract, not normalization of the source evidence.
These are present-day diagnostic reads only. They are not pre-origin
captures, do not authenticate body-to-URL provenance, and do not create an
inventory event or an admitted model input.

### Census AIES and SUSB physical state

Exactly six direct GETs returned HTTP 200 at unchanged effective URLs. The
bodies and response headers were retained only under `/private/tmp` for the
bounded implementation and independent audit. Exact current body identities
are:

| Object | Bytes | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| `AIES00INV.zip` | 28,470 | `d141f6b6f932335b404557d3007766f75d6d110bfa065b533e2b74a0a277664b` |
| `AIES31INV.zip` | 18,902 | `6d2fc3faf1a7e69f9c6fb882233a94f871e5b2e39626963a9c14a3b5228fd3dd` |
| `AIES42INV.zip` | 2,830 | `ad2345d73371f99765d21939e9806be8f14eea71238384877783e5c256406013` |
| `AIES44INV.zip` | 4,081 | `07965c9360d6a918c7f8214e45d14d3da8170c84b394d090c701e3a6c78d7d52` |
| `AIES51INV.zip` | 1,674 | `33aec64ddc61cc1bb59622c3b87bed96b4e27553453ebe8ef3df47829dc7d774` |
| `us_state_6digitnaics_2022.txt` | 56,000,447 | `6f7b2f2b14cbad9dbfeb31d3bfc9f729368a0e971727de4eda88c9f83f77a513` |

Every AIES ZIP has exactly one `DAT`, one `FIELDS`, and one `README` member,
all Deflate method 8 with verified CRCs. The inner files are ASCII,
BOM-free, LF-only, final-LF, and the unquoted pipe-delimited `DAT` header
exactly equals its field dictionary. Exact data-row counts are 1,279, 648,
45, 72, and 8. The physical flag vocabulary is case-sensitive and combines
the quality state with the measure it qualifies: observed value/CV pairs
include `(v,v)`, `(w,w)`, `(D,D)`, `(S,S)`, `(Z,N)`, and `('',Z)`.
`NAICS_F=805` is also present in AIES00 and AIES42. Suppressed estimates are
published as numeric zero plus a flag rather than as a missing value, and the
manufacturing LIFO-reserve values and associated CV fields can be negative.
The accepted logical v1 contract instead partitions value flags from CV flags,
requires empty structural flags, and requires nonnegative CVs. It therefore
cannot accept these bodies without losing information.

The official AIES table notes define `D` as disclosure withholding, `N` as
not available or not comparable, `S` as failing publication standards, `Z`
as rounding to zero, `v` as an estimated CV between 30.0% and 60.8%, and `w`
as an estimated CV above 60.8%. Those meanings must be bound to the exact
flagged measure rather than collapsed into a generic missingness token. The
five package READMEs themselves point to their individual tables on
[data.census.gov](https://data.census.gov/) for those notes; the future
successor must preserve both the package bytes and a separately governed
table-note receipt.

The SUSB file is Windows-1252 rather than UTF-8; byte `0x92` occurs 1,324
times only inside `NAICSDSCR`. It has 570,105 data rows, exactly fourteen CSV
fields, minimal quoting only in that description field, a unique
`(STATE, NAICS, ENTRSIZE)` key, and no blank or textual-suppression cells.
Its physical enterprise-size order is
`01,02,03,26,33,34,35,37,36`, not the invented consecutive logical
`01..09` sequence. The observed noise flags are exactly `G`, `H`, and `J`;
the [SUSB glossary](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/susb/about/glossary.html)
defines those as less than 2%, 2% to less than 5%, and at least 5% noise,
respectively. `EMPLFL_R` is correctly absent because the
[SUSB methodology](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/susb/technical-documentation/methodology.html)
states that employment-range flags were discontinued beginning with reference
year 2018. All 86,416 eligible size groups follow the physical order, and the
published hierarchy identities hold for all five measures. `--` is an
aggregate NAICS marker, not null. `FIRM` nevertheless remains nonadditive
across establishment-industry rows, so those arithmetic identities do not
authorize a firm-count aggregation.

The successor design must preserve the original character encoding, raw
field names, flag-measure pairs, zero-plus-flag states, signed lexical values,
physical ENTRSIZE codes and labels, and every official row. Any convenient
semantic projection must be a separately named, independently validated
derivative. Until that successor exists, the correct result is
`PHYSICAL_BODY_PARSED_LOGICAL_V1_INCOMPATIBLE`, with **0/6 qualified Census
structural profiles**, **0 admitted origins**, and **0 origin-aligned
comparison cells**.

#### Census public-file policy review

A same-day review of the official Census policy surface removes the earlier
blanket `NOT_REVIEWED_BLOCKS_BYTE_ACQUISITION` assumption for these public
static files, but it does not turn the present-day downloads into prospective
evidence. Census describes its public data as open data, explicitly points
users to its FTP service for complete dataset downloads, and says that public
statistical products should be reusable and replicable for verification. Its
[citation guidance](https://www.census.gov/about/policies/citation.html)
expressly covers files from `census.gov` and the Census FTP service and asks
users to preserve the author/sponsor, file or table name, product, vintage,
URL, and access date. It also says that Census is the source of the original
data while conclusions from a user's estimates remain the user's
responsibility. The [open-data
page](https://www.census.gov/topics/research/research-transparency-public-access/open-data.html)
separately distinguishes public data from restricted-use data and identifies
the FTP service as an official dissemination platform.

The resulting capture policy is narrow. A future runner may retrieve the
exact public AIES and SUSB static objects for research, preservation, and
reproducibility, subject to a capture-time recheck of the official policy and
file notices. It must record the exact Census attribution fields and say that
the derived model and conclusions are not Census products or endorsements.
It must not attempt respondent identification, linkage for identification,
or publication of respondent-identifying material. The Census Data API
[terms](https://www.census.gov/data/developers/about/terms-of-service.html)
apply when the API is used; the six bodies above were direct public files, so
an API-key, API-quota, or API-response claim must not be invented for them.
No policy-page bytes, transport receipt, external timestamp, independent
replica, or legal opinion was preserved in this diagnostic pass. Therefore
this review authorizes only the design of a fail-closed public-file capture
path; it does not authenticate the current bodies or qualify any profile.

That capture path cannot be inserted into the frozen v3 dispatch unchanged.
The present SUSB response declared `Content-Type: text/plain`, while
`dispatch.census_susb_structural.v1` permits JSON, ZIP, XLSX, and CSV but not
plain text. The filename extension does not override the observed media type.
V3 is immutable evidence, so a qualified successor must add the exact public
text object type, bind its Windows-1252 decoding rule and physical schema, and
carry a new independent-validation receipt; it must not relabel the response
as CSV merely to satisfy the old allowlist.

#### Prospective Census successor design

The minimum additive capture design is **one six-object controller with two
versioned leaf dispatches**, not six unrelated downloads and not one
media-agnostic Census leaf:

- `dispatch.census_aies_inventory_allocation.v2` owns the five AIES ZIP
  profiles and their common archive/member/flag-note semantics;
- `dispatch.census_susb_structural.v2` owns the one full SUSB
  `text/plain`/Windows-1252 profile and its CSV/key/size-code semantics.

Both leaves may reference one closed capture-set receipt and shared custody
closure, but they must retain distinct independent-validation receipts. The
six exact GETs run under `final_structural_pre_origin`, with no redirects,
retries, credentials, cookies, proxy, netrc, or range requests. The controller
freezes object membership and request ordinals; it does **not** freeze the
present-day body hashes as a future allowlist. A legitimate reissue is
preserved and quarantined on schema drift rather than discarded or silently
retried.

Neither existing common-origin verifier is the production integration point.
V3 excludes the observed SUSB `text/plain` media and has no qualified Census
leaf verifier. V4 is a permanent synthetic BEA/BLS demonstration with no
production trust/runtime/custody branch or Census topology. A later additive
common-origin successor—effectively v5—must consume a raw-object catalog v2,
profile/object-set selection v3 with a Census physical projection v2, and
qualified-leaf result v3. Frozen v3/v4 bytes must not be restamped.

The exact campaign timing remains 2026-10-29 13:30Z through 2026-10-30
13:45Z, with the complete authenticated parent closure strictly before the
2026-10-30 14:00Z origin. Availability is bounded by completion of the closed
set receipt, not by HTTP `Last-Modified`, intermediary `Date`, ZIP member
timestamps, or local filesystem times. The closure must be retained through
at least 2034-09-30 23:59:59Z for h12 mature truth. Qualification additionally
requires capture-date Census policy/file-notice receipts, exact attribution
and no-endorsement language, no-identification covenant, table-note and
SUSB-methodology evidence, two genuinely distinct durable storage domains,
authenticated owner/independent-validator decisions, and RFC 3161 evidence
over the transitive set subject.

The next bounded implementation artifact is therefore a permanently
nonadmitting `census_structural/prospective_capture_set_v1`: frozen six-object
plan, offline physical parser/projection compiler, capture-set compiler, and
two leaf-result compilers, initially with no downloader or raw writer. Present
bodies are external regression oracles only and must emit
`NONPROSPECTIVE_PRESENT_DAY_DIAGNOSTIC_BYTES`; all operational gates remain
false and qualification remains 0/6 until real prospective evidence and the
successor trust interface exist.

The 2017 structure has one populated sheet at `A1:F2218`, two additional
empty visible sheets, 2,196 data rows, and nineteen exact separator rows. The
2022 structure has one populated sheet at `A1:F2147`, 2,125 data rows, and
nineteen exact separator rows. The full directional concordance has 1,150
unique ordered mapping rows, 1,057 unique 2017 source codes, 1,012 unique

Those values are distinct from eight additional styled-but-blank cells at
`F111:F113` and `F1021:F1025`; neither class may be stripped before the raw
workbook fingerprint is closed. Every six-digit source and target code is
present in its corresponding
structure. On the complete ordered pair set, row classifications are 928
one-to-one, 5 one-to-many, 120 many-to-one, and 97 many-to-many. Those counts
are evidence diagnostics, not permission to deduplicate or reverse the
published 2017-to-2022 direction.

The already accepted 2024 summary producer-use and producer-make bodies
rederive 71 ordinary industry codes and 73 commodity codes. Their code arrays
match exactly, but their physical special-account order is `Used, Other`;
the accepted logical v1 profile requires `Other, Used`. The two special titles
also preserve different published footnote labels between use and make, so
the complete title-bearing axes are not byte-identical even though all 71
ordinary codes, all 71 ordinary titles, and all 73 code strings match. A
lossless physical profile must report both differences. It must not sort the
accounts, strip the footnotes, or pretend that the synthetic v1 shared-axis
equality passed.

The BEA concordance's `Summary` code order also matches the 71 ordinary 2024
codes, but its title strings are a different comparison surface: codes `481`,
`482`, and `485` carry respectively two, one, and one trailing spaces relative
to the 2024 title axis. The semantic text is visually identical, yet the raw
strings are not byte-equal. Any normalized-title projection must therefore be
named and hashed separately from both published axes.

Finally, the BEA concordance publishes five hierarchy columns (`Sector`,
`Summary`, `U. Summary`, `Detail`, and `GO Detail`) against related NAICS
codes. It does not give each source row an explicit `Industry` versus
`Commodity` tag of the kind required by the synthetic logical profile.
Ordinary codes may be shared by both BEA axes and the final note explicitly
limits `Used` and `Other` to commodities, but duplicating every ordinary row
onto two axes would still be a derived projection, not a source field. That
projection must be separately specified and audited.

The physical classification candidate must therefore remain a present-day
`CANNOT_RUN` diagnostic, preserve `Other` and `Used` only as terminal
`BEA_SPECIAL_ACCOUNT_NON_NAICS` commodities, and emit explicit successor
requirements for special-account order/title semantics and BEA-axis
projection. Counts remain **0/6 qualified classification profiles**, **0
admitted origins**, and **0 origin-aligned comparison cells**.
